AbnormalEnd.description:
`abnormalEnd` on `session/resume` (ADR 68419 D1): the load found the
session's latest serve segment without a clean end and recorded (or had
already recorded) the `crash_inferred` backstop.

lastActivityAt.description:
RFC 3339 time of the session's latest serve activity (the time the
gate-off notice shows); absent when the log has none.

AccountLoginCancelResult.description:
`account/loginCancel` result: exactly `{cancelled}` — `true` iff a
pending flow existed and was cancelled (spec 28091 FR-29535-5).

cancelled.description: Whether a pending flow was cancelled.

AccountLoginCompletedParams.description:
`account/loginCompleted` params: exactly `{outcome, message?}` (spec
28091 FR-29535-4). `message` is a display string from the typed error
vocabulary — never key material, store content, or an echo of the raw
params (FM-29535-4).

AccountLoginOutcome.description:
How a login flow ended (spec 28091 FR-29535-4). Server-produced, so the
vocabulary is open per the #22785 E2 rule — a future flow may end in a
new way additively.

AccountLoginStartParams.description:
`account/loginStart` params: exactly `{type, apiKey?}` (spec 28091
FR-29535-1). `apiKey` is required non-empty for [`AccountLoginType::ApiKey`]
and forbidden for [`AccountLoginType::DeviceCode`]; both violations are
invalid-params errors (FM-29535-1), enforced by the handler so the error
never echoes the raw params (FM-29535-4). `Debug` is hand-written: the
derive would print the raw key bytes into any `{:?}` context (a tracing
line, an error, a test assert), and the key must never reach a log
(INV-29535-1) — the `McpOAuthRecordV1` posture.

apiKey.description:
The API key to store (the `apiKey` type only). The ONLY
secret-bearing member of the account surface: every log sink carries
[`ACCOUNT_LOGIN_API_KEY_REDACTED`] in its place (INV-29535-1).

AccountLoginStartResult.description:
`account/loginStart` result: exactly `{verificationUrl?, userCode?}` —
both present for a started device-code flow, both absent for the
synchronous `apiKey` type (spec 28091 FR-29535-1). The device-code artifacts
travel ONLY here, to the requesting connection; completion notifications
never carry them (INV-29535-2).

userCode.description: The code the user confirms or enters there (device-code flow only).

verificationUrl.description: Where the user signs in (device-code flow only).

AccountLoginType.description:
Which login flow `account/loginStart` runs (spec 28091 FR-29535-1; ADR D3).
Client-produced, so the vocabulary is CLOSED: an unknown `type` fails
deserialization into the standard invalid-params error (FM-29535-1).

AccountState.description:
The one account payload shape: the `account/read` result and the
`account/changed` params (spec 28091 FR-001/FR-002). Closed vocabulary
(INV-002); `label` and `avatarUrl` are display values that never carry key
material and are omitted, never `null`, when absent.

avatarUrl.description:
Optional display-only HTTPS avatar URL for the winning account-login
identity (ADR 28091 D8). Omitted for every other lane and on absence.

credentialRequired.description:
`false` exactly when the effective provider endpoint needs no caller
credential (keyless/gateway deployments, FR-005), so those clients
never nag the user to sign in.

label.description:
Optional display label for the credential in effect (for example the
account identity for `accountLogin`); never key material (FR-004).

state.description: Which credential lane is in effect.

AccountStateKind.description:
The projected credential state (spec 28091 FR-001; ADR 28091 D2):
`EnvKey → envKey`, `StoredKey → apiKey`, `LoginMint → accountLogin`, and
the absent lane as `loggedOut`. Open per the #22785 E2 rule —
server-produced result vocabularies are open — so a future credential
lane can project additively.

AdmissionChoice.description:
One server-minted admission choice (FR-45445-6): clients select, never
construct. Choice ids are snake_case (the `approval/request` choice
style); labels match the TUI card verbatim.

label.description:
The card label verbatim ("Allow once", "Reject once",
"Allow for this session", "Block for this session").

AdmissionDecideParams.description:
`admission/decide` params (FR-45445-7): a standard SS3 command.
Unknown fields are `invalidParams`.

commandId.description: Client-minted UUIDv7 retry id (required; full SS3.1.1 contract).

sessionId.description: The deciding session (required; must be loaded on this host).

AdmissionDecideResult.description:
`admission/decide` result (FR-45445-7): admission only — every decide is
terminal for its request.

AdmissionDecision.description:
The terminal admission decision (FR-45445-8): `allow_once` |
`reject_once` | `allow_connected` | `block_connected` | `timedOut`.
**Open**: a server-produced result vocabulary (#22785 E2).

AdmissionListPendingResult.description:
`admission/listPending` result (FR-45445-8): each open request in full, as
its `admission/request` prompt carries it.

AdmissionRequestParams.description:
`admission/request` + `admission/requested` payload (FR-45445-6): the
server→client prompt and its cursor-bearing durable fold carry the same
payload, so a gapped client recovers it via `view/page`.

admissionId.description:
Server-minted UUIDv7 durable identity (required) — all correlation
keys on it, never on the JSON-RPC id.

heldBody.description:
The held message's body, verbatim (D17) — one prompt names one
held message. Omitted when empty or absent; a client treats
absent-or-empty as no preview and keeps its preview floor
closed.

requesterLabel.description:
Display string snapshotted at request (required) — the requester may
leave the registry while the prompt pends.

viewCursor.description: The `admission/requested` cursor (required).

AdmissionRequestedViewParams.description:
`admission/requested` view event (FR-45445-6): the cursor-bearing
durable fold of the prompt, so a gapped client recovers the identical
payload via `view/page`.

heldBody.description:
The held message's body, verbatim (D17) — one prompt names one
held message. Omitted when empty or absent; a client treats
absent-or-empty as no preview and keeps its preview floor
closed.

AdmissionResolutionSummary.description:
Winning terminal returned to a losing `admission/decide` command
(amendment 45445 FR-45445-13): `resolvedBy` is omitted on timeout.

decision.description: The winning decision, such as `allow_once` or `timedOut`.

resolvedBy.description:
Who made the winning decision; absent when no person decided, for
example a timeout, an automatic allow, or a cancelled or retired
request.

viewCursor.description: The view cursor of the winning `admission/resolved` event.

AdmissionResolvedViewParams.description:
`admission/resolved` view event (FR-45445-8): the protected settlement
broadcast, so a client that saw the request can always dismiss its
prompt.

decidedByCommandId.description:
The winning wire `commandId` when a wire decide settled this (the
D-209-5 winner association, carried as the decision id); `None` for
non-decide terminals (timeout, sender cancel, retirement).

terminalCause.description:
Open enum, initially `senderCancelled` / `generationRetired`
(#63042 item 1); present only on automatic endings.

ApprovalAmendment.description:
The policy rule a decision created, in display form; the full rule is not
included.

durability.description: How long the rule lasts: `session` or `localPersistent`.

rulePreview.description: A human-readable preview of the rule, for display.

ApprovalAmendmentDurability.description:
How long a rule created by an approval decision lasts. The set is open, so
newer hosts may send other values.

ApprovalChange.description:
The change an `approval/updated` event reports. `kind` says what happened,
and only the fields for that kind are present.

choiceId.description:
The `choiceId` that satisfied the stage. Present only when `kind` is
`stageResolved`.

decision.description:
The decision the chosen option applied to the stage. Present only when
`kind` is `stageResolved`.

executable.description:
A recovery detail: whether the action could run without a new decision.
Present only when `kind` is `restartRecovered`.

kind.description:
What happened: for example `stageResolved` (a shell stage was
satisfied), `policyPersistence` (saving a rule succeeded or failed),
`reviewStarted` or `reviewCompleted` (the automated LLM judge started or
finished reviewing), `restartRecovered` (a host restart recovered this
approval: either the host first resolves it `abort` and a re-ask comes
as a new approval with a new `approvalId`, or it stays pending under
the same `approvalId` with refreshed choices), `alreadyTerminal`
(recovery found it already decided) or `resolving` (a
`computerUseTakeover` approval was marked resolving and waits for the
lock broker; a decide now answers -32059). The set is open, so newer
hosts may add kinds.

reason.description:
Why saving the policy rule failed, as human-readable text. Present only
when `kind` is `policyPersistence` and `status` is `failed`.

reparsed.description:
A recovery detail: whether the command was re-parsed during recovery.
Present only when `kind` is `restartRecovered`.

requirementId.description:
The stage requirement that was satisfied. Present only when `kind` is
`stageResolved`.

ApprovalChoice.description:
One option the server offers for deciding an approval. Clients pick one and
send its `choiceId` in `approval/decide`; they never build their own.

acceptsFeedback.description:
`true` when this choice takes optional `feedback` text in
`approval/decide`, which reaches the model as guidance. Omitted when
`false`.

choiceId.description:
The id to send as `choiceId` in `approval/decide`. The set of ids is
open, so show `label` and do not base behavior on specific ids.

decision.description:
The decision this choice applies, so a client can act on approve or
reject without knowing choice ids.

label.description: The human-readable label to show for this choice.

rulePreview.description:
A human-readable preview of what this choice grants, such as the policy
rule it would create; show it exactly as given.

scope.description:
The grant duration this choice declares: `once` (this request only),
`session` (the rest of the session) or `localPersistent` (saved in the
local policy store).

ApprovalChoiceScope.description:
How long a grant made by a choice lasts. The set is open, so newer hosts may
send other values.

ApprovalCuaCardFacts.description:
One Computer Use card's facts. Empty collections and absent rows are
omitted, never `null`.

data.description:
The data the call would send that the card must name; a card with any
offers only one-shot choices.

page.description: For a browser, the host of the window's current page.

steps.description: Only the consequential steps, in call order.

ApprovalCuaDataFact.description:
One piece of data the call would send. An open union on `kind`
(`secret`, or `other` for a row the host can't word); a client shows
`other` and any kind it doesn't know as a generic data row.

mask.description: For `secret`, the parts of it the card may show, never the value.

secretKind.description:
For `secret`, the scanner's open tag (`github_token`,
`secret_named_value` and so on); a client words the tags it knows and
shows any other as "a secret".

ApprovalCuaMask.description:
A secret's mask: a vendor token's prefix and last 4 characters
(`ghp_…3f9a`), a named value's name and length (`password=… (12 chars)`),
or the length alone; all absent names the kind only.

prefix.description:
A vendor token's fixed prefix (`ghp_`), or a named value's name and
its `=` (`password=`).

ApprovalCuaPage.description: The page's full host, no path or query.

hostAscii.description: The host's `xn--` form; equal to `host` when they don't differ.

ApprovalCuaPoint.description: A point in the model's 0–1000 coordinates.

ApprovalCuaStep.description:
One consequential step. A client renders "Step N: <action> <roleWord>
"<label>" — <effect>"; a key step names its `chord`, and only a step with
a `point` (and no label or chord) reads "at x,y".

action.description: The host's verb phrase, such as `click` or `type into`.

chord.description: The chord, for a key step.

effect.description: The host's trusted sentence for what the step may do.

kind.description:
An open tag for styling and tests only (`verb:<class>`, `unresolved`,
`unlabeled`); a client that doesn't know a value renders the step from
`effect` and its label as usual.

label.description:
The control's label: the app's own text, shown quoted and as plain
text; a client may cap it.

point.description: The step's own 0–1000 model coordinates, only for a point step.

roleWord.description: `button`, `link`, `menu item` or `key`; absent for a point step.

step.description: 1-based, as the batch numbers its steps.

ApprovalDecideParams.description:
`approval/decide` params (tdd SS5.4): the decision. A standard SS3
command — requires the session loaded on this host, requires `commandId`,
durable intake before ack, value-identical replay.

feedback.description:
Free-text guidance delivered to the model with the denial. Only valid
on choices with `acceptsFeedback`. Never persisted in the durable
audit record (live steer only), so it is absent from
`approval/resolved` (tdd SS5.4). Omitted and explicit `null` both
mean "no feedback" (#23468).

requirementId.description:
Must equal the approval's `currentRequirementId`. The multi-stage race
guard: a decision aimed at stage 1 can never accidentally satisfy
stage 2, and a stale value is -32053 (tdd SS5.4).

ApprovalDecideResult.description:
`approval/decide` result (tdd SS5.4). Admission-ack rules still apply: the
authoritative outcome is `approval/resolved` / `approval/updated` on the
view stream.

approvalId.description: The approval this decision was applied to.

terminal.description:
`false` when the choice satisfied a stage but further requirements
remain (the approval stays pending and an updated `approval/request`
follows); `true` when this decision produced the terminal
`DecisionApplied` (tdd SS5.4).

ApprovalDecision.description:
The kind of decision a choice applies or an approval received. The set is
open, so newer hosts may send values this version does not list.

ApprovalListPendingParams.description:
`approval/listPending` params (tdd SS5.7): the pull dual of the re-issued
requests. A log-fold read — no lease, works on loaded and unloaded
sessions, never subscribes.

ApprovalListPendingResult.description:
`approval/listPending` result (tdd SS5.7). Ordering is by opening
`viewCursor`; empty arrays when nothing is pending. The result is
point-in-time — to act on it race-safely, `approval/decide` carries the
`requirementId` guard regardless of how the client learned the state.

approvals.description: Exactly the `approval/request` params, one per pending approval.

userInputs.description: Exactly the `userInput/request` params, one per pending prompt.

ApprovalMode.description:
The approval enforcement modes (tdd SS5.12, camelCased
`ApprovalBackendMode`). **Closed** by design (D-006, select-never-create):
a client selects a preconfigured mode and can never construct one;
widening this enum is a deliberate, gate-visible protocol change.

ApprovalModeApplyOutcome.description:
Whether a mode change did anything (tdd SS5.12), mirroring
`ApprovalReconfigureApplyOutcome`. Apply failures are `commandRejected`.

ApprovalModeSource.description:
How an approval mode took effect (tdd SS5.12, the effective-mode
projection's `source` vocabulary). Open.

ApprovalOrigin.description:
What triggered a tool action, shown so the user can judge it. It is
display-only and untrusted, and policy rules never match on it.

command.description:
The shell command whose process asked for the action. Present when
`kind` is `shellCommand`.

kind.description: Which kind of origin this is: `shellCommand` or `url`.

url.description: The full URL a fetch tool is requesting. Present when `kind` is `url`.

ApprovalPersistenceStatus.description:
The result of saving a granted rule to the local policy store. The set is
open, so newer hosts may send other values.

ApprovalPolicyResult.description:
Whether an approval's final decision lets the action run. The set is open,
so newer hosts may send other values.

approvalId.description:
The approval's stable id. Match `approval/decide`, `approval/updated`
and `approval/resolved` by it, never by the JSON-RPC request id, which
belongs to one connection.

availableChoices.description:
The choices the server offers for the current requirement. Send the
chosen one's `choiceId` in `approval/decide`; clients never build their
own.

cuaCardFacts.description:
A Computer Use card's facts: the page, the window and each step that
may have an effect, in the host's words; absent on every other
approval.

currentRequirementId.description:
The requirement the next decision must target; send it unchanged as
`requirementId` in `approval/decide`. For `shell` it names the first
stage still needing a decision; for other kinds its `sourceIndex` is 0.

itemId.description: The `toolCall` view item waiting on this approval.

judgeEscalated.description:
`true` when the automated LLM judge saw this request first and handed it
to a person without deciding. A display hint only. The host sends it
as `false` when it re-issues the request after a restart or on
`session/resume`; a re-send for a later stage keeps it.

protectedWrite.description:
`true` when this approval guards a write to a protected file. Only
allow-once and reject choices are offered, and a decision is accepted
only while at least one client is subscribed to the session.

rawArgs.description:
The tool call's arguments as a string, usually JSON. With `toolName`, it
lets a client show a subject whose `kind` it does not recognize.

reviewerReason.description:
The judge's escalation reason as one bounded display line (ADR 8609
D3: first sentence, whitespace controls folded, other control and
format scalars stripped, 100 extended grapheme clusters max).
Present only on a request released by a valid structured `escalate`
with a non-blank judge rationale; absent on every other approval. A
display hint only, like `judge_escalated`: it never authorizes
anything.

sessionId.description:
The owning session. For a subagent's approval shown on the parent, this
is the parent session.

sourceRange.description:
The stored records this event was folded from: an opaque token clients
must not interpret.

subagentOrigin.description:
Present only for a child (native subagent) approval projected onto
the parent session's plane (ADR 36182); parent-own approvals omit it.

subject.description:
What the approval is for. Show a `kind` you do not recognize
generically, and never auto-approve it.

taskId.description: The id of the task running the tool call.

toolCallId.description: The model provider's id for this tool call.

toolName.description: The name of the tool being called.

turnId.description: The turn whose tool call is waiting on this approval.

viewCursor.description:
The cursor of the `approval/requested` event that opened this request.
A re-send for a later stage keeps this cursor, so `view/page` at it
returns the opening stage, which may be older than this payload.

ApprovalRequirementRef.description:
Identifies one requirement of an approval: for a `shell` approval, one
stage. A client sends it back as `requirementId` in `approval/decide`, and a
stale-requirement error names the current one.

approvalId.description: The approval this requirement belongs to.

sourceIndex.description:
The requirement's index within the approval, counting from 0; an
approval with a single requirement uses 0.

ApprovalResolutionSummary.description: Winning terminal returned to a losing `approval/decide` command.

decision.description:
The winning decision, as an `approval/resolved` decision value such as
`approved` or `abort`.

resolvedBy.description: Who made the winning decision, such as `user`, `policy` or `llmJudge`.

viewCursor.description: The view cursor of the winning `approval/resolved` event.

ApprovalResolvedBy.description:
Who or what made an approval's final decision. The set is open, so newer
hosts may send other values.

ApprovalResolvedParams.description: `approval/resolved` params: the first durable terminal decision.

abortReason.description:
Why an `abort` was not a cancel, when the host knows: `lockEpochEnded |
brokerUnavailable`, an open vocabulary (tdd SS5.5). Clients render an
unknown value like an absent one.

amendment.description:
The policy rule the decision created. Present only when the decision
created one.

byClient.description:
The client whose `approval/decide` won (ADR 73001 D4): absent
on policy, judge and interrupt terminals, for a connection with no
recorded handshake, and on older logs.

decidedAt.description:
The decision time as RFC3339, projected from the durable
`DecisionApplied` record's own stamp (ADR 45450 D3): optional on the
wire so decoders tolerate its absence, always populated by current
hosts.

decidedByCommandId.description:
The `commandId` of the `approval/decide` command that won. Absent when
no such command made the decision, for example a policy or LLM judge
decision.

itemId.description: The `toolCall` view item this approval was holding.

policyResult.description:
Whether the final decision lets the action run (`allow`) or blocks it
(`deny`).

resolvedBy.description: Who or what made the decision: `user`, `policy` or `llmJudge`.

sourceRange.description:
The stored records this event was folded from: an opaque token clients
must not interpret.

stageEvidence.description:
For a `shell` approval, how each stage was resolved when the decision
became final. Empty for other subject kinds, and it can be empty for
`shell` too.

subagentOrigin.description:
Present only for a child (native subagent) approval projected onto
the parent session's plane (ADR 36182); parent-own approvals omit it.

turnId.description: The turn whose tool call this approval was holding.

viewCursor.description:
This event's view cursor: opaque, and strictly increasing within the
session.

ApprovalRulesApplyOutcome.description:
Whether a rules change did anything (tdd SS5.16), mirroring
`ApprovalReconfigureApplyOutcome`. Apply failures are `commandRejected`.
**Open**: a newer host may add an outcome; a client keeps an unknown word.

ApprovalStage.description:
One stage of a `shell` approval: a single command from the pipeline or
command list, approved separately from the others.

argv.description:
The stage's command words as parsed. When `argvComplete` is `false`,
this can be a single unparsed piece of the command.

argvComplete.description:
`true` when `argv` is the stage's complete command, known before it
runs; `false` when part of it cannot be resolved ahead of time (for
example a command substitution). A stage with `false` never has a
`suggestedPrefix`.

position.description:
This stage's 1-based position in the command; it equals
`requirementId.sourceIndex + 1`.

requirementId.description:
This stage's requirement id. When it equals the approval's
`currentRequirementId`, send it as `requirementId` in `approval/decide`.

resolution.description:
Whether this stage still needs a decision or, if not, how it was
satisfied.

suggestedPrefix.description:
A command prefix the host suggests always allowing in this workspace,
present only when one can be taken from a fully parsed stage.
`availableChoices` shows whether that grant is offered.

totalStages.description: The total number of stages in the command.

ApprovalStageEvidence.description:
How one stage of a `shell` approval was resolved when the decision became
final.

argv.description: The stage's command words as parsed.

position.description: The stage's 1-based position in the command.

resolution.description: How the stage was resolved at the final decision.

totalStages.description: The total number of stages in the command.

ApprovalStageResolution.description:
Whether a shell stage still needs a decision, or how it was satisfied.
Satisfied stages are included so a client can show progress.

argvPrefix.description:
The command prefix saved as an always-allow rule when this stage was
approved. Present only when `kind` is `policyAmendment`.

diagnostic.description:
Free-form text naming the rule or mode that allowed the stage, for
display or troubleshooting. Present only when `kind` is `policyAllow`.

kind.description:
One of `unresolved`, `knownSafe`, `policyAllow`, `allowOnce` or
`policyAmendment`. The set is open, so newer hosts may add values.

ApprovalSubagentOrigin.description:
Child (native subagent) provenance for an approval projected onto the
PARENT session's approval plane (#36182 / ADR 36182): identifies the
originating child run/agent so a client can attribute the prompt. Omitted
(`skip_serializing_if`) on the parent's own approvals, so pre-existing
parent frames stay byte-identical.

childRunId.description: The child run that parked on this approval.

childSessionId.description: The child session stream id whose records carry this approval.

subagentId.description:
The originating child's subagent id, from the parent session's
durable subagent control records.

ApprovalSubject.description:
Open approval subject union. Unknown kinds are rendered generically and
never auto-approved by clients (tdd SS5.2).

access.description:
The access asked for: `read` or `write` for `fileAccess`, `control` for
`process`. Absent for other kinds.

command.description: The full raw shell command. Present when `kind` is `shell`.

holder.description:
The session that holds the Computer Use lock now, by label and times
only. Present when `kind` is `computerUseTakeover` (tdd SS5.2.8).

host.description:
The network host the tool wants to reach. Present when `kind` is
`network`.

kind.description: Open discriminator: `shell | fileAccess | network | unixSocket | process | tool | computerUseTakeover`.

origin.description:
What triggered the action (a shell command or a URL), for display only
and untrusted. It is not sent on `shell` subjects, and policy rules
never match on it.

path.description:
For `fileAccess`, the path the tool asked to access, normalized by the
host (workspace-relative inside the workspace); for
`unixSocket`, the exact resolved socket path, sent unescaped, so escape
it before display.

port.description:
The network port, present only on `network` subjects that name one. A
session grant made from a subject without a port covers every port.

protocol.description:
The network protocol, for example `https`. Present only on `network`
subjects that name one.

stages.description:
The shell command split into stages that are approved separately (the
commands of a pipeline or command list), in order. Present on `shell`
subjects; it may be empty.

target.description:
Display text naming the process the tool wants to control. Present when
`kind` is `process`.

toolName.description: The tool asking for the action. Present for every kind except `shell`.

workspaceRoot.description:
The canonical workspace root the shell command runs in, present on
`shell` subjects when the host knows it. Saved command-prefix rules
apply only within this root.

ApprovalSuggestedPrefix.description:
A suggested always-allow rule for a shell stage: commands starting with
`argvPrefix` would run in this workspace without asking.

argvPrefix.description:
The leading command words the rule would allow, for example `["cargo",
"test"]`.

label.description: A human-readable label for the suggestion, ready to show as is.

ApprovalUpdatedParams.description: `approval/updated` params: the refreshed pending view plus one change.

availableChoices.description: The refreshed choices for the current requirement.

change.description: What changed; `change.kind` names the kind of change.

currentRequirementId.description:
The requirement the next decision must target after this change; send it
as `requirementId` in `approval/decide`.

sourceRange.description:
The stored records this event was folded from: an opaque token clients
must not interpret.

subagentOrigin.description:
Present only for a child (native subagent) approval projected onto
the parent session's plane (ADR 36182); parent-own approvals omit it.

subject.description: The approval's subject, with `stages` refreshed for this change.

viewCursor.description:
This event's view cursor: opaque, and strictly increasing within the
session.

AttentionFlag.description:
One attention flag (tdd SS2.4, ADR 31983 D3): a pending server-initiated
request class parked on the session. Open on the wire — clients MUST
ignore unknown values; future attention kinds are additive.

oneOf.description:
At least one peer-admission request is open (#50032 slice 2b,
amendment 45445 FR-45445-8). Experimental: stripped per-connection
for unopted callers (SS1.5.1).

AutoRecovery.description:
`autoRecovery` on `session/resume` (amendment 26387/68619, owner decision
G-23): the outcome of this resume's own load when it ran with the
`resume_auto_recover` gate on and the session's effective `recoveryMode`
ON. Output only; no request member asks for it.

reason.description: Present only when `outcome` is `refused`.

turnId.description:
The recovery turn's id (the `turnId` of its `turn/started`); present
only when `outcome` is `continued`.

AutoRecoveryOutcome.description: The `autoRecovery` outcome (the amendment's decision table). Open enum.

AutomaticContinuation.description: Whether this feature holds the current source (D7, closed).

BackgroundInitiator.description:
Who durably backgrounded a task (tdd SS4.5.5,
`TaskBackgroundedInitiator`). Open — runtime vocabulary.

BackgroundState.description:
Presentation state of a backgrounded running tool item (ADR 50041 D1).
Open — new states are additive. Asserts presentation only, never durable
backgrounding (that claim stays `Item::background`, set only behind a
durable `TaskBackgrounded`).

BackgroundStatus.description:
The backgrounded-row payload for a running `toolCall` item (ADR 50041
D1): the presentation state plus the live status text the row body
renders. Experimental — stable clients ignore the member.

detail.description:
The live status text the backgrounded row body renders. The flip
gate requires non-empty detail (the fold always sets it); a
state-only member leaves the row alone.

BackgroundTarget.description:
One call's live background-target record (tdd SS4.5.5; ADR
63254-background-target-on-tool-call D2): exactly the runtime
snapshot's four facts, no new nouns.

backgroundRequested.description: Whether the background was already requested for this call.

foregroundWaitActive.description: Whether the call sits in its foreground wait right now.

manualReleaseAdmissible.description:
Point-in-time Ctrl+B chooser hint; the runtime re-checks
admission on the action.

toolCallId.description: The tool call this record describes (the provider call id).

BackgroundTasks.description: Keep or Stop (D7's closed request choice).

BackgroundTerminalCompletion.description:
`backgroundTerminalCompletion`: the facts the Finished cell
renders (ADR 50041 D3/D4, plus the optional exit code from D28 and
the optional reason from D29).
The fold reads them from the inbox terminal record and the
backgrounded call it names; every member is required (empty
output serializes as `""`, never absent) except `exit_code` and
`reason`, each absent when the terminal carries none.

command.description: The title text gate-off shows for the backgrounded command.

exitCode.description:
The process exit code from the terminal record's `exit_code: `
line (ADR 50041 D28); absent when the terminal carries none.
`i32`, the gate-off frozen-header twin's width
(`BackgroundTerminalTailTerminal.exit_code`). Old clients
ignore the unknown member (tdd evolution rule).

output.description: The completion text; empty when the terminal carries none.

outputTruncated.description: True when `output` is a prefix of the terminal text.

reason.description:
The terminal's reason from the terminal record's `reason: `
line, trimmed like gate-off's parse (ADR 50041 D29); absent when
the terminal carries none or an empty one. Old clients ignore
the unknown member (tdd evolution rule).

terminalStatus.description:
One of `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `timedOut`,
`rejected` (the ItemStatus wire vocabulary, tdd SS4.4.1).

toolCallId.description:
The backgrounded call's call id: the live/history correlation
key behind the skip-when-minted rule (ADR 50041 D6).

BackgroundTerminalInboxItemDrainedParams.description:
`backgroundTerminal/inboxItemDrained` params (ADR 83474 D2): one
background-terminal inbox drain with its recorded stamp. The member
set mirrors `MonitorInboxItemDrainedParams` (tdd SS4.5.18), like the
peer drain's.

deliveryVisible.description:
The drain record's `delivery_visible`: true for a delivery (a
snapshot-carrying drain), false for the claim-only settle of a
served completion.

drainTargetRunStream.description:
The draining run stream (`StreamRef`), absent means the current
draining run.

itemId.description:
The drained inbox item id: the served completion's `itemId`
(tdd SS4.5.19).

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

BackgroundWork.description:
The advisory work census (D7): a flat object (see
`RewindAvailability`). Counts are present exactly when `state` is
`known`; `reason` exactly when `unavailable`.

continuingCount.description: Continuing logical owners, present when known.

endingPersistentMonitorCount.description:
Separate direct-source persistent monitors that will end, present
when known.

reason.description: Why the census is unavailable, present exactly then; an open string.

BlockedPrompt.description:
The cold recall seed on `session/resume` and `session/read` results
(ADR 50074 D2): at most one, the latest blocked Main prompt — exactly
the host's mirror of `prompt_recovery::replay::ReplayInput`'s choice.

text.description:
The exact submitted prompt, verbatim — no truncation, no
normalization; recall fidelity requires exactness.

BranchState.description: The latest branch observation in the snapshot (tdd SS4.6.4, SS4.9.1).

branch.description: The observed branch; `null` on a detached-HEAD observation.

vcs.description: The detected version-control system; absent when none was detected.

CapabilityName.description:
A grantable capability name. Open: the experimental-only `rawLog` entry
joins the stable domain as an additive open-enum extension when it graduates
— closed would make that a retype.

oneOf.description:
Cross-session peer messaging and admission (#45445, ADR 45445 D10):
the one gate for `peer/*` and `admission/*` — granted at
`initialize` iff the host serves the plane (unix platform with
registry access over a spawner-is-client or same-user transport),
refused on beyond-same-user transports. Experimental-tier only
(owner ruling on PR #50979): the per-variant stability strips it
from the stable render, like `rawLog` below.

The raw-log altitude: the SS6 `log/*` record methods and
`projection/*`; the `log/physical*` export has its own
`rawLogPhysical` grant (ADR 58371 D3). Experimental-tier only: granted
solely on connections that opted into `experimentalApi`; a v1 host
never grants it as a stable surface. The per-variant stability strips
it from the stable render, so the stable bundle names it only in
reserved tables.

The physical export (ADR 58371 D3): `log/physicalSubscribe`,
`log/physicalFiles`, `log/physicalUnsubscribe`. Experimental-tier
only and independent of `rawLog`: either can be withheld alone.

The experimental `journal/*` surface: lets a client act as the
durable store for the host's session journal. Experimental tier
only, behind `experimentalApi`; not granted by default.

The socket daemon's vacate contract, revision 1 (ADR 69813 D5 item 3;
spec 59770 amendment #69912): a client that requests it re-resumes
its sessions on the canonical socket after `vacated`, and a granted
connection counts as one that follows a vacate. Experimental-tier
only, because the contract's own words are (ADR 59770 D9); only the
socket daemon acts on it. A later revision of the contract takes a
new name.

The serve process's launcher context in `InitializeResult`
(`launchContext`; ADR 86936 D1): a client that requests it is told
the invocation id and context the launcher started this process
with. Experimental-tier only (ADR 86936 D2); gates no method.

CheckpointBoundary.description:
A served checkpoint-prune boundary (spec 13929 amendment
FR-50042-1; ADR 50042 D3): `through_item_id` names the last
first-opened item that opened strictly before the boundary
checkpoint event.

throughItemId.description: The last pre-boundary item's id, in served (first-opened) order.

ClientApprovalRule.description:
One client-supplied shell prefix allow-rule (tdd SS5.16, ADR 47712 D2):
argv tokens in the `ShellPrefixSuggestion.argv_prefix` shape. An object,
not a bare array, so the element can grow additively later.

argvPrefix.description:
The argv-token prefix. Must be non-empty with no empty token; banned
prefixes refuse the carrying call (tdd SS5.16, ADR 47712 D4).

ClientApprovalRuleState.description:
One listed client-supplied rule in `EffectivePermissionState` (tdd SS5.16,
ADR 47712 D6): the prefix plus its origin.

origin.description:
Always `client` on this surface; carried so the listing stays
attributable if it ever merges families.

ClientCapabilities.description:
The client's requested capability posture (SS1.4.1). Every member
defaults; an absent `capabilities` object means all defaults.

experimentalApi.description: Opt into experimental methods, fields, and variants (default `false`).

requestedCapabilities.description:
Names from the capability registry. Unknown entries are not an error
and simply do not appear in `grantedCapabilities` — which is why this
is a list of free strings rather than of registry names.

userInputDialogs.description:
Whether this client can render a `userInput/request` dialog and answer
it (SS5.10). **Absent means capable** (D-047): a client that predates
the member keeps today's contract, so no existing client changes its
handshake. `false` makes the host withhold `userInput/request` toward
this client — the D-027 additive-optional-field + withheld-method
convention.

Deliberately NOT a `requestedCapabilities` name: that registry records
operations a host GRANTS (SS1.4.4), and whether a client can draw a
dialog is a fact about the client, never a privilege the host hands
out.

ClientInfo.description:
Client identification inside `initialize` params (SS1.4.1). Diagnostics
and telemetry attribution only; never an authority claim (SS1.10).

name.description: Machine identifier, `[a-z0-9_]+` (SS1.4.1).

ClientRef.description:
A client's own name for an image part (ADR 78319 D2): 1 to 256 bytes of
UTF-8, returned verbatim. Open, so a later optional member decodes on an
older client.

CodeModeLanguage.description:
The language a Code Mode cell ran in (ADR 42727 D2). Open: values are
lowercase VS Code language identifiers, and only `javascript` (the V8
engine) is minted today.

CodeModeOutputSpan.description:
One public-output span inside the item's `visibleOutput` (ADR 42727 D3).

Offsets index the UTF-8 encoding of the **decoded** `visibleOutput`
string, never the JSON-escaped wire text; both ends fall on code-point
boundaries; named and measured like `item/readOutput`'s byte range.

lengthBytes.description: Length of the span, in bytes.

offsetBytes.description: Start of the span, in bytes.

CodeModeOutputStream.description:
What a Code Mode output span's bytes are (ADR 42727 D3). Open: each
engine mints its own values.

CodeModeReceipt.description:
Code Mode's `details` payload (ADR 42727 D2/D3).

Every member is absent when it does not apply, never `null`; an empty
`outputSpans` list is never served.

cellItemId.description:
`wait` only, when the producer resolved it: the `itemId` of the
`execute` item that started the cell.

language.description:
`execute`, and `wait` when the producer resolved the originating
execute: the language the cell ran in.

outputSpans.description:
The public cell-output spans, ascending and non-overlapping; absent
when there is no cell body or a hook rewrote the served body.

sourceArg.description:
`execute` only: the top-level key of the item's `args` object whose
value is the cell source. A pointer, never source bytes.

CommandAcceptedResult.description:
The uniform SS3.1.2 command acknowledgement: admission only, never an
outcome. `session/compact` alone may answer `"noop"`; every other command
answers `"accepted"`.

status.description: `"accepted"` for every admitted command (SS3.1.2; closed vocabulary).

CommandAckStatus.description:
The ack-status vocabulary: `"accepted"` for every admitted command;
`session/compact` alone may answer `"noop"`. Closed: the protocol defines
exactly these two values, so SDK clients get a discriminated type and
validation catches a wrong status — and a client that received a third value
would have been told nothing it can act on, unlike [`TurnStartDisposition`],
where "acked, not otherwise classified" is a usable reading.

CommandStatus.description:
The SS3.1.2 ack `status`: `accepted` for every admitted command.
`session/compact` is the one method that may additionally answer `noop`
([`crate::method::runtime::CompactStatus`]); no other command uses another
status (tdd SS3.1.2).

CompactStatus.description:
`session/compact`'s ack status (tdd SS3.7): the one method that may answer
`noop` in addition to the SS3.1.2 `accepted`. A noop is a success, not an
error, and it is durably settled like any other outcome.

CompactionOutcome.description: Compaction outcome (tdd SS4.5.10, the SS3.7 vocabulary). Open.

CompactionTrigger.description: What initiated a compaction (tdd SS4.5.10). Open.

ComputerUseApp.description: One row of the Settings apps list.

bundleId.description: The app's bundle ID: the stored key.

choice.description: The choice as it applies: a block wins over a grant.

lastAskedAt.description:
When Computer Use last showed an approval card for the app, RFC3339
UTC; absent when it never has.

locked.description:
Settings can't change this row; its choice is `blocked`. Omitted
means false.

lockedBy.description: Why the row is locked, when it is.

name.description:
The name the approval card shows for it, else the name stored with
its grant or its last card; absent when there is none.

ComputerUseAppLock.description: Why Settings can't change a row. **Open**.

ComputerUseAppPatch.description: One per-app choice to set in `computerUseSettings/update`.

choice.description:
`ask` removes the app's grant and the user's block; `alwaysAllow`
saves a grant and removes the user's block; `blocked` adds the
user's block and removes the grant.

ComputerUseBlockedApp.description: One row of the Settings blocked-apps list.

bundleId.description: The app's bundle ID, or the family prefix when `prefix` is true.

locked.description: A built-in block, which Settings cannot remove (ADR 630 D18.8).

prefix.description:
A built-in family row: it blocks every bundle ID that starts with
`bundleId`. Omitted means false; only locked rows are prefixes.

ComputerUseChoice.description:
A capability dropdown's value (ADR 630 D18.4). **Open**: the read result
carries it, so an older client tolerates a value it does not know.

ComputerUseInstalledApp.description: One installed or running app, for Settings' app picker.

name.description: The name the approval card shows for it.

ComputerUseLockHolder.description:
The Computer Use lock's holder as a `computerUseTakeover` approval shows
it: never its app, window, target or current action (ADR 73131 D2).

acquiredAt.description: When the holder took the lock (RFC 3339).

lastActivityAt.description: When the holder last acted under the lock (RFC 3339).

ComputerUsePermission.description: One macOS permission as setup last saw it. **Open**, like the phase.

apps.description:
The apps list: apps Computer Use has asked about, most recent first;
then the other saved grants, then the user's other blocks; then the
locked rows. Each app once. A host that serves the list always
answers it, so its absence means an older host.

blockedApps.description:
The user's blocks in the order they were added, then the built-in
blocks when `showBuiltIns` asked for them.

computerControl.description:
The computer-control dropdown, as it applies: `ask` while the stored
blocked-apps list can't be read (ADR 630 D18.4).

installedApps.description:
The installed and running apps, sorted by name, when the read asked
for `installed`.

screenshots.description: The screenshots dropdown, under the same rule.

installed.description: Also answer `installedApps`, for an app picker. Omitted means false.

showBuiltIns.description:
Also list the built-in blocks as locked rows (the D18.8 toggle).
Omitted means false.

ComputerUseSettingsUpdateParams.description:
`computerUseSettings/update` params: a patch. Omitted members are left
alone; the whole patch applies or none of it does.

apps.description:
Per-app choices to set. A locked app is refused; so is a bundle ID
named twice, or also in `blockApps` or `unblockApps`.

blockApps.description:
Bundle IDs to add to the user's blocked apps. A built-in block is
refused: it is already blocked.

unblockApps.description:
Bundle IDs to remove from the user's blocked apps. Only the user's own
entries can be removed; a built-in block stays.

sessionId.description:
The session whose setup state changed; absent for the host's own
setup, which only `computerUseHostSetup` holders receive.

ComputerUseSetupPhase.description:
Where the session's setup stands: `cua_setup`'s state codes, camelCase.
**Open**: a result vocabulary, so an older client tolerates a new state.

sessionId.description:
The session whose setup to read. Omitted reads the host's own setup,
which needs the `computerUseHostSetup` grant.

commandId.description: The client's id for this command.

sessionId.description:
The session whose setup to start. Omitted starts the host's own
setup, which needs the `computerUseHostSetup` grant.

ComputerUseSetupState.description:
The session's setup state: the result of both methods and the
`computerUseSetup/changed` payload's `state`.

inputMonitoring.description: Input Monitoring: computer use is ready without it; some actions need it.

message.description: The sentence `cua_setup` gives the user for this answer.

refused.description: The `cua_setup` refusal code when the call was refused, verbatim.

ContextPressureLevel.description:
Context pressure level (tdd SS4.6.6): hard threshold first, both
inclusive `>=`. Open.

ContextUsage.description:
The SS4.9.1 snapshot `contextUsage` block: the latest
`(windowTokens, usedTokens, pressure)` triple; the snapshot member is
`null` until the fold's generation chain holds a tracked anchor AND the
current basis is present (absent is never fabricated).

usedTokens.description: Counted-once occupancy at the latest provider-reported fact.

windowTokens.description: The effective context-window size; absent when the basis has no limit.

ContinuePausedSource.description:
D7's explicit continuation object on `session/resume`: requests explicit
continuation of the named loaded actor, subject to ordinary drive
authorization and actual successful acceptance.

sourceInstanceId.description: The loaded source actor to continue.

CronQuarantine.description:
`cronQuarantine` on `session/resume` (ADR 72647 D1): this resume's own
load opened the session cron store and quarantined a corrupt database.

quarantinePath.description:
Host-local path the corrupt database was moved to; the path the
gate-off warning shows.

CronReceipt.description:
Cron's `details` payload (ADR 42728 D2, thirteenth directive).

Every field a family owns lives here, under the container's one `details`
key, rather than flat beside the discriminators. Each is a **bounded machine
fact**: scalars, short identifiers and a small fixed-shape array of those.

jobId.description:
Cron `create` and `delete`: the job id. On `delete`'s `missing` arm this
is the caller's own id echoed back — that arm has no server-side subject
to name.

On the `created` + `cancelled` pairing, this field also conveys the
hidden fact: a job row was committed and will fire.

jobs.description:
Cron `list`: the served jobs in server order, `active` and `firing`
rows only.

nextFireAtMs.description:
Cron `create` (`created`, `duplicate`): absolute epoch-milliseconds of
the job's next scheduled fire (the existing job's on `duplicate`,
ADR 42728 D2).

CronReceiptJob.description:
One row of the Cron `list` receipt's `jobs` array (ADR 42728 D2).

Server order, and **`active` + `firing` rows only**. A small fixed-shape
array of scalars, which is what keeps it a bounded machine fact.

nextFireAtMs.description: Absolute epoch-milliseconds of the job's next scheduled fire.

CuaLockChange.description: One lock transition for one session. Open discriminated union on `kind`.

bySessionId.description:
The session that took the lock over. Present only when `reason` is
`takenOver`.

epoch.description:
The per-Mac lock epoch: the one that ended for `lost`, the new one for
`acquired`. It rises by one on every acquire and appears in no
Computer Use tool result.

reason.description:
Why the session lost the lock: `takenOver | reaped | released |
lapsed`, an open vocabulary. Present when `kind` is `lost`.

CuaLockChanged.description:
`cua/lockChanged` params: one per lock transition, sent to the
`computerUseSetup` holders that follow the affected session.

sessionId.description: The session whose hold on the lock changed.

CumulativeCost.description:
Server-computed session cost member of [`CumulativeTokenUsage`]
(tdd SS4.6.5, Amendment #41610 FR-41610-2/3).

partial.description:
True when at least one leg lacked price data — clients render
`(partial)`.

usd.description: Estimated USD total, finite and non-negative.

CumulativeTokenUsage.description:
Session running totals of counted-once usage (tdd SS4.6.5).

The cache splits and server-computed `cost` join the counters. The counters
stay accumulate-only; `cost` is the documented exception — it may move
either way on price re-adoption and is labeled estimate. `Copy` was dropped
for the `cost` member.

cacheReadTokens.description:
Cache-read tokens, session total (FR-41610-1): saturating sum of
the per-completion splits; an absent split contributes 0.
Additive-optional: absent on the wire reads as 0 and zero totals
are omitted, so pre-feature bytes decode and re-encode identically.

cacheWriteTokens.description:
Cache-write tokens, session total (FR-41610-1). Additive-optional
like the read split.

cost.description:
Server-computed session cost (FR-41610-2): `None` (wire-absent)
when no leg is priced — clients omit the row. Additive-optional:
absent reads as unpriced.

DamagedRange.description:
`damagedRange`: what one damaged range of the session log cost (ADR
60914 D1/D2). The reader finds the range in the log bytes; no log record
is written for it, so every member is derived from the readable records
around it.

lastGoodTurnId.description:
The last finished turn before the first damaged range, when one
exists: the safe `session/fork` cut (ADR 60914 D1 "Fork cuts", D4).

missingRecords.description:
Records the log proves missing (session-stream sequence numbers no
readable record or unreadable line accounts for).

readableBeforeAt.description:
RFC3339 `recordedAt` of the last readable record before the range;
absent when the range starts the log.

unreadableLines.description: Physical log lines in the range that are not a readable record.

DeliveredInput.description:
One input the read session's log delivered to a subagent (tdd
SS2.5.5, ADR 72596-delivered-inputs-on-read D2): the queue-note
summary (never the body) plus the queue and drain record sequences,
the order and re-read dedupe keys, plus the join ids clients adopt
already-rendered rows by.

deliveredSequence.description:
The matching drain record's log sequence: the Delivered row's
position key.

sequence.description:
The queued record's log sequence: entry order, and half of the
sequence-pair join key.

sourceCommandId.description:
The `SubagentInput` record's command id: the key wire-twin rows
join by in either order. Absent when the record carries none.

sourceRunRecordId.description:
The queue record's run-log id: the record-row join key. Absent
when the host's record carries no mirror metadata (a pre-feature
host), which falls back to the command id, then the
sequence-pair join.

subagentId.description: The subagent the input was delivered to (parent-scope id).

summary.description: The stored queue-note summary (never the body).

DriveChangedReason.description:
Why a session's drive holder changed (tdd SS2.16; ADR
58706-drive-handover D3). **Open**: a newer host may add a reason; a
client keeps an unknown word and treats the frame as a holder change. No
`started`: every `session/start`, `fork` and `sideChat` already
broadcasts `session/started`, and the starter drives by construction.

DriveReleaseStatus.description:
The answer to a drive release (tdd SS2.16). **Open**: a newer host may
add a status; a client keeps an unknown word and treats it as "not
released".

DriveRequestStatus.description:
The answer to a drive request (tdd SS2.16). **Open**: a newer host may
add a status; a client keeps an unknown word and treats it as "not
granted".

EarlierHistory.description:
`earlierHistory`: the boundary checkpoint's transcript tail, served in
place of every item that opened in its pruned prefix (ADR 71910 D1/D3).
No log record carries it; the host derives it from the checkpoint.

messages.description:
The tail entries whose source record is in the pruned prefix, in
tail order (at most 50, spec 6127 INV-002). May be empty.

EarlierHistoryMessage.description: One transcript-tail message of an [`EarlierHistory`] item.

role.description:
Open string enum: `"user"` or `"assistant"`, the only roles a host
serves; a client skips any other value (spec 6127 FM-004).

text.description:
The stored tail text verbatim (at most 1,000 characters); clients
apply their own assistant display rules.

EffectiveApprovalModeState.description:
The effective approval-mode projection (`EffectiveApprovalModeState`,
tdd SS5.12): the same object `session/setApprovalMode` returns as
`effectiveMode` and the `Session` object carries as `approvalMode`.

lastCommandId.description: The command that last set it; `null` when no command did.

EffectiveModel.description: The latest effective-model fact in the snapshot (tdd SS4.9.1).

providerId.description: The selected provider; `null` when the selection names none.

EffectivePermissionState.description:
The effective permission-state projection (`EffectivePermissionState`,
amendment 42624 FR-42624-4): the committed native permission snapshot
(profile identity, reviewer authority) plus the live per-session runtime's
attachment evidence. The same object `session/setPermissionProfile`
returns and the `Session` object carries as `permissionState`. Served
values must be coherent: a read never combines an old profile with a newer
runtime's attachment claim (ADR 42197 D3).

axes.description:
The committed profile's effective four axis values (amendment 44483
FR-44483-2): the resolved filesystem, network, approval, and reviewer
the YOLO predicate reads. Omitted when unknown — an older host, the
no-profile state, or the commit-receipt fallback arm that reports
without a re-inspect — and a client MUST fall back to the served id
there, never infer equivalence it cannot see.

clientApprovalRules.description:
The session's client-supplied shell prefix allow-rules with origin
(tdd SS5.16, ADR 47712 D6, ruled). Absent means the host folded none
— never fabricated. **Experimental**.

profileId.description:
The committed profile id; `null` when the committed source is a launch
override (`LaunchOverrides` pins `id: None`); every catalog row and
configured/default commit carries a non-null id.

reviewerAttached.description:
Whether an executable reviewer is currently installed for this loaded
session (live runtime evidence).

ErrorData.description:
The optional `error.data` object (SS1.6). All members additive-optional;
`kind` is always present when `data` is.

admissionId.description: Admission identity on admission errors (amendment 45445 FR-45445-13).

after.description:
The rejected raw-log anchor, on `missingAnchor`, `prunedPrefix`,
and `wrongStream`.

alignedNextOffset.description:
The next provable UTF-8 boundary on a misaligned text-media
`item/readOutput` read (`-32602` `invalidParams`, FR-016b/D-17214-2):
absent when no boundary is provable from the stored bytes ahead.

anchor.description:
The rejected anchor value on `notFound`/`missingAnchor` and the
`-32042` boundary arms (SS4.7.3, SS4.11); on `-32042` it is served
as an explicit `null` when the request named no concrete anchor
(spec 208 FM-005).

availability.description:
The stored output's availability on `outputUnavailable` — the durable
`ToolOutputAvailability` value, read-time-derived when the durable
record still says `available` (SS4.5.5; spec 208 FM-008).

axes.description:
Every too-wide axis with its requested and ceiling values, on
`limitsAboveMax` (tdd SS2.9; ADR 39851-ss1-10 D2 Q2; ADR 59770 D4).

capability.description:
The missing capability, on `capabilityRequired` errors. Typed on the
grantable registry, so the experimental-only `rawLog` joins the stable
domain as an additive open-enum extension when it graduates.

capacity.description: The configured command-admission bound, on `backpressured` errors.

commandId.description:
The rejected command's identifier, on `commandRejected` errors. The
ratified v1 contract pairs it with `reason`
(specs/13929-msp-activation/tdd.md SS3.6 admission-failure table and
its `-32030` example), so a client can settle the exact command it
sent without parsing the message string.

cursorStream.description: The stream the anchor's id actually belongs to, on `wrongStream`.

descriptor.description:
On `experimentalRequired` errors, the name of the experimental method,
field or variant the request used, for example
`turn/start.providerRequestOptions`.

earliestCursor.description:
The oldest servable view position on `viewTruncated` (`-32040`,
SS4.11); served as an explicit `null` when nothing before the head
is servable — the null is present on the wire, never a dropped key
(spec 208 FM-005 / Scenario 6.2).

failureKind.description:
The mint failure class, on `usageRefreshFailed` (ADR 32563 D6 item
5): `terminal`, `transient` (a 5xx, 429 or network failure; the only
class with `retryable: true`), `onboarding`, `age_requirement`,
`payment_subscription_required` or `credential_rejected`. Never
credential material.

index.description:
The rejected edit's index into the `settings/writeMany` `edits`
array, on the same arms; absent on `settings/writeValue`, which
carries no edit list.

itemId.description:
The item whose stored output was requested, on the `item/readOutput`
arms (`notFound`, `outputUnavailable`, and the misaligned-offset
`invalidParams`).

keyPath.description:
The rejected settings key path, on the `settings/writeValue` and
`settings/writeMany` arms: the structural `-32602 invalidParams`
shape and the `-32030` managed-denial block (spec 13929 amendment
43458 FR-43458-3/FR-43458-6). File spelling verbatim, like the
request's `keyPath`.

kind.description: The stable camelCase category clients branch on.

latestBoundaryCursor.description:
The latest installed boundary's view cursor on the `-32042` arms —
always present in the `-32042` JSON and explicitly `null` when no
boundary exists (SS4.11, FM-004).

limitBytes.description: The exceeded byte limit, on `inputTooLarge` errors.

name.description:
The rejected marketplace name on `marketplaceNotFound` (`-32034`,
SS3.29.7) and `marketplaceAlreadyExists` (`-32036`, SS3.29.2); the
rejected plugin name on `pluginNotFound` (`-32035`, SS3.29.1).

outputRef.description: The requested `outputRef.id`, on the same `item/readOutput` arms.

path.description:
The subject repository path, on `workspaceNotTrusted` (ADR 31776
D11 E1, #31776).

reason.description:
Failure detail vocabulary (e.g. `"missingAnchor"` on `notFound` for a
missing view-cursor anchor).

recoveryObservation.description:
The original recovery-dependent construction's coherent observation.
An absent or unusable observation establishes no supported recovery.

retryAfterMs.description:
How long until the next refresh may mint, on
`usageRefreshRateLimited` (ADR 32563 D6).

retryable.description:
Whether retrying can succeed (e.g. `overloaded`). When present,
overrides the error table row's `retryable` default for this code.

seedFallbackReason.description:
Why the branch seed did not use a checkpoint, on the same arms:
one of `no_usable_checkpoint`, `unsupported_checkpoint_shape`,
`checkpoint_has_model_visible_tail`, `checkpoint_missing_suffix`;
absent when the seed used a checkpoint or no fallback was recorded.

seedPath.description:
The branch-seed path the host read before rejecting, on
branch-validation rejections (`session/fork`, `session/sideChat`:
the `forkBoundaryInvalid`, `commandRejected` and `sessionNotFound`
arms; SS2.5.3, SS2.5.7; #51365): one of `runtime_checkpoint_tail`,
`runtime_full_replay`, `legacy_session_data` — the durable
branch-seed vocabulary, so the client cites the real seed decision
instead of guessing at a stale binary.

selector.description: The rejected skill selector on `skillNotFound` (`-32032`, SS3.22.4).

sessionId.description: Session identity on errors whose lookup is session-scoped.

stream.description:
The rejected raw-log stream, on the SS6.9 anchor arms
(`missingAnchor`, `prunedPrefix`, `unknownStream`).

uploadId.description: The rejected upload id on `uploadNotFound` (`-32038`, SS3.33).

viewCursor.description: The blocked view position on `pageEventTooLarge` errors.

ErrorKind.description:
A stable `error.data.kind` category: camelCase, the value clients branch on.
Open: new kinds are added as their methods land, and a new `kind` is
additive only because this domain is declared open.

oneOf.description:
A drive-taking verb refused because this daemon is draining on the
binary-change upgrade path (`-32039`, the SS3 command-plane
block's free tail — see [`DAEMON_DRAINING_CODE`]); `data.paths` names the
canonical socket to retry against and `data.retryable` is `true`
(ADR 59770 D6/D7). Experimental tier with the socket surface
(promotion gate in #69224).

The daemon's startup credential or catalog step is still running
(`-32015`, the SS1 cross-cutting block); `data.retryable` is
`true` and the message names the pending step (ADR 59770 D8,
#68575). Experimental tier with the socket daemon surface.

A `session/start` choice is wider than the host ceiling on at least
one axis (`-32028`, the SS2 session-lifecycle block); `data.axes`
names every too-wide axis with its requested and ceiling values and
`data.retryable` is `false` (tdd SS2.9; ADR 39851-ss1-10 D2 Q2;
ADR 59770 D4; #59776 takes over #44493). Experimental tier with the
socket limits surface.

A worktree action names an untrusted repository (`-32029`, the SS2
session-lifecycle block); `data.path` names the subject repo and
`data.retryable` is `false` (ADR 31776 D8/D11 E1, #31776).
Experimental tier with the worktree surface (D7).

A raw-log cursor position names no position of the requested stream
(`-32060`, SS6.9); `data.stream` and `data.after` name the rejected
anchor. Experimental tier (#44985).

A raw-log anchor (or the origin) falls in a retention-pruned prefix
(`-32061`, SS6.9); `data.nextAvailable` carries the earliest readable
position. Experimental tier (#44985).

A raw-log anchor id exists in the session but belongs to a different
stream (`-32062`, SS6.9). Experimental tier (#44985).

No such stream in the session (`-32063`, SS6.9). Experimental tier
(#44985).

No such registered projection (`-32064`, SS6.9). Experimental tier
(#44985).

Decide after the durable terminal (`-32071`, amendment 45445
FR-45445-13); `data.admissionId` plus the winning
`data.admissionResolution`, `data.retryable: false`. Experimental tier.

Choice is not among the current `availableChoices` (`-32072`,
amendment 45445 FR-45445-13); `data.admissionId` and
`data.choiceId` name the rejected pair. Experimental tier.

A `usage/refresh` inside the per-host window (`-32080`, ADR
32563 D6); `data.retryAfterMs` is the time left, `data.retryable:
true`. Experimental tier.

A `usage/refresh` on a host with no Meta-account login to mint
with (`-32081`, ADR 32563 D6). Experimental tier.

A `usage/refresh` whose mint failed (`-32082`, ADR 32563 D6);
`data.failureKind` names the class. Experimental tier.

ErrorObject.description: The `error` member of an error response (SS1.2 §2.4).

code.description:
Registry code (Appendix B). Typed as a plain integer on the wire; the
value domain is the registry below (INV-018).

message.description: Human-readable message. Never a branch point (SS1.6).

ErrorResponse.description:
An error response frame (SS1.2 §2.4). Exactly one of `result` or `error`
appears on a response; this type is the `error` half.

id.description:
Echo of the request id; `null` **only** for an unrecoverable parse
error whose offending id could not be recovered (SS1.3). Always
serialized, so `None` renders as `null` rather than being omitted —
required-but-nullable (see [`require_nullable_id`]).

EventLogDegradedCode.description:
Why a session's event log degraded (ADR 72648 D1). **Closed**, like the
record code it mirrors (ADR 10139): a new code is a deliberate protocol
change, because a client renders each code's own text.

ExternalWaitView.description:
The live host-declared external wait as served on a `Session` object
(`Session.externalWait`): present exactly while a declaration is
live for the loaded session, absent otherwise. Absence is never
fabricated — an unloaded row carries no member.

reason.description:
The host's label for what the session waits on. Omitted when
the host declared without one.

FeedbackClassification.description:
`feedback/submit` classification (tdd SS3.25): the four TUI classes in
camelCase wire spelling. **Closed**: a client-selected param
vocabulary (#22785 E2).

FeedbackSubmitOutcome.description:
`feedback/submit` result `outcome` (tdd SS3.25): how one confirmed
submit resolved, mirroring the TUI `FeedbackSubmitOutcome` taxonomy.
**Open**: a server-produced result vocabulary (#22785 E2) — an older
client reading a newer value it does not know follows the open-enum
tolerance rule instead of rejecting it.

FeedbackSubmitParams.description:
`feedback/submit` params (tdd SS3.25): mirrors the TUI confirm-time
`FeedbackRequest`. The call itself is the explicit confirm.

attachSessionRecord.description:
Consent to attach the session record; honored only for
`bug`/`badResult` with `session_id` present. `true` with
`with_files: false`, with a non-`bug`/`badResult` classification,
or without `session_id` is `invalidParams` (F4, F8).
Defaults to `false`.

clientArtifactsPath.description:
An absolute same-host path to a client-packed bundle, admitted
only as a regular file under a size cap.

note.description: The user report text (required; non-empty for `bug`).

sessionId.description:
Names the session this call is about when present (F8,
superseding F3): the bundle lands in that session's dir. Names a
session this host owns. When absent, the bundle lands in the
host-level feedback folder and the `session_id` tag is omitted.

bundlePath.description: The host-local absolute path of the always-written local bundle.

cause.description:
The failure cause on the `failed`, `acceptedWithoutReceipt`,
`trackingFailed`, and `trackingUncertain` arms.

localTracingNote.description: The consent-vs-reality local-tracing note, kept for display.

retryAfterMs.description: The effective retry delay in milliseconds, on `rateLimited`.

sessionNote.description: The consent-vs-reality session note, kept for display.

sessionRecordAttached.description: Whether the consented session record rode at all.

sessionRecordTruncated.description: Whether the consented session record rode shortened to fit.

taskId.description: The internal receipt-Task id once that Task succeeds.

uploadId.description:
The intake's accept id — always present on the `uploaded` arm,
optional on `trackingFailed`/`trackingUncertain`; never fabricated
on `recorded`.

ForkCutPoint.description:
Where a fork cuts the source history (tdd SS2.5.3). Turn ids are used
instead of counts because ids stay stable across compaction and concurrent
appends while indices do not.

lastTurnId.description:
The last completed turn to copy, inclusive. Naming an in-progress or
unknown turn fails `forkBoundaryInvalid`.

ForkProvenance.description:
Fork provenance folded from the durable `session.fork.created` record
(`ForkProvenance`, tdd SS2.4).

commandId.description: The `commandId` of the `session/fork` that created it.

cutCursor.description:
An **opaque provenance string** preserved verbatim from the durable
record. Display-only — not one of the SS6.2 cursor families: clients
MUST NOT parse it and no method accepts it (tdd SS2.4).

cutExplicit.description: Whether the fork named an explicit cut point.

isRewind.description:
`true` when validated full provenance records a conversation rewind,
`false` for a proved ordinary fork (ADR 50280 D8). **Additive-optional**:
omitted when the serving face holds no full provenance, which means
unknown, never a guessed ordinary fork; never `null`.

sessionId.description: The source session this fork was cut from.

Goal.description:
The session goal block (tdd SS4.6.2, mirrors the runtime's goal state,
camelCased). `status` and `percentComplete` are carried **verbatim** —
out-of-contract status strings and >100 percents pass through; display
clamping is the renderer's job.

createdAtMs.description:
Goal creation time, epoch milliseconds, verbatim from the durable row.
Absent on blocks whose producer never carried it (tool-result adoptions,
older logs); absence must never render as a fabricated zero.

status.description:
Goal status, verbatim from the durable goal state (free string by
design: out-of-contract values pass through).

updatedAtMs.description:
Last goal mutation time, epoch milliseconds, verbatim from the durable
row. Same absence rule as `createdAtMs`.

GoalClearParams.description:
`goal/clear` params (tdd SS3.18). An `objective` here is an unknown field
and rejects `-32602 invalidParams` — the bare verbs carry exactly this
pair.

GoalCommandResult.description:
The shared SS3.18 goal ack, admission-only: all five verbs answer this
one shape (the tdd's "Shared contract"), differing only in when `turnId`
is present.

turnId.description:
Present by exactly the four SS3.18 result cases: an idle wake carries
the fresh goal turn's id; a busy `set`/`edit`/`resume` carries the
admission-time active turn's id (a routing fact, not a delivery
promise); `pause`/`clear` never carry it; an idle admission whose
resulting goal is not unfinished parks the notification and carries
none. **Additive-optional**: absent means "no turn named", never
fabricated.

GoalEditParams.description:
`goal/edit` params (tdd SS3.18): replace the current goal's objective.
Same shape as `goal/set`; the verbs differ in their `missing_goal`
precondition, not their payload.

objective.description: The replacement objective; same trim/non-empty rule as `goal/set`.

GoalSetParams.description: `goal/set` params (tdd SS3.18): set the session's goal objective.

objective.description:
The objective text; required, non-empty after Unicode-whitespace trim
(the trimmed text is the payload). Empty-after-trim is
`-32602 invalidParams` (tdd SS3.18).

HeldFor.description:
What holds a tool call before it is admitted to execute (ADR 50063 D6).
Open: a client reads an unknown value as held by something it does not
know, never as released.

HistoryMode.description:
What history a lifecycle result actually served (tdd SS2.5.2). Open on the
client side: report-what-was-served means a client treats an unknown mode
as "page it yourself".

HistoryNoneReason.description:
Why a result served `history.mode: "none"` — the server's typed reason for
serving no history, with one push-only exception: `projectionRebuildFailed`
rides only a `session/viewHealthChanged` notification; no resume or read
result carries it (see its variant doc). Open on the client side: an
absent (older server) or unknown (newer server) value decodes
conservatively as an unknown reason, and `viewCursor` text never
substitutes for it.

HistoryPreference.description:
The `history` request preference of `session/resume` (tdd SS2.5.2). The
forced values downgrade `anchored` → `inline` → `snapshot` → `none`; under
`auto` the full rung order is anchoredSnapshot → anchored pending cut →
inline → snapshot → pending cut → elided snapshot → elided pending cut →
none, a pending cut being the snapshot with its `monitorInbox` cut to the
entries still awaiting delivery.

HookAnswerKind.description:
A hook's answer word (ADR 79509 plugin hooks D4). **Closed**: client input
that the host checks, and no word approves a tool call.

enabled.description:
The row's own switch (tdd SS3.26.1). Non-enabled rows are
included as `false`, never dropped.

event.description: The event the handler runs on (ADR 33398 D7 item 2).

handlerKind.description: Where the handler comes from (ADR 33398 D7 item 1).

key.description: The handler key (config key or plugin hook id).

event.description:
The agent's hook event for the plugin event, as `hook/list` spells it: only
`sessionStart`, `userPromptSubmit`, `preToolUse`, `postToolUse` and
`stop` are hook events of a plugin.

matcher.description: A tool name pattern, only for `preToolUse` and `postToolUse`.

timeoutMs.description: The hook's deadline in milliseconds; 2,000 when absent.

HookDeclareParams.description:
`hook/declare` params (tdd SS3.41, FR-79509-1): the connection's whole
hook set, in install order and then manifest order. The call replaces the
set that the connection declared before, and an empty list removes it.

HookEventName.description:
Hook event names (tdd SS3.26.1, ADR 33398 D7 item 2): the
lowercase-first-letter spelling of every `HookEventKind::all()`
variant. Open (server-produced result vocabulary, the #22785
enum-openness rule): a future event value is additive.

HookHandlerKind.description:
A hook row's origin (tdd SS3.26.1, ADR 33398 D7 item 1): the config
`HookSourceKind` values plus plugin-contributed. Open (server-produced
result vocabulary, the #22785 enum-openness rule): a future origin is
additive.

HookListParams.description:
`hook/list` params (tdd SS3.26.1). Per-session because hook scope
follows the session's workspace and plugin state.

HookListResult.description:
`hook/list` result (tdd SS3.26.1): one row per installed handler per
event — a `ResolvedHookHandler` carries one event, and grouping would
lose matcher/command identity (ADR 33398 D7 item 1).

hooks.description:
The session's installed hook rows (tdd SS3.26.1 promises the
set, not an order).

HookRequestParams.description:
`hook/request` params (tdd SS3.41, FR-79509-2): one call of a hook that
the receiving connection declared.

input.description: The hook call's arguments: the shared `HookInputs` member of the event.

sessionId.description: The session whose event the hook sees.

timeoutMs.description: The rest of the hook's deadline when the host sent the request.

turnId.description: The turn; absent only for `sessionStart`.

HookRequestResult.description:
`hook/request` result (FR-79509-2): the hook's answer, the shared
`HookAnswers` member of its event, as the hook tool's `structuredContent`
gave it. Each answer has the word `answer` and the members of its kind.

context.description: Text for the model, for `continue` and a prompt `rewrite`.

input.description: The new tool input, for a `preToolUse` `rewrite`.

reason.description: Why, for `deny`, `ask` and `block`.

HookRunStatus.description:
`hookRun` durable outcome (tdd SS4.5.11). Open: new outcomes are
additive, and clients MUST render unknown values generically.

HostReadLimitsResult.description: `host/readLimits` result (tdd SS1.10): the host's posture ceiling.

maxLimits.description: The starter's limits: what a connection may choose.

HostShutdownParams.description:
`host/shutdown` params (ADR 73975 D2, B2): the park choice. `park`
absent (or `false`) keeps B1's abort semantics — a B1 client sending
`{}` keeps working against a B2 host. `park: true` parks every
pending prompt instead of aborting it: the drain skips settling them
and the next resume re-presents them before any turn. An ephemeral
host has no log to resume from, so it aborts and echoes
`parked: false` (#86579).

park.description: Park instead of abort (ADR 73975 D1/D2, B2).

HostShutdownResult.description:
`host/shutdown` result (ADR 73975 D2, B2): the mode echo. The reply
itself is the acknowledgement: the wire layer writes it during task
settlement, before the wind-down finalizer runs the drain, so
receipt means only "shutdown accepted". Drained is signaled by the
finalizer's `session/closed` frames, then EOF and serve exit; the
caller waits for exit before powering down.
`parked` echoes the effective mode: `true` = this shutdown parks
pending prompts, `false` = it aborts them (or the host predates B2,
whose `{}` deserializes to `false` — correctly, since a B1 host
always aborts). Parked-prompt COUNTS are not here: the drain runs
after the reply, so any count at reply time would be a pre-drain
snapshot, not the parked set — the parked set is the pending
approvals left pending in the log, and the trailing `clean`
SessionEnd makes the next resume re-present them (MspLoadClean).

parked.description: The effective shutdown mode (ADR 73975 D2, B2).

IfBusy.description:
Disposition when a turn is already running (tdd SS3.2). The wire default
is `queue`: an SDK caller who has not looked at session state should not
silently mutate an in-flight turn.

capabilities.description: Capability posture; absent means all defaults.

experimentalApi.description: Echo of the effective negotiated experimental setting.

grantedCapabilities.description:
Subset of the requested capabilities, plus policy-implicit grants.
Fixed for the connection lifetime (INV-009).

launchContext.description:
The launcher context this serve process started with (ADR 86936
D1). **Experimental**: present exactly when `grantedCapabilities`
lists `launchContext`, absent otherwise.

museHome.description: Absolute path of the muse home directory.

sandboxAvailability.description:
Whether this host can enforce the sandbox. Optional so adding it stays
backward compatible; a v1 host always sends it, and a client reads
absent as unknown — the host predates the field, so the client falls
back to its own probe rather than inventing an answer.

sandboxUnavailableReason.description:
Why enforcement is impossible. Sent only when `sandbox_availability`
is `unavailable`; a client MUST NOT infer a reason when none is
sent.

schema.description: Envelope schema version and stable-surface fingerprint.

sessionDurability.description:
Whether this host persists its sessions. Optional so adding it stays
backward compatible; a v1 host always sends it, and a client reads
absent as `durable` because no server that omits it has the ephemeral
profile.

userAgent.description: Exact user-agent string presented to upstream model providers.

Item.description:
