One transcript item at one revision (tdd SS4.4.1 common fields plus the
per-kind fields of SS4.5.2–4.5.11, all optional and owned by the kind
their doc names). `item/started`, `item/updated`, and `item/completed`
carry the full object; `item/delta` appends to it by field path.

action.description:
`webSearch`: the search action as an open-enum string — `search` |
`openPage` | `findInPage`, else tolerated unknown (tdd SS4.5.15,
**experimental**). Absent while the call is open (the action is not
final until the item completes).

approvalId.description:
`toolCall`: the approval that gated this call (tdd SS5); join key for
the approval view events.

args.description:
`toolCall`: the model-authored argument JSON, **verbatim**; clients
parse. Verbatim keeps the fold byte-deterministic and survives
model-emitted almost-JSON (tdd SS4.5.5).

attachments.description:
`userMessage`: image attachment metadata only — base64 payloads are
not echoed back on the view (tdd SS4.5.2).

background.description:
`toolCall`: `true` once the task was durably backgrounded; delivered
via `item/updated`.

backgroundInitiator.description:
`toolCall`: who backgrounded the task; absent on pre-split records —
never inferred (tdd SS4.5.5).

backgroundStatus.description:
`toolCall`: the backgrounded-row payload for a running
backgrounded item (ADR 50041 D1) — auto-yield or an explicit
user/timeout background; may appear with or without
`background`/`backgroundInitiator`. Experimental, delivered via
`item/updated`. Presentation only — never a durability claim.

backgroundTarget.description:
`toolCall`: this call's live background-target record
(tdd SS4.5.5; ADR 63254-background-target-on-tool-call D1–D2).
Set when the foreground tool starts, refreshed by whole-item
`item/updated` when the facts change, omitted once the call
settles or unregisters — present means a live candidate.
Absent (pre-feature hosts, unregistered calls) keeps the
client's derived behavior, never an error. Old clients
ignore it.

backgroundTerminalCompletion.description:
`backgroundTerminalCompletion`: the five facts the Finished
cell renders (ADR 50041 D4).

blocking.description:
`reminderChild`: `true` when this child is a blocking reminder (it holds
the turn open until it settles); absent otherwise, never `false` (ADR
41191 D4). The status word stays off the wire; clients name the
reminder from `reminderAgentId`.

byClient.description:
`userMessage`: the client that sent the message or steer (ADR 73001
D4); absent when unrecorded and on older logs.

childPromptRefs.description:
`workflow`: one `outputRef`-shaped link per recorded child spawn
with an objective (`kind: "workflow_child_prompt"`), fetched via
`item/readOutput` (tdd SS4.5.8/SS4.7.4, #45449).

childSessionId.description:
`subagent`/`reminderChild`: the child's own session id, readable via
`session/read`/`view/page` — child transcript drill-down without a
second protocol (tdd SS4.5.7).

childSessionLogPath.description:
`reminderChild`: parent-session-dir-relative child log path; absent
when no filesystem log.

children.description:
`workflow`: folded per-child state, keyed by `(childId, attempt)`,
re-emitted whole on every change — the item `revision` is the
ordering guard (tdd SS4.5.8).

commandId.description:
`userMessage`/`userShell`: the submitting command — multi-client UIs
de-duplicate their local echo on it.

controlStatus.description:
`subagent`: camelCased `SubagentControlStatus` (open enum); `status`
stays the generic item vocabulary.

cutOff.description:
`agentMessage`: `true` when the provider stream died mid-reply and
the run failed with this partial text committed (ADR 50063 D2) —
the wire mark for the gate-off "incomplete response" rule
(#13328). Absent otherwise; never cleared once set.

damagedRange.description: `damagedRange`: what the damaged range cost (ADR 60914 D2).

declaredPhase.description:
`workflow`: the run-level declared-phase label — the last `Phase`
detail-row label of the reconciled projection; terminal-only, absent
while live (tdd SS4.5.8, #45449).

deliveredBeforeTurnEnd.description:
`subagentInput` (`delivered`): `true` when the drain landed on its
turn before that turn's terminal, which ends the turn's final answer
as gate-off's drain record does; absent otherwise (ADR 70249 D4).

displayLabel.description: `toolCall`: the tool's own words for this call; absent = none (tdd SS4.5.5).

displayText.description:
`userMessage`: presentation form (tdd SS3.2); absent when the client
sent none.

durationMs.description:
`userShell`/`subagent`: observed wall-clock duration. `workflow`: the
run's wall time from launch to reconciliation, set only on the
settling `item/completed` — never a sum of child durations.
`toolCall`: the Backgrounded row's duration (ADR 50041 D11) — the
open→update record delta in whole ms, served on the
`backgroundStatus` re-emission and frozen there; absent otherwise.

earlierHistory.description:
`earlierHistory`: the boundary checkpoint's transcript tail (ADR
71910 D3, tdd SS4.5.22).

event.description: `hookRun`: the hook event in Q2 camelCase vocabulary (tdd SS4.5.11).

exitCode.description: `userShell`: the process exit code, when it exited by code.

exitSignal.description:
`userShell`: the terminating signal NUMBER, when signalled (e.g. 9) —
the durable payload verbatim; nothing maps numbers to names, and the
fold never invents one.

failureKind.description:
`toolCall`: machine-readable failure class (`TaskFailureKind`,
snake_case verbatim — durable runtime vocabulary, the SS1.6 casing
exemption).

fallbackText.description:
Server-provided one-line human summary any kind MAY carry, for
generic rendering of kinds a client does not recognize; new kinds
SHOULD carry it during their first release cycle (tdd SS4.10).

finalSummary.description:
`workflow`: the human terminal summary projected from the reconciled
Launch envelope, bounded at the 64 KiB surface budget; terminal-only
(tdd SS4.5.8, #45449).

held.description:
`toolCall` (ADR 50063 D4/D6): `true` while the call is held before it
is admitted to execute. Present on an item started at hold time,
cleared by the release `item/updated`, absent on calls never held.

heldFor.description:
`toolCall` (ADR 50063 D6): what holds the call; present exactly when
`held` is.

historyUnreadable.description:
`subagent`: the host could not read this live child's run records
when the parent resumed (ADR 68425 D1); a client says so once. A
resume-time observation: present only as `true`, absent otherwise,
never `false`, and never carried by a live notification.

inputPhase.description:
`subagentInput`: the record the item stands for; see
[`SubagentInputPhase`] (#70249).

itemId.description:
Bare UUIDv7; the item's identity across its whole lifecycle. Identity
rule (tdd SS4.4.1): the task id for task-backed kinds
(`toolCall`, `subagent`), the pre-minted commit `message_id` for
delta-streamed kinds (`agentMessage`, `reasoning`), `EventId::derive`
over the session id and the range's starting sequence number for
`damagedRange` (no record carries it, SS4.5.16), the same over the
boundary checkpoint's sequence number for `earlierHistory` (SS4.5.22),
and the opening durable record's event id for everything else.
Opaque to clients.

jobId.description:
`scheduledFire`: the cron job id that fired (tdd SS4.5.17;
ADR 45446 D2, spec 13929 amendment #62595 FR-62595-1).

kind.description:
The item kind (open enum): clients MUST render unknown kinds
generically — kind name plus `status` plus `fallbackText` (tdd
SS4.10).

message.description: `workflow`: the reconciled terminal message, set on completion.

messagePhase.description: `agentMessage`: the phase the model declared; see [`MessagePhase`].

modelVisibleContent.description:
`toolCall`: rich content the model saw beyond text; base64 is not
inlined on the view (tdd SS4.5.5).

monitorDescription.description:
`monitorFeed`: the monitor's arm-time description with the
durable `"Monitor event: "` summary prefix stripped; model-
controlled tool input under the 64 KiB per-surface budget —
sanitize before render (ADR 50058-monitor-feed-wire D1/D3).

monitorId.description:
`monitorFeed`: the monitor task id — the same value as that
monitor's `toolCall` `itemId` (ADR 50058-monitor-feed-wire D1).

nextFireAtMs.description:
`scheduledFire`: the next scheduled epoch in milliseconds;
absent on a final delivery (tdd SS4.5.17; ADR 45446 D2).

noticeKind.description:
`systemNotice`: an optional open machine code for what happened, minted
per origin by the slice that adds its producer; omitted for `monitor`
and for `hook` (tdd SS4.5.23).

noticeOrigin.description:
`systemNotice`: the producing family, so a client routes a notice
without parsing its text (tdd SS4.5.23). Absent means the server named
no origin: render generically, never infer one.

noticeSeverity.description:
`systemNotice`: the notice's level — `info` | `warning` | `error`,
open (tdd SS4.5.23; ADR 42729 D1). Absent means the server classified
no level.

noticeSubject.description:
`systemNotice`: the durable thing the notice is about — for `hook`,
the hook run's item id and its bounded label (tdd SS4.5.23; ADR 75121
D2).

objective.description:
`subagent`: objective as spawned, bounded on the wire at the 64 KiB
retained-text budget (tdd SS4.5.4, ADR 35691 D9); a cut sets
`truncated`. The durable record stays verbatim.

outputRef.description:
`toolCall`/`userShell`: stored-output reference; fetch the full bytes
via `item/readOutput` (served by #208).

parentSubagentId.description:
`subagent`: the `subagentId` of the subagent whose own session spawned this child, by
`subagent/list`'s `parentSubagentId` rule. **Additive-optional**: absent for a child of the
view's own session, or when no open `subagent` item in this view owns the spawning session;
never guessed, never derived from `agentPath` (tdd SS4.5.7, #88542).

patchRef.description:
`toolCall`: stored structured-patch reference (`kind: "tool_patch"`,
`mediaType: "application/json"`); the body is fetched via
`item/readOutput` with `patchRef.id`, and the ref survives the
SS2.5.2 elided-snapshot rung exactly like `outputRef` without ever
being an elision trigger (tdd SS2.5.2, SS4.5.5; #33025).

patchSummary.description:
`toolCall`: server-authored edit-family diff summary (#33025)
— always beside `patchRef`; absent = no diff available (tdd SS4.5.5).

pattern.description:
`webSearch`: the in-page pattern, verbatim — present iff
`action == "findInPage"` (tdd SS4.5.15, **experimental**).

paused.description:
`workflow`: `true` only while a durable pause fact is in force for
the run's generation; absent otherwise, never `false` (tdd SS4.5.8,
ADR 45437 D2; the fold sets it on pause commit and clears it on
resume-commit supersession or the generation's terminal).

peerMessage.description:
`peerMessage`: the four facts the consumed card renders (ADR
72708 D2, tdd SS4.5.24).

providerItemId.description:
`reasoning`: provider reasoning item id (e.g. `rs_...`), for
provider-side correlation.

providerStatus.description:
`webSearch`: the provider's terminal status, verbatim
(`"completed"` | `"failed"` | `"cancelled"` | other) — present on
the completed item (tdd SS4.5.15, **experimental**).

query.description:
`webSearch`: the search query, verbatim — present iff
`action == "search"` with a query to carry (tdd SS4.5.15,
**experimental**).

rawItem.description:
`webSearch`: the verbatim raw provider JSON frame under the 64 KiB
per-surface budget; past-budget frames cut here and ride whole
behind `outputRef` (tdd SS4.5.15, **experimental**).

reason.description:
`compaction`: noop/failure reason, verbatim (snake_case durable
vocabulary, e.g. `"no_compactable_history"`). `hookRun`: terminal-only
capped terminal reason (tdd SS4.5.11).

recordedAt.description:
RFC3339 timestamp of the item's driving durable record. Absent on
ephemeral-opened items until first durable re-emission (tdd SS4.4.1).

replayHint.description:
Monitor `toolCall`: the D26 hint verdict plus anchor
(`ReplayHint`); absent means no hint.

resultStatus.description: `subagentResult`: the consumed attempt's outcome; absent if unseen at the drain (#88809).

results.description:
`webSearch`: the typed result hits, verbatim, never truncated —
clients read `results.length` for the count (tdd SS4.5.15,
**experimental**).

retracted.description:
`userMessage`: `true` after an accepted retract (tdd SS4.5.1);
re-emitted via `item/updated`.

revision.description:
Integer >= 1, strictly monotonic per item; apply rule is
replace-iff-higher. `item/delta` never bumps it (tdd SS4.4.1).

runStatus.description:
`hookRun`: terminal-only durable outcome; stays `blocked` when the
item settles `rejected` (tdd SS4.5.11).

scheduledFireAtMs.description:
`scheduledFire`: the fire's scheduled epoch in milliseconds
(tdd SS4.5.17; ADR 45446 D2).

selector.description:
`skillRead`: the read skill's catalog selector (matches the
`skill/list` row; the raw observed id when the read resolved to
no catalog row). Set on every `skillRead` item (ADR 33401 D10);
old clients render it beside the kind name (SS4.10).

sideSessionId.description:
`sideChat`: the side's own session id, readable via
`session/read`/`view/page` — drill-down without a second protocol
(tdd SS4.5.13; ADR 45435 D3).

source.description:
`skillRead`: the catalog source (matches the `skill/list` row);
empty when the host could not resolve the read to a catalog row
(replay without the tool result, context-only evidence). Set on
every `skillRead` item (ADR 33401 D10); each client composes the
notice line from `selector` + `source`.

status.description:
Open enum; terminal = anything other than `"inProgress"`. Unknown
values MUST be treated as terminal-unknown and rendered generically
(tdd SS4.4.1).

statusAttempt.description:
`toolCall`: the latest external-attempt facet, field-for-field —
countdown inputs the client renders the tick from; absent when the
latest detail carries none (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448).

statusChildren.description:
`toolCall`: the latest child-summary facet, field-for-field; absent
when the latest detail carries none (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448).

statusHealth.description:
`toolCall`: the latest health facet, field-for-field; absent when
the latest detail carries none (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448).

statusLine.description:
`toolCall`: the task's visible latest-status line — the latest
`Status` message through the shared detail normalization; absent
when no status folded or nothing displayable remains (tdd SS4.5.5,
#45448).

statusPhase.description:
`toolCall`: the latest detail's phase row, verbatim; absent when the
latest detail carries none (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448).

statusProgress.description:
`toolCall`: the latest progress facet, field-for-field; absent when
the latest detail carries none (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448).

statusStep.description:
`toolCall`: the latest active-step facet, field-for-field; absent
when the latest detail carries none (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448).

steered.description:
`userMessage`: `true` when injected mid-turn via `turn/steer` or
`ifBusy: "steer"`; absent otherwise.

stopAvailable.description:
`workflow`: display-only stop affordance — `true` while the run is
open, `false` once settled; stopping rides `workflow/cancel`
(tdd SS4.5.8, #45449). Authorizes nothing.

summarizedThrough.description:
`compaction`: opaque provenance string naming the compaction boundary.
Also a compaction-anchored read anchor, accepted by `session/resume` and
`view/page`. Still opaque — clients relay it, never parse it.

summary.description:
`reasoning`: one entry per summary part; part *n* streams via
`item/delta` field `"summary.n"` (part boundary = index change).

terminalRowAfterItemId.description:
Terminal `toolCall`, or a `subagent` whose result drained
(#70249): the item after whose rows the terminal row renders
(tdd SS4.5.21, ADR 56496 D2/D3).

text.description:
`userMessage`: the prompt text as submitted. `agentMessage`: the
accumulated reply, streamed via `item/delta` field `"text"`.
`reasoning`: raw committed reasoning text where the provider exposes
it (never streamed in v1, tdd SS4.5.4).

tokenBudget.description:
`workflow`: the run's launch token budget, set from the launch fact
(tdd SS4.5.8, #45449); absent when the launch carried none.

tokensAfter.description: `compaction`: token budget snapshot after, when measured.

tokensBefore.description: `compaction`: token budget snapshot before, when measured.

toolReceipt.description:
`toolCall`: the shared semantic receipt — what the operation did, as
machine-readable fact (ADR 43399 D1, tdd SS4.5.5). Optional and
additive: absence is always valid and is never an error (D3). When
present, a server serves the **same** receipt on every item path —
`item/completed`, `view/page`, seeded snapshots and resume (D3).
Observation only; carries no control authority (D4), and no field in
it enters model-visible content (D7).

truncated.description:
`true` when the server's per-surface text budget saturated a streamed surface
(`agentMessage.text`, `reasoning.summary[*]`, `toolCall.visibleOutput`,
`userShell.visibleOutput`), cut a `subagent` surface (`objective`, `fallbackText`,
`result.summary`, `result.text`), or cut a `monitorFeed` surface (`text`, `fallbackText`,
`monitorDescription`) (ADR 50058-monitor-feed-wire D3), or cut a `systemNotice` surface
(`text`, `fallbackText`; the committed-surface budget, ADR 42729 D1, tdd SS4.5.23). On a
`subagent` item the flag is item-level and never cleared: once any of those four is cut,
every later update keeps it, even when `result.text` arrives whole (ADR 35691 D9). The
durable full text remains in the log (tdd SS4.5.4).

turnId.description:
The owning turn (== the submitting `commandId` for fresh turns, tdd
SS3.1.4). `null` for the kinds outside a turn: `userShell` always
(tdd SS4.5.6), `hookRun` for session-boundary runs, `monitorFeed`
always (ADR 50058-monitor-feed-wire D1), `sideChat` always (SS4.5.13),
`damagedRange` always (ADR 60914 D2), `earlierHistory` always (ADR
71910 D3), `systemNotice` when produced outside a turn (tdd SS4.5.23).

url.description:
`webSearch`: the page URL, verbatim — present iff
`action == "openPage"` or `"findInPage"` (tdd SS4.5.15,
**experimental**).

usage.description:
`subagent`: **transitive** observed usage — the child and its own
descendants; updated in place, absent until first observation; never
folded into `session/tokenUsage.cumulative` (tdd SS4.6.5).

visibleOutput.description:
`toolCall`/`userShell`: bounded transcript-visible result text
(budget per tdd SS4.5.4); streams via `item/delta` field `"output"`.

wakeSourceDescriptions.description:
`agentMessage`: the Monitor source descriptions for the wake
turn's first answer (ADR 62265 D1, #62265) — stripped,
bounded, one entry per arming drain in drain order. Absent
(or empty) means untagged: the row renders the ordinary
untagged shape. The client scrubs per part before joining.

workId.description:
`toolCall`: the task's registered Work ID, verbatim
(`work.v2.managed_bash.sha256.…`); present only when the task
registered a ManagedBash id, absent otherwise (tdd SS4.5.5,
ADR 50041 D20). Stable from day one: no `x-msp-stability`
marker. The host serves it at the later of the task terminal
and the inbox admission (D21); absence keeps the client's v1
derivation.

workflowRunId.description:
`subagent`/`workflow`: the owning durable workflow run id (opaque
string — not a UUID family).

ItemCompletedParams.description:
`item/completed` params (tdd SS4.3): the item reached its terminal state
— the authoritative final object. Always cites a durable `sourceRange`
(tdd SS4.2). Clients MUST accept `item/completed` for an `itemId` they
never saw `item/started` for (single-shot kinds; after a gap fill; tdd
SS4.4.1).

item.description: The full item at its terminal revision.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

ItemDeltaParams.description:
`item/delta` params (tdd SS4.3.1): a UTF-8-safe streaming append to an
open item's field. Ephemeral-sourced by definition: this params object
has **no** `sourceRange` member at all (spec 14653 INV-009 — the schema
enforces the exemption). Deltas never bump `revision`.

delta.description:
The appended text; concatenation of a field path's deltas in cursor
order equals that field's value on `item/completed` unless the
surface saturated (spec 14653 INV-005).

field.description:
Dotted field path the append targets (`"summary.0"`, `"output"`,
...); absent means `"text"` (tdd SS4.3.1).

itemId.description: The open item being appended to.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

ItemKind.description:
The eleven v1 item kinds (tdd SS4.5.2–4.5.13) plus post-v1 kinds
(tdd SS4.5.14+). Open: a new kind is additive evolution, and clients
MUST render unknown kinds generically (tdd SS4.10).

oneOf.description:
A skill-read notice (tdd SS4.5.14; ADR 33401 D4/D7/D10):
single-shot only, status `completed` — a notice has no progress.
Experimental: stripped per-connection for unopted callers (SS1.5.1).

ItemReadOutputEncoding.description:
The `item/readOutput` content encoding (tdd SS4.7.4). Closed: text media
is ALWAYS `utf8` and binary media `base64`; a third value would change
the client's decode contract.

ItemReadOutputParams.description:
`item/readOutput` params: byte-ranged fetch of stored full output that the
view truncated, via the item's `outputRef`. Read-only; works on loaded and
unloaded sessions; no lease.

itemId.description: The item whose stored output is fetched.

lengthBytes.description:
STORED bytes requested; default and max 6 MiB (tdd SS4.7.4). A value
above the max is served at the max.

offsetBytes.description:
STORED-byte offset to start from; 0 when omitted. STORED bytes are a
property of the output, not of a transport (tdd SS4.7.4).

outputRef.description:
The `outputRef.id` from the item (never the `uri`; the uri is
display/provenance).

sessionId.description: The session the item belongs to.

byteLen.description:
STORED bytes served in THIS response (not the output's total; that is
`outputRef.byteLen` on the item). The next page's `offsetBytes` is
`offsetBytes + byteLen` — short-serving and advancing are separate,
so paging never skips or double-reads a byte (tdd SS4.7.4).

eof.description: `true` when this range reached the end of the stored output.

offsetBytes.description: The STORED-byte offset this response actually served from.

ItemStartedParams.description:
`item/started` params (tdd SS4.3): a new item opened on the transcript.
`sourceRange` is absent when the item opens on an ephemeral record (the
delta-streamed kinds); the item's authoritative open is re-stated by its
durable-sourced `item/completed` (tdd SS4.2).

sourceRange.description:
The durable records this event folded from; absent on an
ephemeral-sourced open (spec 14653 INV-009).

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

ItemStatus.description:
Item status (tdd SS4.4.1). Open; terminal = anything other than
`"inProgress"`, and unknown values are terminal-unknown, rendered
generically.

ItemUpdatedParams.description:
`item/updated` params (tdd SS4.4.2): an open item changed non-terminally
in a way deltas cannot express — the full item re-emitted at a higher
revision (apply rule: replace iff higher).

item.description: The full item at a higher revision.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

descriptor.description:
Create-only storage descriptor of a child session's journal (ADR
61595 D5): sent on its first admission ever; a later open omits it or
repeats it unchanged. Absent, never null, for a root session.

journalError.description: In-band journal error (one-to-one with the journal taxonomy).

sourceGeneration.description:
The store's generation of this source (D117 amendment, ADR 61595
D3.3), maintained by the store and starting at 1. The store raises
it each time it discards and recreates this source, and at no other
time; it never lowers it. The host sends it back on every
`journal/commitBatch`; the store refuses a commit from another
generation with the conditions error.

JournalAnchor.description: A journal anchor: bare per-source ordinals plus the qualified binding.

throughWriteId.description:
The meaning of the batch at the qualified cut (ADR 61595 D3.2). The
field's name and shape are decided with the S4 anchors; until then it
keeps its name and carries the meaning.

JournalBatchStamp.description:
The multi-request batch stamp (ADR 61595 D3): present on every
record of a logical transaction the host split across several
`commitBatch` requests, absent otherwise. `end` is the closing
row's sequence; readers hold stamped rows until it arrives. The
client store carries the stamp opaquely and returns it unchanged.

JournalChildKind.description:
The kind of a child session that has its own journal (ADR 26387-SRL
D22). Reminder children stay local and never have one.

closesJournal.description:
The transaction carries a child run's terminal record, so the store
marks the child's journal closed once the transaction qualifies (ADR
61595 D5). The host decides it from its own records; the store never
parses them. A later qualified commit (a successor attempt, an owed
abort) reopens the journal. Absent, never false, otherwise, so other
commits' bytes are unchanged.

meaning.description:
The batch's meaning (ADR 26387-SRL D14.1, ADR 61595 D3.2): the
`sha256-v1:<hex>` digest of its own records. The store's idempotency
key is source plus meaning. Every batch is named by its own records,
each part of a split transaction included, the last one too.

sourceGeneration.description:
The source generation the store answered in
`journal/admissionContext` (D117 amendment, ADR 61595 D3.3). The
store raises its generation each time it discards and recreates
the source, so a commit prepared before that carries the old one;
the store refuses a mismatch with the conditions error before any
other check, exact retries included.

ids.description:
Record ids this request admitted, in sequence order. Every request,
a split transaction's closing request included, is named by the
digest of its own records and reports its own ids; the store tracks
no runs, and the client adapter assembles the run (ADR 61595 D3.2,
owner D120).

JournalCommitConditions.description: Writer fencing conditions carried by admission and rechecked at commit.

owner.description: The writer term number issued at admission.

predecessor.description:
ADR 26387-SRL D12.1: the journal's current tail (bare per-source
ordinal), required on every commit; an empty journal names 0.

state.description: ADR 26387-SRL D12.1: carried but never checked; absent when unset.

JournalConfirmThroughParams.description:
`journal/confirmThrough` notification params (client -> host report).
Carries the client's `confirmedThrough` position; a watermark hint,
never evidence. No response (notifications are never answered).

JournalLimits.description: Negotiated journal limits (values not yet fixed).

meaning.description: The meaning of the batch to observe (ADR 61595 D3.2).

ids.description:
Record ids admitted under the observed meaning, in sequence order:
that request's own ids, a split transaction's closing request
included; the client adapter assembles the run (ADR 61595 D3.2,
owner D120).

JournalPageRecord.description: One paged record with its source-supplied original bytes, when present.

JournalReceipt.description: A client-issued qualified receipt (bookkeeping, not an authority token).

meaning.description: The meaning of the batch this receipt qualifies (ADR 61595 D3.2).

JournalRecord.description:
One record inside a batch/page (owner D115): the session record's v1
envelope fields, flat and camelCase (no envelope `schema_version`), with
the domain payload embedded as a JSON value under its own payload type.

batch.description:
Split-transaction stamp (ADR 61595 D3). Absent — never null —
on single-request transactions, so their bytes are unchanged.

durability.description: `durable` or `ephemeral`, as the record's v1 envelope carries it.

recordType.description:
The record's type (`event`, `status`, ...), as its v1 envelope
carries it.

sequence.description:
The record's journal position (D37): a journal is
single-session, so every record is on the session's own stream
(`streamKind == "session"`, `streamId == ` the session id) and
its sequence is its position in the journal, strictly +1 from
the previous record, starting at 1. A store refuses a
commitBatch with a non-session stream, a foreign session id,
or a non-contiguous sequence with the conditions-style
journal error and appends nothing; the session is poisoned and
reopens from the ledger. 0 is never a sequence.

JournalSessionDescriptor.description:
How a child session's journal was created and which journal it links to
(ADR 61595 D5). Storage-level only: the store creates and links the
child's journal from it and never parses records.

createdAt.description:
The time recorded in the parent's record that started the child (never
a live clock read, so a repeat after restore is identical), in the unit
of `JournalRecord.recordedAt`.

parentSessionId.description: The parent's session id; for a fork or side chat, the source session.

LastTurn.description:
The last `turn/completed` the session-view fold applied, restated on
`session/resume` and `session/read` so a reopened session can report a
failed last turn (tdd SS2.5.2, ADR 36635 D2/D3).

error.description:
Copied when the `turn/completed` carried it: runtime `failed`
terminals do, host-death `failed` terminals do not (ADR 36635 D2).

reason.description:
Copied when the `turn/completed` carried it; a synthesized host-death
`failed` terminal carries only this (`crash`, `crash_inferred`, or
`incomplete`). Free display text: clients never branch on it.

terminal.description: The turn's terminal (tdd SS4.5.1; open enum).

turnId.description:
The turn's id, as on its `turn/completed`; clients deduplicate a
live `turn/completed` against this member by it (ADR 36635 D2).

LaunchContext.description:
`InitializeResult.launchContext` (ADR 86936 D1): the two launcher
variables of the serve process's environment, verbatim, read once at
process start; one value for every connection and session the process
hosts. Each member is `null` when its variable is unset.

LimitKind.description: Quota limit kinds (tdd SS4.5.1, ADR 50047 D2): open for evolution.

LimitsAboveMaxAxis.description:
One too-wide axis in a `-32028 limitsAboveMax` refusal (tdd SS2.9; ADR
39851-ss1-10 D2 Q2): every too-wide axis is listed, never the first only.
`requested`/`max` carry the axis's own JSON values.

LimitsAxisValue.description:
One axis value in a limits refusal: a boolean on the four boolean axes,
the mode string on `sandboxNetwork` (tdd SS2.9). **Closed**: exactly the
two shapes, never another — named in ADR 51992 D10's closed
untagged-union list (`CLOSED_WITHOUT_MARKER`), since the untagged shape
carries no schema marker. Untagged so the wire
carries the bare JSON value; untagged also keeps the §4.3 shape the
schema builder requires (a bare `serde_json::Value` renders no type and
is rejected).

LimitsNetworkMode.description:
The sandbox-network axis values (spec 14404 FR-002 grammar). **Closed**:
a client selects one of the three serve spellings and can never construct
another; the socket promise is same-version, so the result use needs no
unknown arm (E2; the experimental tier carries no cross-version promise).

LogFlushDegradedCause.description:
Which log a degraded turn-end flush lost or misses (ADR 78845 D1).
**Open**: a newer host may add a word; a client keeps it and draws the
counts row. `session` is the current conversation's log, `other` another
conversation's on the same host; `Deleted` and `Replaced` are lost,
`Missing` may come back.

LogGapParams.description:
`log/gap` notification params (tdd SS6.5): the raw-altitude shape of the
shared SS1.7 gap contract, per subscription. The client MUST fill
`(after, next)` with `log/page` before treating its fold as current,
except for an `overFrame` gap (see [`LogGapReason`]).

after.description: The last position the subscription delivered or named.

next.description:
`replayAnchorLost`: the first position it will deliver. `overFrame`:
the skipped record itself when its position is readable, else the
next record it delivers (ADR 58371 D8).

reason.description: Why the gap opened; absent from hosts that predate it (#58371).

LogGapReason.description:
`log/gap` `reason` (ADR 58371 D8): only a `replayAnchorLost` gap is
refillable through `log/page`; an `overFrame` gap is a known hole on that
connection, its hole `(after, next]` less `next` when it is delivered.
**Open**: a server-produced vocabulary.

from.description: Read strictly after this position; omitted reads from the origin.

limit.description: 1–1000; the server may serve fewer records.

LogPageResult.description:
`log/page` result (tdd SS6.4): a contiguous, gap-free run of the stored
rows in sequence order, each as written to disk (#65544): envelopes and
stored `omitted_live_only` markers alike. Clients that read record
contents must skip markers.

nextCursor.description:
The cursor after the last returned row (a marker's cursor is its
`position`), or null when `records` is empty. Page to the tail by
looping `from = nextCursor.after`.

records.description:
The served rows, in sequence order: a [`RawLogRecordEnvelope`], or at
a position stored as a marker line the retained-gap marker (spec 018
shape verbatim). A member carrying `retained_marker` is the marker,
any other member is the envelope; free-form for the same reason as
`LogRecordParams::record`. A marker counts toward `limit`.

sessionId.description:
The session whose home is listed: a root lists its whole tree, a
child id lists that child's subtree.

files.description: The root file first, then every child file at any depth.

LogPhysicalLineParams.description:
`log/physicalLine` notification params (ADR 58371 D6): one chunk of one
complete physical line; the chunks concatenated plus `\n` are the line.

chunk.description: This chunk's place in the line.

data.description: The chunk's UTF-8 text, split on a character boundary.

endOffset.description: The offset of the line's terminating newline (exclusive end).

LogPhysicalResetParams.description:
`log/physicalReset` notification params (ADR 58371 D7): the terminal
notification of a subscription that met a fault.

at.description: The last line boundary fully delivered.

reason.description: Why it ended.

after.description: Where delivery starts; required (`{0, 1}` is the file's start).

chunkBytes.description:
An upper bound on one chunk's raw UTF-8 bytes (default 1 MiB); at
least 4, the widest character.

sessionId.description: The session whose file is followed: a root or a child session.

relPath.description: The followed file, relative to the sessions root.

subscriptionId.description: Connection-scoped id carried on every notification it produces.

tailOffset.description:
The file's size at subscribe time. The consumer has caught up once
its cursor's `byteOffset` (the subscribed `after`, then
`endOffset + 1` after each line) is at or past it; a half-written
last line counts once its `\n` is written. A size, not a cursor, so
the acknowledgement never counts lines (Constitution VII).

LogRecordParams.description:
`log/record` notification params (tdd SS6.5): one per position, in
sequence order, for each active subscription on the record's stream.

record.description:
The record: a [`RawLogRecordEnvelope`] — or, at an evicted or
omitted ephemeral position stored as a marker line (served on replay
and on a durable stream's follow; a live stream such as
`session.live` never pushes one, #65544),
the retained-gap marker (spec 018 shape verbatim: the
`retained_marker` discriminator `omitted_live_only`, the envelope
schema version, `stream`, `position`, and the `omitted_record`
kind-shape; tdd SS6.5). Free-form because the
envelope-or-marker union is unkeyable by the node-keyed gate walk
(spec 14652 Clarifications 2026-09-28, #44121): a member carrying
`retained_marker` is the marker, any other member is the envelope
(the `RawLogRecordEnvelope` schema root publishes its shape).

LogStreamEntry.description:
One enumerated stream (tdd SS6.3). RPC-level members are camelCase —
only the record envelope itself is storage-verbatim.

prunedThrough.description: The pruned prefix's end, when a retention pass removed one.

tail.description: The last appended position, or null for an empty stream.

sessionId.description: The session whose streams to enumerate.

streams.description: Every stream of the session, with tails and earliest positions.

after.description:
Resume position: the server replays `(after, tail]` before any live
record. Omitted tails from now (back-fill with `log/page` for
history).

sessionId.description: The owning session (must be loaded on this host).

subscriptionId.description:
Connection-scoped id, carried on every notification the subscription
produces.

tail.description:
The stream tail at subscribe time: the client is live once
`sequence` passes it.

LogUnsubscribeResult.description:
`log/unsubscribe` result (tdd SS6.5): the empty object. Idempotent —
detaching an unknown or already-detached id succeeds.

McpForfeitReason.description:
The forfeit trigger behind a `mcpServer/forfeited` notice (ADR 74052
D2). Open (server-produced, the #22785 E2 rule). One value per trigger:
the deadline, the framing desync, the notification-write timeout, and
the cancel-write failure — the rmcp and legacy deadline forfeits share
`operationTimeout`. The four-value shape corrects ADR 74052 D2's
two-value wire shape; the ADR-text correction rides the follow-up
docs PR.

McpOAuthLoginOutcome.description:
The login flow's terminal vocabulary (ADR D4). Open
(server-produced result vocabulary, the #22785 enum-openness rule).

McpOAuthRevocation.description:
The upstream revocation attempt's outcome (ADR D3). Open
(server-produced result vocabulary, the #22785 enum-openness rule).

McpRuntimeInventoryRow.description: State is open: clients preserve and label an unfamiliar word as unknown.

McpServerForfeitedParams.description:
`mcpServer/forfeited` params (ADR 74052 D2): one notice per forfeit,
fire-and-forget — serve waits for no reply. The holder's strategy
decides what happens next, through `mcpServer/reconnect` (D3) or never.

consecutiveFailedReconnects.description:
Consecutive failed reconnects for this server in this session: 0
on the first forfeit; the crash-loop signal for the holder's
strategy. Reset on a successful reconnect (ADR D4). `u8`: the
counter rides A's `McpForfeitEvent` field of the same type.

reason.description: The trigger that forfeited the connection.

sessionId.description: The loaded session whose server forfeited.

McpServerListOAuth.description:
A list row's OAuth state: the D5 presence-first ladder (ADR D5). Open
(server-produced, the #22785 E2 rule). `loggedIn` always implies a
wire-cleanable credential.

McpServerListParams.description:
`mcpServer/list` params (ADR D5): without `sessionId`, the host-global
set; with it, that loaded session's effective set (host rows plus its
frozen ADR-32760 additions).

sessionId.description:
The loaded session whose effective set to project; absent for the
host-global set.

McpServerListResult.description:
`mcpServer/list` result (ADR D5): the projected rows, catalog-join
order for host rows, session additions after.

McpServerListRow.description:
One `mcpServer/list` row (ADR D5): config-and-auth facts only. All
three member enums are open (server-produced, the #22785 E2 rule).

name.description:
The server name the verbs resolve (host rows) or the session-scoped
name (session rows, never verb-resolvable).

McpServerListSource.description:
A list row's source (ADR D5). Open (server-produced, the #22785 E2
rule).

McpServerListTransport.description:
A list row's transport spelling (ADR D5). Open (server-produced, the
#22785 E2 rule); `unknown` marks a disabled row's unresolvable
transport — such rows list, never vanish.

server.description: The binding whose pending flow the cancel targets.

cancelled.description: True iff a pending flow for that binding existed and was cancelled.

message.description:
A display string on `denied`/`expired`/`failed` only — never key
material, flow artifacts, or the authorization URL.

McpServerOAuthLoginParams.description: `mcpServer/oauthLogin` params (ADR D3): the one required member.

server.description: A server name in the host-global population (settings + plugin).

McpServerOAuthLoginResult.description:
`mcpServer/oauthLogin` result (ADR D3): the flow the ack STARTED — never
its outcome. Reaches only the requesting connection.

authorizationUrl.description: The provider authorization URL the client opens in a browser.

server.description: The binding whose stored credential the logout deletes.

McpServerOAuthLogoutResult.description:
`mcpServer/oauthLogout` result (ADR D3): the upstream revocation is best
effort, and the local credential deletion is authoritative.

removed.description: True iff a stored credential was deleted.

revocation.description: What the upstream revocation attempt did.

McpServerReadDisplayCatalogParams.description: Read only the addressed loaded session's retained MCP identity catalog.

McpServerReadDisplayCatalogResult.description: Null means no retained catalog yet; an empty array is a present empty catalog.

McpServerReadInventoryParams.description: The addressed loaded runtime; this query performs no MCP discovery.

McpServerReadInventoryResult.description: A runtime snapshot with only privacy-safe diagnostic copy (ADR 79187 D2).

McpServerReconnectParams.description:
`mcpServer/reconnect` params (ADR 74052 D3): the holder's explicit
instruction to reconnect one server. Serve reconnects only when told.

sessionId.description: The loaded session whose server reconnects.

McpServerReconnectResult.description:
`mcpServer/reconnect` result (ADR 74052 D3): whether a restart
happened. Idempotent: an already-live server answers
`reconnected: false` without restarting.

reconnected.description: True iff a restart happened; false iff the server was already up.

McpToolDisplayMetadata.description: The session-pinned tool ID and its validated raw route, including reserved routes.

MediaUploadParams.description:
`media/upload` params (tdd SS3.33, ADR 45443 D5): one chunk of a
client-minted upload. All members required.

chunkBase64.description: This chunk's bytes; each call's frame stays in the SS1.1 budget.

commandId.description:
One per call. While the host runs, replaying it with the same params
returns the recorded receipt, and reusing it with different params is
refused. After a host restart, start over under a new `uploadId`.

sessionId.description: The session owning the video store.

totalBytes.description: The assembled byte count; must equal the bytes the chunks deliver.

uploadId.description: The client-minted upload id (UUIDv7), sent on every chunk.

MediaUploadResult.description:
`media/upload` result (tdd SS3.33): echoes the client-minted id, on
every chunk and replay.

uploadId.description: The receipt the turn part references.

MessageAttachment.description:
`userMessage` image attachment metadata (tdd SS4.5.2): metadata only —
the durable bytes live in the log and are reachable on the raw altitude.

attachmentId.description:
This attachment's name, `<itemId>/<n>` — the item's id plus this
entry's 1-based position in its `attachments` array (tdd SS4.5.2,
D-071, ADR 42850; #42850). Name only: no link form and no byte read
by id (#42648).

Set by the server on every attachment entry it emits, and identical
on live, paging, snapshot and rebuild paths (tdd SS4.5.2). Optional
in the schema so older servers stay valid; clients compare and store
the whole string and MUST NOT parse it (ADR 42850).

type.description:
Attachment type, `"image"` in v1 (free string: attachment vocabulary
grows additively with the runtime's intake surface).

MessagePhase.description:
`agentMessage.messagePhase` (tdd SS4.5.3, #50254): the phase the model
declared, never inferred from position. Set on every completed item, and
on `item/started` when the host knows the phase (#77396): absent or
unknown there means not yet known, and the completed value wins. A failed
item carries none, and its missing value does not read as `"finalAnswer"`.
Open: a client reads an absent or unknown value on a completed item as
`"finalAnswer"` and still decodes the item. Not a turn-done signal;
`turn/completed` is.

MissingInputAssets.description:
What a cold load does when a retained input image file is missing or
corrupt (ADR 78319 D1). Omitted means `fail`.

MissingPredecessor.description:
`missingPredecessor` on `session/resume` (ADR 77295 D1): this resume's own
load found the session's committed `SessionStarted` naming a predecessor
whose retained log is not in the session store.

sessionId.description:
The missing predecessor's session id, the one the gate-off notice
names.

ModelCancelParams.description:
`model/cancel` params (tdd SS3.40, FR-90352-4): the `commandId` of the
call to cancel, not a retry id of its own.

ModelCancelResult.description:
`model/cancel` result (ADR 90352 D6): always empty, for a call in flight
and for an id no call holds alike; `model/completed` reports the outcome.

ModelCatalogEntry.description:
One visible catalog row (tdd SS3.10). Catalog rows marked hidden never
reach the wire, so a client cannot select one.

contextLimit.description: Context limit; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

cost.description: Cost block; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

defaultReasoningEffort.description:
The row's catalog default. Optional only for decoding older hosts; a
present value is never null and is always a member of `variants`.
Absent under `"unknown"` (ADR 33400 D2).

description.description: Description; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

isActive.description:
Marks the session's effective model when `sessionId` was supplied. May
be false for every row — a client MUST NOT assume exactly one.

isDefault.description: Marks the catalog's default row. May be false for every row.

outputLimit.description: Output limit; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

profileId.description: Provider profile; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

reasoningEffortVariants.description:
Described selectable tiers, a same-order subset of `variants`.
Optional only for decoding older hosts; a present value is never
null. Absent under `"unknown"` (ADR 33400 D2).

releaseDate.description: Release date; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

variants.description:
Complete ordered selectable efforts. Optional only for decoding older
hosts; a present value is never null. Current hosts always send it.

ModelCatalogSource.description:
Where a model catalog came from (tdd SS3.10). **Open**: an unrecognized
value is an unknown source, not an error.

ModelChangeSource.description: What drove a model selection (tdd SS4.6.1). Open.

ModelCompleteOutcome.description:
How a `model/complete` call settled. **Open**: a server-produced result
vocabulary, so a word a newer host adds decodes to `Unknown` (tdd SS1.9).

ModelCompleteParams.description:
`model/complete` params (tdd SS3.40, FR-90352-1): the retry id, 1 to 32
messages (the first and the last `user`), an optional system text and
the output bound. No session and no model: the host picks the model
(ADR 90352 D3). The host answers an unknown field with `invalidParams`;
the type itself accepts it.

commandId.description: The client-minted UUIDv7 retry id (required, SS3.1.1).

maxTokens.description: The most tokens the model may write.

messages.description: What the model answers, oldest first.

system.description: The system text, when the caller sends one.

ModelCompleteResult.description:
`model/complete` result (tdd SS3.40): admission only — the ack is never
the completion.

ModelCompleteRole.description:
Who said one `model/complete` message. **Closed**: a client-produced
input the host validates, so an unknown role is `invalidParams`.

ModelCompleteStopReason.description:
Why the model stopped on a `completed` call (FR-90352-2). **Open**: a
server-produced word, so a word a newer host adds decodes to `Unknown`
(tdd SS1.9).

ModelCompleteUsage.description:
The provider's token counts for one completed call (ADR 90352 D5): real
counts only, never an estimate.

inputTokens.description: Input tokens, as the provider counted them.

outputTokens.description: Output tokens, as the provider counted them.

ModelCompletedParams.description:
`model/completed` params (tdd SS3.40, FR-90352-2). `text`, `stopReason`, `modelId` and
`usage` ride `completed` (`usage` only when the provider reported counts);
`message` rides `failed`; `cancelled` and `timedOut` carry neither. The
struct marks the conditional members optional; the SS prose pins the
per-outcome rule. `text` is untrusted model output.

commandId.description: The request's id — the correlation key.

message.description: Why the call failed, in words (on `failed`).

modelId.description: The `model/list` id of the model that ran (on `completed`).

usage.description: The provider's counts (on `completed`, when it reported them).

ModelCost.description:
Per-1M-token catalog cost, carried **verbatim** for display and never
rounded or re-formatted by the host (tdd SS3.10). Cost arithmetic stays
client-local view math.

currency.description: Currency; nullable — today's catalogs are USD.

ModelDescribedReasoningEffort.description:
One described reasoning-effort tier of a `model/list` row (tdd SS3.10,
ADR 33400 D2): a selectable tier plus the catalog's display string for
it when declared.

description.description:
The catalog's per-tier display string; absent when the catalog
declared none. Optional only for decoding; a present value is never
null.

tier.description: The tier, in the closed D-024 vocabulary.

ModelIdRefusal.description:
`modelIdRefusal` on `session/resume` (ADR 24046 D7): the host refused
this resume's `modelId`, so the session opened on its recorded model.

reason.description: The host's reason, display text a client shows as is.

ModelListParams.description:
`model/list` params (tdd SS3.10): the discovery half of the model-picker
gesture. **A query, not a command** — no `commandId`, no durable intake
record, no view event.

sessionId.description:
When present, the row matching that session's effective model is
flagged `isActive`. When absent, no row is active — a client may list
before it has a session (tdd SS3.10).

ModelListResult.description:
`model/list` result (tdd SS3.10). A snapshot at call time: v1 has no
catalog subscription. `models` MAY be empty — a build shipped with no
bundled models is a supported configuration.

source.description:
Where the catalog came from — how a client tells a live provider
catalog from a test fake and labels it honestly.

ModelReasoningEffortVariants.description: A complete ordered effort set, or an explicit unknown capability.

ModelSelection.description: A model selection (tdd SS3.8). Empty strings are normalized to absent.

profileId.description:
Provider profile. Omitted and explicit `null` both mean "no profile"
(#23468).

ModelVisibleContent.description:
Rich content the model saw beyond text (tdd SS4.5.5,
`ModelVisibleToolContent`): metadata only — fetch bytes via
`item/readOutput` when an `outputRef` exists.

sourceToolName.description: The tool that produced the content.

type.description:
Content type, `"image"` in v1 (free string, grows with the durable
vocabulary).

MonitorInboxItemAdmittedParams.description:
`monitor/inboxItemAdmitted` params (tdd SS4.5.18): one monitor
inbox admission — the fold keys gate-off consumes.

displayBody.description:
The producer-recorded pre-augmentation content; absent on
pre-#24686 records.

eventKind.description:
Monitor event kind, snake_case, open vocabulary — clients
ignore unknown kinds.

lineIndex.description: Line order key; absent when the event has no line.

queuedAt.description: Admission stamp (RFC3339); consumed by the pending sort.

showLines.description: Whether the event carries displayable lines.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

taskId.description: The owning monitor task id (per-task set key).

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

MonitorInboxItemDrainedParams.description:
`monitor/inboxItemDrained` params (tdd SS4.5.18): one monitor inbox
drain — a consumption marker with its recorded stamp.

deliveryVisible.description:
False is a local claim-only recall: no delivery row or recovery
consequence, but the drain still stamps the awaiting verdict.

drainTargetRunStream.description:
The draining run stream (`StreamRef`), absent means the current
draining run.

drainedAt.description:
The drain record's recorded stamp (RFC3339), the drain-side
operand of drain-vs-void latest-wins.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

MonitorInboxItemVoidedParams.description:
`monitor/inboxItemVoided` params (tdd SS4.5.18): one wake-missed
void — count-only, no transcript row (spec 9627 D15).

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

voidedAt.description:
The anomaly's recorded stamp (RFC3339), the void-side operand
of drain-vs-void latest-wins.

MonitorInboxSnapshotEntry.description:
One snapshot `monitorInbox` entry (tdd SS4.9.1, FR-56492-7 as amended by
#76729): a retained admission in the `monitor/inboxItemAdmitted` shape,
envelope-stripped, plus the newest drain and void stamps folded for it.
The entry is still awaiting delivery when `drainedAt` is absent, or when
`voidedAt` is strictly newer than it (FR-56492-3).

displayBody.description:
The producer-recorded pre-augmentation content; absent on
pre-#24686 records.

drainedAt.description: The newest drain stamp (RFC3339); absent while never drained.

eventKind.description: Monitor event kind, snake_case, open vocabulary.

lineIndex.description: Line order key; absent when the event has no line.

showLines.description: Whether the event carries displayable lines.

taskId.description: The owning monitor task id (per-task set key).

voidedAt.description: The newest wake-missed void stamp (RFC3339); absent while never voided.

NoticeOrigin.description:
`systemNotice`: the producing family, so a client routes a notice without
parsing its text (tdd SS4.5.23). Open. The v1 vocabulary is the Monitor
notice and the three system-chrome producers (ADR 42729 D1) plus the
hook-run producer (ADR 75121 D2) and the paused-Workflow checkpoint
producer (ADR 39490 D5); absent means the server named no
origin, and a client never infers one.

NoticeSeverity.description:
`systemNotice`: the notice's level (tdd SS4.5.23). Open; an unknown value
is an unknown-but-present level, rendered generically (SS4.10).

NoticeSubject.description:
`systemNotice`: the durable thing the notice is about (tdd SS4.5.23).
`id` is required whenever the object is present; `label` is the
producer's sanitized, already-capped display value, omitted when it is
empty, never `""`.

id.description:
The subject's durable identity: for `monitor`, the monitor's task id
(its `toolCall` `itemId`); for `hook`, the hook run's item id (the
opening `HookRunStarted` record's event id, SS4.5.11).

label.description: The subject's bounded display label (the `hookRun.label` shape).

Notification.description:
A notification frame, either direction (SS1.2 §2.2). No `id`; a
notification is never answered.

params.description: Method-specific parameters; omitted entirely when empty.

OutputRef.description:
Stored-output reference (tdd SS4.5.5): the camelCased fold of the durable
`ToolOutputRef`. The fetch path is `item/readOutput` (#208).

availability.description: Whether the bytes are servable (tdd SS4.5.5).

kind.description:
The stored output's kind, verbatim durable vocabulary (e.g.
`"tool_output"`; snake_case per the SS1.6 casing exemption).

OutputRefAvailability.description:
Whether a stored output's bytes are servable (tdd SS4.5.5). Open —
durable runtime vocabulary may grow additively.

PatchSummary.description:
Server-authored edit-family diff summary (tdd SS4.5.5, #33025):
`files` counts the stored patch document's file entries; `added` and
`removed` are the total `+`/`-` prefixed LINE counts summed over the
stored patch's hunks across all files — line counts, never hunk or byte
counts. Rides the `toolCall` item beside `patchRef`; the body is fetched
via `item/readOutput` with `patchRef.id`.

added.description: Total `+`-prefixed line count across all files' hunks.

files.description: File entries in the stored patch document.

removed.description: Total `-`-prefixed line count across all files' hunks.

PeerInboxItemDrainedParams.description:
`peer/inboxItemDrained` params (#72279 cause 2): one peer inbox
drain — a consumption marker with its recorded stamp. The member
set mirrors `MonitorInboxItemDrainedParams` (tdd SS4.5.18) so the
client fold is the monitor arm's twin.

deliveryVisible.description:
False is a local claim-only recall: no delivery row or recovery
consequence, but the drain still stamps the awaiting verdict.

drainTargetRunStream.description:
The draining run stream (`StreamRef`), absent means the current
draining run.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

PeerListParams.description:
`peer/list` params (FR-45445-1): the viewing session, excluded from its
own rows. Unknown fields are `invalidParams` (the goal-family strict
exception shape, spec 14408).

sessionId.description:
The viewing session (required; need not be loaded — reads never
take the lease).

PeerListResult.description:
`peer/list` result (FR-45445-1): no pagination, no cursor — one
snapshot carries the whole plane.

peers.description:
One row per live registry entry except the viewer, ordered by
session id ascending (required).

PeerMessage.description:
`peerMessage`: the four facts the consumed card renders (ADR 72708
D2, tdd SS4.5.24). The fold reads them from the drained inbox
record's delivery snapshot; `senderLabel` already ran the
gate-off label rule host-side, so the client renders it verbatim.
Stable from day one (the `scheduledFire` precedent): no
`x-msp-stability` marker.

body.description:
The message text verbatim — never cut (an over-budget event
answers the typed `pageEventTooLarge` arm).

remote.description:
True for mailbox/remote senders, false for local session
senders.

senderLabel.description:
The peer label gate-off shows: the sender name when the
durable record names one, else the sender id shortened as
gate-off shortens it, else `unknown session` — and `remote
session` verbatim for a remote sender.

senderSessionId.description:
The local sender's session id; absent for remote senders and
when the record names none.

PeerMessageDisplayContext.description:
The connector presentation facts of a forwarded message (ADR 25011 D22),
every member optional.

relayContext.description: The relay's own context block, opaque and read-only.

PeerMessageOwner.description: Which coordinator lane owns the forwarded conversation.

PeerMessageOwnerState.description:
Whether the owning lane is alive. **Open** (#22785 E2): a newer host's
state decodes to `Unknown`.

PeerOriginCodeIdentity.description:
How the sender generation's code identity was established. **Open**
(#22785 E2): a newer host's identity decodes to `Unknown`.

PeerOriginPlatform.description:
The sender generation's platform. **Open** (#22785 E2): a newer host's
platform decodes to `Unknown`.

PeerRow.description:
One `peer/list` row (FR-45445-1): local rows only — no
`discoverySource`, no mailbox rows, no `host`.

canReceive.description:
Whether the row's eligibility is message-capable (required): false
exactly for launch-excluded rows.

lastSeenAgeMs.description: Milliseconds since the row was last observed (required).

sessionName.description:
The spec-923 authority join (required, nullable): null when that
authority is absent, incompatible, or unavailable.

PeerSettlement.description:
One settlement: an optional admission decision plus the outcome of each
message the settlement released, in order (FR-45445-16).

decision.description: The admission decision this settlement records, when it records one.

outcomes.description:
One entry per released message, in release order (required); a
`null` entry keeps the ordinal of a message with nothing to show.

PeerSettlementDecision.description: The admission decision a settlement records.

origin.description: The sender origin the timeline coalesces by (required).

senderLabel.description: The sender label snapshotted at settlement (required).

PeerSettlementDecisionKind.description:
A connected-sender decision kind, spelled with the decision ids that
`admission/resolved` uses for the same decisions (ADR 45445 D6). **Open**:
a server-produced result vocabulary (#22785 E2), so a word this build does
not know decodes to `Unknown` instead of failing the page.

PeerSettlementDeliveryPolicy.description:
A released message's delivery policy, spelled with the durable
snake_case words. **Open** (#22785 E2): a newer host's policy
decodes to `Unknown`.

PeerSettlementOrigin.description:
The sender origin a settlement belongs to. Rows with the same
authenticated generation coalesce on the timeline; a non-coalescing origin
never coalesces with another. A flat object rather than a tagged union so
the experimental gate can key every member.

generation.description:
The authenticated generation; present exactly when `kind` is
`authenticated`.

value.description:
The non-coalescing key; present exactly when `kind` is
`nonCoalescing`.

PeerSettlementOriginKind.description:
Which kind of sender origin a settlement belongs to. **Closed**: the
receiver timeline keys on exactly these two.

PeerSettlementOutcome.description:
What one released message shows on the receiver timeline. A flat object
rather than a tagged union so the experimental gate can key every member.

decisionId.description: The releasing decision; present exactly when `kind` is `allow_once`.

deliveryPolicy.description:
The release's delivery policy (#71573 FR-71573-1); absent on
pre-A1 records and unparseable ones.

displayContext.description:
The connector's presentation facts on a forwarded message; only on
`normal`.

settledAtUs.description:
The settlement instant in Unix microseconds; present exactly when
`kind` is `normal`.

wakePolicy.description:
The release's wake policy (#71573 FR-71573-1); absent on
pre-A1 records and unparseable ones.

PeerSettlementOutcomeKind.description:
Which kind of released message an outcome shows. **Closed**: the receiver
timeline renders exactly these two.

PeerSettlementPosition.description:
A settlement's position in the receiving session's log: the settlement
record's id and its stream sequence. Clients treat it as an opaque cursor
that orders by `sequence`.

sequence.description: The record's stream sequence, at least 1 (required).

PeerSettlementWakePolicy.description:
A released message's wake policy, spelled with the durable
snake_case words. **Open** (#22785 E2): a newer host's policy
decodes to `Unknown`.

PeerSettlementsChangedParams.description:
`peer/settlementsChanged` params (FR-45445-17): a non-view notification
to the receiving session's connections. `revision` grows by at least one
per committed settlement batch; it is a wake hint, not a cursor, and the
client reads `peer/settlements` from its own cursor.

revision.description: The settlement revision after the change (required).

after.description:
The position of the last settlement the client folded; absent reads
from the first settlement.

limit.description:
Page size, 1 to [`PEER_SETTLEMENTS_PAGE_MAX`]; absent means the
maximum.

sessionId.description: The receiving session (required; loaded on this host).

PeerSettlementsResult.description: `peer/settlements` result (FR-45445-16): one page, ascending by position.

through.description:
The last settlement in this page, or `requestedAfter` when the page
is empty (required, nullable). The next read passes it as `after`.

PeerStatus.description:
`peer/list` row `status` (FR-45445-1): the `LocalSessionStatus`
vocabulary. **Open**: a server-produced result vocabulary (#22785 E2).

PendingApprovalPointer.description:
A pending approval in the snapshot: the SS2.5.2 pointer shape plus the
gated `itemId` when one exists (tdd SS4.9.1).

itemId.description: The parked item, when one exists.

viewCursor.description: The cursor the approval opened at.

PendingRequestKind.description:
The `pendingRequests` discriminator (tdd SS2.5.2). Open enum, v1 values
`approval` and `userInput`.

PendingRequestPointer.description:
A late-joiner pointer at an unsettled server-initiated request
(tdd SS2.5.2, SS2.2.1). The full payloads arrive as re-issued
server-to-client requests right after a `session/resume` response
(tdd SS5.6); `session/read` never re-issues them (tdd SS2.5.5).

The protocol defines two kind-discriminated entry shapes (`{kind:
"approval", approvalId, viewCursor}` / `{kind: "userInput", userInputId,
viewCursor}`). This type is one flat object with both ids optional, as for
`ApprovalSubject` and `TurnInputPart`, because the v1 model names no
object-variant union; the serialized JSON is the same, but the published
schema also accepts `{"kind":"approval","userInputId":…}` and an entry
carrying no id at all. Unlike `TurnInputPart.type`, `kind` here is an OPEN
enum.

viewCursor.description: The cursor the request opened at.

PendingUserInputPointer.description: A pending user-input prompt in the snapshot (tdd SS4.9.1, SS5.10).

itemId.description: The parked item, when one exists.

viewCursor.description: The cursor the prompt opened at.

PermissionApprovalAxis.description:
A profile's effective approval axis (amendment 44483 FR-44483-2).
**Open**: the vocabulary can widen.

PermissionAxes.description:
A committed profile's effective four axis values (amendment 44483
FR-44483-2): the resolved filesystem, network, approval, and reviewer
the YOLO predicate reads. The reviewer member reuses
`ReviewerAuthority`, so its spelling never drifts from the served
`reviewerAuthority`.

filesystem.description: The resolved filesystem mode in the picker's wording.

network.description: The resolved local-command network mode in the picker's wording.

PermissionFilesystemAxis.description:
A profile's effective filesystem axis (amendment 44483 FR-44483-2).
**Open**: the vocabulary can widen.

PermissionNetworkAxis.description:
A profile's effective local-command network axis (amendment 44483
FR-44483-2). **Open**: the vocabulary can widen.

PermissionProfileApplyOutcome.description:
Whether a profile change did anything (amendment 42624 FR-42624-2). The
accepted arm spells `completed` exactly as `session/setApprovalMode`
(SS5.12, `ApprovalModeApplyOutcome::Completed`) so the shared member never
forks spellings. Apply failures are `commandRejected`.

PermissionProfileListParams.description:
`permissionProfile/list` params (amendment 42624 FR-42624-3): read the
native profile catalog. A read-only method — takes no lease, grants
nothing.

sessionId.description:
When present, availability is answered in that loaded session's
context; when absent, in host context (a fresh-session answer).

PermissionProfileListResult.description:
`permissionProfile/list` result (amendment 42624 FR-42624-3): one row per
host-defined profile in the native catalog.

profiles.description: One row per profile the native catalog defines.

PermissionProfileRow.description:
One native-catalog profile row (amendment 42624 FR-42624-3). The
availability facts are the same ones the native picker marks disallowed
profiles unavailable with (ADR 42197 D2) — never an authority statement.

available.description: The native catalog's availability answer for this profile.

description.description:
The profile's native description, served verbatim so every client
matches the TUI picker on the same host (FR-44483-1; the built-in
strings are ADR 11237's ratified copy). OMITTED (never `""`/`null`)
when the native row carries none — a description-less row displays
its id alone.

unavailableReasons.description:
Why the profile is unavailable — non-empty exactly when `available` is
false, OMITTED (never `[]`/`null`) when `available` is true.

PermissionProfileSource.description:
How a permission profile took effect (amendment 42624 FR-42624-5, the
change event's `source` vocabulary). **Open**. Transliterates the native
`PermissionTransitionCauseV1` (agent-session-permissions `snapshot_digest`)
cause-for-cause; the wire never adds a cause the native enum lacks. Only the
UserCommand-kind causes (`livePicker`, `resumeCli`) and the ManagedRefresh
causes are reachable on the change event post-epoch-one; the Initialization
causes are enumerated for fidelity but ride only the epoch-one/derivation
facts this event does not fold.

PermissionProfileUnavailableReason.description:
Why a profile is unavailable (amendment 42624 FR-42624-3). Open camelCase
vocabulary; a client that meets an unknown entry treats the profile as
simply unavailable. The fold of `PermissionSurfaceDisabledReasonV1`;
`SessionBlocked(_)` has no wire fold (its only native bearer is the
synthetic disabled row `permissionProfile/list` does not serve).

PhysicalChunk.description: One chunk's place within its line.

count.description: How many chunks the line has.

PhysicalCursor.description:
A physical line boundary in one file plus the client's ordinal label
(ADR 58371 D5): `byteOffset` is zero or follows a `\n`; `nextOrdinal` is
echoed and never checked against the file, but must be in `1..=2^63`.

byteOffset.description: The boundary's byte offset in the file.

nextOrdinal.description:
The ordinal the next line carries: the client's label, echoed and
never checked against the file; must be in `1..=2^63`.

PhysicalFileEntry.description: One log file in a session home.

relPath.description: The file, relative to the sessions root.

sessionId.description: The session the file belongs to (the root or a child).

sizeBytes.description: The file's current size in bytes.

PlatformFamily.description:
The server runtime's platform family; may differ from the client's. Closed:
the protocol fixes the value set, so widening it is a deliberate,
gate-visible protocol change rather than a silent addition (a later
`Closed`→`Open` flip is itself additive).

PlatformOs.description:
The server's operating system (SS1.4.1). Closed, for the same reason as
[`PlatformFamily`].

enabled.description:
The record's own install switch; non-enabled rows are included
as `false`, never dropped.

source.description: The installed record's source provenance (ADR 33398 D7 item 3).

PluginChangedParams.description:
`plugin/changed` params (tdd SS3.29.5): an install landed; clients
re-issue `plugin/list` (plus `hook/list` and `skill/list`).

PluginDataChangedParams.description:
`pluginData/changed`: the changed records, or `reset` with no records
when the reader must read again (FR-008).

PluginDataFilter.description:
A read's filter (FR-006). `turnId` and `tool` apply to tool calls only,
`outcome` to turns only, and `projects` takes no filter.

since.description: RFC 3339; matches a `startedAt` at or after it.

PluginDataProject.description:
A picked project folder. Times are RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds, and
`null` when the host does not know them (FR-002).

name.description: The folder's last part.

root.description: The picked folder, in canonical form (FR-018).

PluginDataReadParams.description: `pluginData/read`. `roots` are the picked folders, absolute paths.

PluginDataReadResult.description: `nextCursor` holds no ID, and is `null` when no older record matches.

PluginDataRecords.description:
The records of one resource, newest first, tagged with the resource's
name: `{"resource": "turns", "turns": [...]}` (FR-001). A union in the MSP
bundle needs a member with a fixed string in each arm (spec 206 data-model
4.2.1), and a tool call record holds every turn field, so the tag also
makes decoding unambiguous.

PluginDataSubscribeParams.description:
`pluginData/subscribe`: a read's scope and filter, with no cursor and no
limit (FR-008).

subscription.description: Opaque, and unique on its connection.

PluginDataToolCall.description: A tool call's name and timing, never its input or output.

itemId.description:
The `toolCall` item's `itemId`, never the provider's `callId`, which
two calls can share. With `sessionId` it keys the record, because a
fork or rewind child repeats its source's IDs.

PluginDataToolOutcome.description: A tool call's outcome; `running` until it ends.

PluginDataTurn.description:
A turn's place, times and outcome. With `sessionId`, `turnId` keys the
record, because a fork or rewind child repeats its source's IDs.

root.description: The longest picked folder that holds the session's folder.

PluginDataTurnOutcome.description: A turn's outcome; `running` until it ends.

PluginDataUnsubscribeResult.description:
`pluginData/unsubscribe` answers `{}`, also for a subscription that has
already ended.

path.description:
The host folder to install from; absolute recommended, relative
resolves against the host working directory.

name.description: The plugin name within the store.

PluginInstallParams.description:
`plugin/install` params (tdd SS3.29.1). Per-session params plus a
client-generated `commandId` (UUIDv7) with the uniform SS3.1.1
idempotency contract.

sessionId.description: The target session; its workspace resolves project scope.

PluginInstallResult.description:
`plugin/install` result (tdd SS3.29.1): the SS3.1.2 ack envelope plus
the installed receipt.

warning.description:
The installer's advisory text when the install succeeded with a
caveat; absent otherwise.

PluginInstallScope.description:
The `plugin/install` local-path scope (tdd SS3.29.1). Closed: an
unknown scope is `-32602 invalidParams`.

PluginInstallTarget.description:
The one structured install target (tdd SS3.29.1): a flat object with
two optional arms, exactly one present — the `TurnInputPart`
convention, since the v1 schema model names no object-variant union.
Both arms or neither is `-32602 invalidParams`.

localPath.description: The local-path arm: install from a host folder.

marketplace.description: The marketplace arm: install a named plugin from a store.

PluginListParams.description:
`plugin/list` params (tdd SS3.26.2). Per-session params; rows are the
installed plugin records.

PluginListResult.description:
`plugin/list` result (tdd SS3.26.2): one row per installed plugin
record; the spec promises the set, not an order.

PluginMarketplaceAddParams.description:
`plugin/marketplaceAdd` params (tdd SS3.29.2). Per-session params plus
a client-generated `commandId` (UUIDv7).

name.description: The marketplace name to configure.

source.description:
The app's source vocabulary: `owner/repo`, a git URL, a `file://`
URL, or a local path.

PluginMarketplaceChange.description:
What happened to a marketplace (tdd SS3.29.6). Closed: an unknown
change is a contract violation, never tolerated.

PluginMarketplaceChangedParams.description:
`plugin/marketplaceChanged` params (tdd SS3.29.6): a marketplace was
added, updated, or removed.

name.description: The marketplace name.

pluginCount.description:
The stored record's plugin count; omitted on `removed`, never
fabricated.

skippedCount.description:
The stored record's skipped count; omitted on `removed`, never
fabricated.

PluginMarketplaceRecordResult.description:
The stored marketplace record both add and update answer (tdd
SS3.29.2, SS3.29.3): the SS3.1.2 ack envelope plus the record.

name.description: The configured marketplace name.

pluginCount.description: The plugins the store now offers.

skipped.description:
Entries the store could not offer, with the reason each was
skipped; empty when nothing was skipped.

PluginMarketplaceRemoveParams.description:
`plugin/marketplaceRemove` params (tdd SS3.29.4). Per-session params
plus a client-generated `commandId` (UUIDv7).

name.description: The marketplace name to remove.

PluginMarketplaceRemoveResult.description:
`plugin/marketplaceRemove` result (tdd SS3.29.4): the SS3.1.2 ack
envelope plus the removed name.

name.description: The removed marketplace name.

reason.description: Why it was skipped.

PluginMarketplaceSourceShape.description: The normalized stored marketplace source (tdd SS3.29.2).

PluginMarketplaceUpdateParams.description:
`plugin/marketplaceUpdate` params (tdd SS3.29.3). Per-session params
plus a client-generated `commandId` (UUIDv7).

name.description: The marketplace name to refresh.

PluginSource.description:
A plugin row's source provenance (tdd SS3.26.2, ADR 33398 D7 item 3):
camelCase of `PluginSourceProvenance`. Open (server-produced result
vocabulary, the #22785 enum-openness rule): a future provenance is
additive.

PolicyRuleOrigin.description: Where a session policy rule came from (tdd SS5.16, ADR 47712 D5/D6).

ProbeDegradedReason.description:
Why a workspace status probe produced no fresh reading (#35065 item 2).

**Open**: a new reason is additive evolution, and a client MUST render an
unknown value as an unknown-but-present reason rather than rejecting the
row.

ProjectionBasis.description: The fold basis of a projection snapshot (tdd SS6.6).

experimental.description: Whether the projection itself is experimental.

name.description:
The wire name (`task-status`, `muse-run-output`,
`session-policy-overlay`).

ProjectionReadResult.description:
`projection/read` result (tdd SS6.6): one snapshot plus the fold basis
that makes it reconcilable against the log.

basis.description: The exact log frontier this snapshot reflects.

state.description:
The projection's own serialization (per-projection schema,
experimental).

PrunedSubagent.description:
One child session pruned below a checkpoint boundary (tdd SS2.5.5,
ADR 71910 D8): the restored row's key, text, and stoppability —
never pruned transcript.

label.description:
The served display label (the spawn's role, agent path as
fallback); absent when the spawn records carry neither.

sessionId.description:
The child session id — the trace key for `session/read` on the
child, exactly as for a live child row.

QueuedInput.description:
One input still queued for delivery to a session (tdd SS2.5.5,
ADR 63254-queued-inputs-on-read D2): the full message body plus its
log record sequence, the delivery-order and re-read dedupe key, plus
the run-log record id clients join served entries against
record-seeded rows by.

sequence.description:
The queued record's log sequence: delivery order, and the key
clients deduplicate re-reads by.

sourceCommandId.description:
The `SubagentInput` record's model-authored command id: the key
wire-twin rows join by in either order (the twin reads the same
string from the verbatim wire args). Absent for root own-queue
members, which are never `SubagentInput`.

sourceRunRecordId.description:
The run-log record id the served mirror was taken from: the key
clients join served entries against record-seeded rows by, so an
already-rendered input never mints a second row under diverged
sequences. Absent when the host's record carries no mirror
