metadata (a pre-feature host), which falls back to sequence-key
dedup only.

text.description: The full message body, verbatim (never truncated, never a summary).

QuotaDetail.description:
Typed quota-exhaustion detail (tdd SS4.5.1, ADR 50047 D2): the limit
kind plus the provider's reset instant.

limitKind.description: Which quota was exhausted (open enum; unknown values fall back).

resetsAtMs.description: Epoch milliseconds at which the provider says usage resets.

RawLogCursor.description:
A stream-scoped cursor: "this stream consumed through this position"
(tdd SS6.2). Cursors never cross streams (`wrongStream`, SS6.9).

RawLogRecordEnvelope.description:
One raw record on the wire (tdd SS6.2): the stability boundary. Members
are storage-verbatim snake_case, exactly as the host writes them to its
JSONL segments (the SS1.6 casing exemption).

causation_id.description: The causing record's id, when known.

id.description: Globally unique event id; the idempotency anchor.

recorded_at.description: Microseconds since the Unix epoch, assigned by the writer.

sequence.description: Position within `stream`: dense, strictly increasing from 1.

ReasoningEffort.description:
The reasoning-effort tier sampled at submission (tdd SS3.2, SS3.3). The
**same closed tier vocabulary** on both the fresh-turn and steer lanes,
spelled identically; invalid tiers are invalid params. `none` is a tier of
the vocabulary (ask for no reasoning), not a way to say "unset".

ReasoningEffortChangeSource.description:
What drove a reasoning-effort default change (tdd SS4.6.9). Open; v1's
only producer is `user` (an accepted `session/setReasoningEffort`).

ReasoningEffortState.description:
The snapshot's standing session-default reasoning effort (tdd SS4.9.1,
ADR 31255 D1): the fold of the latest completed
`runtime.reasoning_effort_reconfigure` fact — the same pair
`session/reasoningEffortChanged` carries.

reasoningEffort.description:
The standing default tier — the closed SS3.2 vocabulary, spelled
identically to `turn/start.reasoningEffort`.

source.description: Which actor class set the default.

RecapCancelParams.description:
`recap/cancel` params (tdd SS3.28.5): the session plus the cancel's
own retry id. No target — one in-flight slot per session makes the
target unambiguous.

commandId.description: The cancel's own retry id (required, SS3.1.1).

sessionId.description: The session whose in-flight recap to cancel (required).

RecapCancelResult.description:
`recap/cancel` result (tdd SS3.28.5): admission only. In flight →
the recap settles `cancelled`; idle → accepted no-op.

RecapCompletedParams.description:
`recap/completed` params (tdd SS3.28.2): the settlement, delivered
to the requesting connection outside the view stream — no
`viewCursor`, no `sourceRange`. `text` is required on `completed`
(plus optional `title`, untrusted model output — clients MUST
sanitize per spec 442 INV-015); `reason` is required on `failed`;
neither rides `cancelled`/`timedOut`. The struct marks the
conditional members optional; the SS prose pins the per-outcome
rule, the `turn/completed` usage/error convention.

commandId.description: The request's id — the correlation key.

reason.description: Why the side-call failed (on `failed`).

title.description: The model-produced short title (on `completed`, when produced).

RecapFailureReason.description:
`recap/completed` failure reason (tdd SS3.28.2/SS3.28.8): post-ack
failures fold to the single initial value. **Open**: later splits
stay additive (#22785 E2).

RecapOutcome.description:
`recap/completed` outcome: the terminal vocabulary, in camelCase. **Open**:
a server-produced result vocabulary.

RecapRequestParams.description:
`recap/request` params (tdd SS3.28.1): the session plus the
client-minted UUIDv7 retry id. No other param; unknown fields are
`invalidParams`.

RecapRequestResult.description:
`recap/request` result (tdd SS3.28.1): admission only — the ack is
never the recap.

RecordPosition.description:
One end of a [`SourceRange`]: a record's event id and its sequence number
within the stream (tdd SS4.2).

sequence.description: The record's sequence number within its stream.

RecoveryEffectiveSource.description: Proven effective-choice provenance, independently of input presence.

RecoveryMode.description: A requested construction choice; omission is distinct from explicit OFF.

RecoveryObservation.description: One coherent producer snapshot; all members are required and non-null.

RecoveryObservedMode.description: A proven mode or unknown; future strings cannot establish OFF.

RecoveryQualification.description: This construction's assessment, never an operation acceptance receipt.

ReplayHint.description:
The D26 first-tree-transition hint verdict plus anchor (tdd
SS4.5.21, ADR 56496 D3): `rowKinds` is the open lowercase row-kind
vocabulary the client formats through its shared kind-noun
constructor; `afterItemId` is the item id after whose rows the
hint renders. Both members always ride when the object does.

id.description: Client-chosen id, unique among that client's in-flight requests.

params.description: Method-specific parameters; omitted entirely when empty, never `null`.

RequestId.description:
A request id (SS1.3): client-chosen string or integer. `1` and `"1"` do
not compare equal; each direction owns its own id space.

RequestReceipt.description:
The SS5.3.3 presentation receipt — the client's response to a
server-initiated request (`approval/request`, `userInput/request`).

The response acknowledges presentation only ("a surface showed or will
show this"): it changes no state, the server uses it for diagnostics
alone, and the decision/answer travels as a command (`approval/decide`,
`userInput/answer`). An error response or a dropped connection means this
connection could not present the request; the approval or prompt stays
pending and the request is re-issued on the next subscribe (SS5.6).
There is no dismiss-without-deciding on the wire.

RestartReceipt.description:
One `restartReceipts` entry on `session/resume` (ADR 71350-B2 D1): a
copy of the runtime `ManualCompactionReceipt` in its own serde
vocabulary — display event ids, `StreamRef` streams, and the runtime's
snake-case status/reason/outcome words.

candidateId.description: The summary candidate id, when the receipt carries one.

commandId.description: The compaction command's event id, display form.

reason.description: The runtime reason word, when the receipt carries one.

sessionStream.description: The session stream the command was accepted on.

targetStream.description: The compaction target run; absent on target-less receipts.

RetractOutcome.description:
A `turn/retracted` settlement outcome (tdd SS4.5.1, ADR 50074 D1).
Open enum (D-033): decode is tolerant — a value outside the list reads
as `Accepted` (the event's historical meaning — pre-feature hosts emit
it only for accepted retracts), never fails. The bundle keeps
enumerating the known values for codegen and docs.

ReviewerAuthority.description:
A profile's selected reviewer authority (amendment 42624 FR-42624-3/4).
**Open**: the reviewer vocabulary can widen.

RewindAttempt.description:
One passively observed Keep/Stop attempt (D7). The nested
`source_instance_id` binds the attempt's actor, so a reload cannot
conflate it with the current top-level instance.

attachCommandId.description: The attaching command's id once attached. Required-nullable.

backgroundTasks.description: Keep or Stop (D7's closed request choice, echoed here).

commandId.description: The attempt's command id (called `attemptId` by read/attach).

error.description:
A stored command failure, preserving its kind, code and registered
data; reading it never recodes it as a refusal. Required-nullable.

phase.description:
The coordination phase. Open: an unknown value cannot authorize
submission or attachment.

sourceInstanceId.description: The actor bound to this attempt.

stopFailure.description: The known owner failure, when present. Required-nullable.

stopProgress.description:
Authoritative selection progress; null before authoritative
selection and on Keep. Required-nullable.

RewindAvailability.description:
The rewind availability summary (D7): a flat object, not a tagged
union (the `PendingRequestPointer` precedent — v1 names no
object-variant union). Producer obligation: `reason` is present
exactly when `state` is `unavailable`; the `session/rewindRead`
serve layer (T-50280-078) refuses a mispaired summary as
invalidParams.

reason.description:
Why the summary is unavailable. Present exactly when `state` is
`unavailable`; an open string.

RewindPointsParams.description:
`session/rewindPoints` params (D7): one page of full current rewind
candidates. The source must already be loaded. Command-ID-free.

cursor.description:
The paging cursor; absent/null begins evaluation. Nullable
(D7's null-tolerant set): plain `Option` spells the default by
omission and accepts explicit null identically.

limit.description:
Page size, 1-200, default 50; may short-serve under budgets.
Omit-only: explicit null is invalidParams.

sessionId.description: The source session under existing identity resolution.

RewindReadInputParams.description:
`session/rewindReadInput` params (D7): a bounded read of the selected
input's exact current text refill. Command-ID-free.

cursor.description:
The text-read cursor; absent/null reconstructs, validates and
freezes one text read. Nullable (D7's null-tolerant set).

lengthBytes.description:
Chunk length cap in bytes; defaults/caps at the `item/readOutput`
6 MiB read bound and must be positive. Omit-only.

sessionId.description: The source session under existing identity resolution.

sourceInstanceId.description:
The loaded source actor this read binds to; a stale instance
refuses `notFound`/`rewind_source_changed`.

RewindReadParams.description:
`session/rewindRead` params (D7): cheap availability/source state,
optional work census, and passive attempt observation. Command-ID-free.

attemptId.description:
The attempt to observe, a UUIDv7 (ADR 50280 D7); absent reads no attempt (`attempt: null`).
Omit-only: explicit null is invalidParams.

includeWork.description:
Advisory logical-owner census for confirmation/refresh. Omitted
means false and returns `backgroundWork: null`. Omit-only.

sessionId.description: The source session under existing identity resolution.

RewindReadResult.description:
`session/rewindRead` result (D7). A successful read establishes
whole-family support; missing required full-mode fields is unsupported.

attempt.description:
The observed attempt, or null when no `attemptId` was read.
Required-nullable.

automaticContinuation.description: Whether this feature holds the current source.

backgroundWork.description:
The advisory work census, or null when not requested.
Required-nullable.

sourceInstanceId.description:
The current actor's opaque instance, or null when no authoritative
current actor identity exists. Required-nullable.

RulesChangedSource.description: One refreshed rules source (tdd SS3.37, ADR 70236 D1).

displayPath.description:
The tag's unescaped display path, relative or `~/`-prefixed. No
host-local absolute path crosses the wire; clients resolve those
against their own known sources.

scope.description:
The tag's scope word (`user` / `project` today). A plain string —
not an enum — so an unknown word skips one source instead of
dropping the whole push (the receiving fold skips per source;
the parser itself passes the raw word through).

RunningElsewhere.description:
The `runningElsewhere` member of a `Session` (ADR 69811 D5): another live
process on this machine runs the session.

origin.description:
Which kind of process runs it, taken only from facts the host already
reads; omitted when unknown, never guessed.

RunningElsewhereOrigin.description:
Which kind of process runs a session elsewhere on this machine (ADR
69811 D5).

**Open**: a new origin is additive evolution, and a client MUST treat an
unknown value as an unknown-but-present origin rather than rejecting the
row.

RuntimeWorktree.description:
The runtime-owned git worktree a child session runs in, mirrored from the
`subagent.worktree.*` records on its parent's log (tdd SS2.5.5, ADR
50042-child-worktree-on-read D2). The four enums are open: clients
treat an unknown value as unknown.

baseCommit.description: The commit the worktree was created from.

cleanupDiagnostic.description:
The cleanup outcome's recorded diagnostic, verbatim (#70088); absent
when the outcome records none.

cleanupPolicy.description: How the worktree is cleaned up.

cleanupReason.description:
Why cleanup kept the worktree or failed, as the cleanup outcome
recorded it (#70088); absent when the outcome records no reason.

headCommit.description: The head commit the active lease recorded.

parentDirtyExcluded.description:
True exactly when the parent's uncommitted changes were recorded as
excluded from the checkout.

worktreeRoot.description:
The recorded worktree root, verbatim (recorded history; serving it
never probes the path).

RuntimeWorktreeCleanupPolicy.description:
How a session's worktree is cleaned up. The set is open, so newer hosts
may send other values.

RuntimeWorktreeCleanupReason.description:
Why a session's worktree cleanup kept the worktree or failed. The set is
open, so newer hosts may send other values.

RuntimeWorktreeCleanupState.description:
Where a session's worktree cleanup stands. The set is open, so newer
hosts may send other values.

RuntimeWorktreeOwnership.description:
Who owns a session's worktree. The set is open, so newer hosts may send
other values.

SandboxAvailability.description:
Whether this host can enforce the sandbox (ADR
50064-startup-report-sandbox-availability D2/D4). A property of the host
process, probed once at construction and identical for every session and
every connection it serves — never requested, granted, or negotiated,
which is why it is not a capability. Open: a future enforcement posture
arrives as a new value, read by older clients as unknown.

SandboxUnavailableReason.description:
Why sandbox enforcement is impossible on this host. Sent only when
[`SandboxAvailability`] is `unavailable`; a client MUST NOT infer a
reason when none is sent. Open: a future reason arrives as a new
value, read by older clients as unknown.

ScheduleListParams.description:
`schedule/list` params (tdd SS3.38). Per-session over the read
session's retained schedule; no load required.

ScheduleListResult.description:
`schedule/list` result (tdd SS3.38): one row per live schedule, in
server store order.

ScheduleRow.description:
One live schedule (tdd SS3.38; ADR 45446 D2). Membership is the
liveness verdict — no `status` member rides the row.

cronExpr.description: The verbatim cron expression, opaque on the wire.

jobId.description:
The schedule's job id (`CronJobRow.id`). Unique within one
response.

recurring.description: The spec 3062 FR-014 one-shot versus recurring split.

SchemaInfo.description:
The `schema` pair in [`InitializeResult`] (SS1.4.1, SS1.5.3). `version`
is the wire **envelope** schema version — distinct from the session-view
`schemaVersion`, the raw-log `schema_version`, and the 0.x/1.0 stability
posture, which is not on the wire at all (INV-006a).

fingerprint.description:
`sha256:<64 lower hex>` content hash of this server binary's
stable-surface bundle (INV-003). A mismatch is a warning condition,
not an error (SS1.4.1).

version.description:
Envelope schema version; `1` in v1, expected to stay `1` for a long
time (SS1.4.1).

ServeIsIdleResult.description:
The `serve/isIdle` result: whether serve can shut down for now,
and the earliest armed fire time.

idle.description: True iff no session has running work.

nextWakeAt.description:
The earliest armed fire time in epoch milliseconds (a runtime
scheduled delivery or an active cron/reminder job), or `None` when
nothing is armed.

name.description: Server name.

Session.description:
The session object every lifecycle method returns or lists (tdd SS2.4).

Additive-optional evolution applies: clients must ignore unknown fields.

activeTurnId.description:
The `turnId` of the current foreground turn when `status` is
`running`, and `null` when the session is idle (tdd SS2.4).

**Required-nullable.** Every served `Session` carries the member: `null`
when the session is idle or not loaded, the turn id when it is running.
An optional-absent shape would publish it as plain `string` and reject
every idle `Session` frame the host sends.

approvalMode.description:
The folded effective approval mode. **Additive-optional**: a Session
object that omits it means the host has not folded a mode, which is
why the index-derived `session/list` entry may legitimately omit it
(tdd SS2.4, SS5.12).

attention.description:
Attention flags (tdd SS2.4, ADR 31983 D3). **Additive-optional**,
present only when at least one flag is set; absence is a
NON-assertion (nothing pending, or the loaded session's pending
source declined to answer). Loaded sessions only: a `notLoaded` row
omits it even while its durable pending set is non-empty.

branch.description:
Derived workspace branch (tdd SS2.14.1, #27598) — the index's last
derived value; the live-change signal stays `session/branchChanged`
(SS4.6.4). **Additive-optional**, omitted when underivable.

createdAt.description:
RFC3339. For a fork this is the fork session id's UUIDv7 mint instant
(tdd SS2.4).

createdByClient.description:
The handshake `ClientInfo` recorded when the session was opened
(FR-003), echoed verbatim — provenance, never an interpretation, and
never a visibility gate (INV-005). **Additive-optional**; absence has
four indistinguishable causes (INV-004): an in-process open; a
pre-#23124 record; a half stamp where only one of name/version was
recorded (FM-005) and `ClientInfo` requires both; and a session with
no admitting handshake of its own — a fork child or a subagent —
which never carries a stamp to begin with.

currentLimits.description:
This session's effective limits (tdd SS1.10; ADR 39851-ss1-10 D1;
ADR 59770 D4): the clamp output — each axis the session chose clamps
its durable stored choice (the clamp input) to the live ceiling, and
an axis it never chose reads the daemon default: untrusted unless the
daemon serves trusted by default, and the daemon's own posture on the
sandbox axes, except that a resume over a sandbox-off posture can keep
a recorded sandbox on, and a `session/fork` or `session/sideChat` child
starts with its parent's recorded shell, write and sandbox limits and
its parent's chosen trust, clamped to the live ceiling (ADR 69811 D2
choice (c) as amended by #70458 and #83669). A sandbox kept on this way
over a sandbox-off posture runs its recorded network, or `restricted`
when none was recorded, while #63513 is open (tdd SS1.10). These are the limits the session
runs with.
**Experimental, same-user socket only** (`Session.currentLimits`;
stripped per-connection for unopted callers). Loaded sessions only
(`notLoaded` rows and hosts with no limits regime omit it) — absent
is never fabricated.

driveHolder.description:
The handshake `ClientInfo` of the connection that currently holds
this session's drive grant (spec 39851 INV-001; spec 42713
FR-58706-1, ADR 58706 D2), served on `session/read` only, as `name`
and `version` (the handshake's
display `title` is never served, the `createdByClient` rule).
**Additive-optional, loaded-only, live**:
present exactly when a live connection holds the grant and its
handshake is known; absent on `notLoaded` rows, once the holder's
connection drops (its orphaned turn included), and for a holder with
no handshake stamp. Provenance only
(INV-005): whether a client may drive is answered by
`session/resume` / `turn/start` (`sessionInUse`), never by this
member (FR-58706-4).

externalWait.description:
The live host-declared external wait for this session, served on
`session/read` only.
**Additive-optional, loaded-only, live**: present exactly while
a declaration is live for the loaded session; absent on
`notLoaded` rows, once the declaration is cleared, once the next
user input clears it, and after a restart or resume, which lose
it. Presence is the declaration — a client must never infer one
from any other member.

firstUserPrompt.description:
Derived first-user-prompt preview (tdd SS2.14.1, #27598).
**Additive-optional**, omitted when underivable.

forkedFrom.description: `null` for root sessions; fork provenance otherwise (tdd SS2.4).

generatedName.description:
The served generated short title (tdd SS2.4/SS2.14.1, #50048; ADR
50048-generated-name D1). **Additive-optional**, **fold-only**: the
snapshot fold derives the latest retained generated pair's short
title from the log; `session/list` rows never carry it. Omitted when
no pair was ever published — absent reads as unpublished, never
fabricated, never inferred from the name text. `name` stays the
canonical name it always was.

itemCount.description:
The published head's ordinal (kt-dvw5): the head reference's own
ordinal — the count of head slots in its sequence, including any
reserved ones — as of the probe that served this row. A sizing
hint for a first `view/page`, so the Console can size its page
without folding the log. **Additive-optional**, present only on
metadata reads (`session/read` with `excludeItems`), where the
client has no items to count; full reads carry the items
themselves and omit it. Absent when no head is published (unknown),
never fabricated. May lag a live log: the head is a snapshot, and
appends after its publication are not counted.

kind.description:
What kind of session this is (spec 42713 FR-001, ADR 42713 D1/D4).
**Open enum**, v1 values `"root"` and `"subagent"`; a client treats an
unknown value as an unknown-but-present kind and renders it, never
rejecting the row. **Additive-optional**: absence asserts nothing —
the host could not determine the home shape (FM-001), or the value is
not yet available to serve (FM-003).

lastActivityAt.description:
Content-activity recency, RFC3339 (tdd SS2.4, ADR 31983 D5).
**Additive-optional**: omitted when no content record exists. Never
advanced by lifecycle bookkeeping (the resume marker, re-stamps) or
a fork's copied seed-replay records, and never precedes `createdAt`.

logBytes.description:
The durable log's byte length at read time (kt-dvw5): the size hint
paired with `itemCount`, so the Console can size its first page
without folding the log. **Additive-optional**, present only on
metadata reads (`session/read` with `excludeItems`); full reads omit
it. Absent when the log's length is not known (unknown), never
fabricated. A live log grows after the read; the value is a snapshot.

modelId.description: The winning metadata fold's model; `null` when that record omits it.

name.description:
The durable allocated session name (tdd SS2.4/SS2.14.1, #27598;
ADR 27598 D2/D4). **Additive-optional**: present when the serving path
holds an allocated name, omitted otherwise — absent is never
fabricated. Authoritative and renameable via `session/rename`.

nameOrigin.description:
How the served `name` was set (tdd SS2.4/SS2.14.1, #50048; ADR 50048
D1/D2). **Additive-optional**, **fold-only**: the snapshot fold
(`session/read`, the resume/start/fork-ack snapshot) derives and
carries it from the log; `session/list` rows never carry it. Absent —
and any value the client does not recognize — reads as unknown,
never fabricated.

parentSessionId.description:
The containing session's id when `kind` is `"subagent"` (FR-002,
INV-002) — the id of the TOP-LEVEL session whose home holds this
child, which is **not necessarily the session that spawned it**:
native-child homes are physical siblings under the outer session's
`subagent/` directory, so a subagent spawned by another subagent
resolves to the outer session, not to its spawner. A client building
a tree from this field gets one level, not a chain.
Flat rather than nested: there is exactly one fact to
carry, unlike `forkedFrom`'s structured `ForkProvenance`.
**Additive-optional**; a root carries none.

path.description:
Absolute path of the session's durable log; non-nullable. Under the
ephemeral session profile it is the **empty string**, meaning "no
durable log exists" (tdd SS2.13.2) — the one value a client must not
hand to a filesystem call.

permissionState.description:
The folded effective permission state (amendment 42624
FR-42624-4). **Additive-optional**: a `"notLoaded"` row omits it
(no live evidence, matching the `attention` precedent) and an
older host omits it everywhere; absent is unknown, never active
(INV-42624-1). `approvalMode` stays the effective-mode answer;
this never restates it.

probeDegradedReason.description:
Why the workspace status probe produced no fresh reading (#35065
item 2) — the index's last derived value, like `branch`, so the TUI
can show WHY status is unavailable instead of a generic unavailable.
**Additive-optional**, omitted when the latest probed observation
carries no reason or none exists. **Open enum**: a client treats an
unknown-but-present reason and renders it, never rejecting the row.

providerId.description: The winning metadata fold's provider; `null` when that record omits it.

quiescent.description:
Whether the answering host holds no live work for this loaded
session (#77011): the held predicate the host's idle unload and
upgrade drain use, over the pending answer `attention` reads. `true`
when it finds no run in flight or finishing its post-run work, no
owned background task or live background process, no background
completion waiting to wake the session, no session-name or
goal-recovery work, and no pending approval, user-input or admission
request; `false` while any is held or a read cannot prove it absent.
**Experimental** (`Session.quiescent`; stripped per-connection for
unopted callers) and **loaded-only**: carried by `session/read`,
`session/list` rows, the `session/resume` result and the
`session/listChanged` frames built from the same row. A run or a
pending request starting pushes a frame carrying `false`; other held
work (session-name maintenance, a leave in progress) shows on the
next read. A session served `false` is rechecked about once a second
and its frame is pushed once it reads `true`. Absent on `notLoaded`
rows, on a host whose `session_quiescent_witness` gate is off, and
for a session with no live pending-request source: absence asserts
nothing.

resumedByClient.description:
The handshake `ClientInfo` of the connection whose wire
`session/resume` most recently loaded this session (spec 42713
FR-58706-2, ADR 58706 D2): stamped on the durable `session.resumed`
marker, folded into the session index, and served from that column by
every carrier; while the session is loaded, the stamp the loading
resume wrote replaces the column on every carrier (the ack,
`session/read`, `session/list`, `session/listChanged`), and after the
next fold the column serves it. **Additive-optional** and
**provenance only** (INV-005); a resume with no admitting handshake
(TUI, exec) stamps nothing, a warm attach to an already-loaded session
writes no marker, and a half stamp serves nothing (FR-003a), so
absence asserts nothing. `createdByClient` never follows a resume
(FR-58706-3).

runningElsewhere.description:
That another live process on this machine runs this session, and
which kind of process when the host can tell (ADR 69811 D5).
**Experimental** (`Session.runningElsewhere`; stripped per-connection
for unopted callers), on `session/list` rows and the
`session/listChanged` frames built from the same row. No frame is
pushed when only this member changes; a client sees the change on its
next `session/list` or on a frame sent for another reason. Present exactly
when the answering host does not hold the session loaded and another
live process on this machine does (it holds the session's writer
lease, or a live local session registry record names the session),
so only `notLoaded` rows carry it. Absence asserts only that the host
saw no other holder when it built the row. Provenance only: whether a
client may drive is answered by `session/resume` / `turn/start`
(`sessionInUse`), never by this member.

sideFrom.description:
`null` for root sessions and forks; side provenance otherwise (tdd
SS2.4/SS2.5.7; ADR 45435 D2). A session carries at most one of
`forkedFrom` and `sideFrom`.

spawnedBy.description:
The session that opened this one (spec 42713 FR-69621-6, ADR 69621
D4), recorded once in this session's creation record and served from
the session index. Unlike the containing session `parentSessionId`
names above, its `parentSessionId` is the exact spawner, except that
any `muse` started in a later pane of the worker's tmux session or
Herdr workspace names the worker's manager and carries the worker's
`project`/`thread` labels (ADR 69621 D8); `project` and `thread` are
opaque labels the spawner may name beside it.
**Additive-optional** and **provenance only** (INV-005): never a
visibility or authority gate. Absence asserts nothing — no recorded
spawner, a later session of the spawned process, a row folded before
the member existed, or a session the index has not folded yet.

status.description:
Load state as this host knows it; `session/list` reports `notLoaded`
for sessions loaded by *other* hosts (tdd SS2.4).

title.description:
Derived display title (tdd SS2.14.1, #27598): a heuristic that may
evolve — its carriage, not its derivation, is the contract.
**Additive-optional**, omitted when underivable.

turnCount.description: Completed-turn count from the session view fold (tdd SS2.4).

workspaceRoot.description:
The winning metadata fold's workspace root; `null` when that record
omits it — absent is never fabricated (tdd SS2.4).

worktree.description:
The worktree this session runs in — path and origin only (the branch
stays in `branch`). **Experimental** (`Session.worktree`; stripped
per-connection for unopted callers). Omitted when the session runs in no
worktree.

SessionApprovalModeChangedParams.description:
`session/approvalModeChanged` params (tdd SS5.12): the fold of the
durable approval-mode reconfigure audit fact — every accepted change
writes one; a mode flip without an audit fact is a runtime bug by design.

clientName.description:
The requesting client's `clientInfo.name` (tdd SS1.4.1), recorded on
the audit fact.

clientVersion.description:
The requesting client's `clientInfo.version`, beside `clientName`
(ADR 73001 D4): absent when unrecorded and on older logs.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionBranchChangedParams.description:
`session/branchChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.4): a durable workspace-branch
observation landed.

branch.description:
The observed branch; `null` on a detached-HEAD observation — a fact,
not "unchanged" (tdd SS4.6.4).

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

vcs.description:
The detected version-control system; absent when no repository was
detected.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

sessionId.description: The loaded session the declaration is cleared for.

declared.description: Always `false` on a successful clear: no declaration is live.

SessionClosedParams.description:
`session/closed` params (tdd SS2.6.2; enrolled by #33065): a loaded
session was unloaded from this host, broadcast to every initialized
connection. After it, the session is `notLoaded`; the log remains on disk
and `session/resume` reloads it. A crash emits nothing — only the
orderly unload paths do (idle unload, host shutdown and a released
`session/leave`), and each writes the durable `SessionEnd` record first.

reason.description: Which orderly unload path fired.

viewCursor.description:
The final view head; a client that stores it can later
`session/resume {cursor}` and receive exactly the (empty) suffix. An
**opaque** view cursor: clients relay it, never parse it (tdd SS4.1).

**Required-nullable**: the producers always write the member and
write `null` when the final fold failed at unload (`session/idle.rs`,
`serve/shutdown.rs`; PR #16779 review) — the host defines no cursor
values of its own and never invents one, and the subscriber still
learns the session closed.

SessionClosedReason.description:
The SS2.6.2 closed-reason vocabulary. Server-produced and published
OPEN by owner ruling — the #33065 menu-B pick (PR #33201 comment
5638727249, recorded in the enrollment decision record), which settles
that this notification reason enum publishes open rather than resting on
E2's result-vocabulary rule by analogy. A crash is deliberately not a
reason, because a crash emits no notification at all.

oneOf.description:
A draining daemon unloaded this session on the upgrade path and
released its lease (ADR 59770 D7; tdd SS2.6.2). The successor on
the canonical socket reloads it at the next resume. Socket-only,
experimental tier (promotion gate in #69224). A connection that
did not opt in receives the `hostShutdown` fallback for this
value; opted-in connections decode `vacated`.

SessionCompactParams.description:
`session/compact` params (tdd SS3.7): manually compact the session's
conversation context — the `/compact` gesture. Compaction runs
asynchronously; the ack is admission only.

turnId.description:
The run whose context to compact. Omit and the server resolves the
session's current/latest run; a session with no resolvable run rejects
with `commandRejected` reason `missing_run` (tdd SS3.7). Any
syntactically valid UUID: a turn from an older session may carry a v4
or v5 id. A malformed id is `invalidParams`.

SessionCompactResult.description:
`session/compact` result (tdd SS3.7). Failures *after* admission
(`summarizer_failed`, `install_rejected`, `cancelled`) are not wire errors
— they arrive as the compaction's terminal view event.

reason.description:
Why the command was a noop, e.g. `no_compactable_history`. Present on
a `noop` status (tdd SS3.7).

SessionConfig.description:
The open configuration extension object shared by `session/start` and
`session/resume` (ADR 32760 D1).

Unknown keys are ignored on the wire, never rejected: the live decoder
tolerates them, and no exported bundle carries `additionalProperties:
false`. The Rust typed model's `deny_unknown_fields` is internal and never
exported — the closedness export applies nowhere, and the `x-msp-closed`
opt-in mechanism stays inert. Recognized `mcpServers` values are typed and
validated before they leave the wire boundary.

developerPrompt.description:
Experimental (ADR 32029 D38): developer instructions for this session
only, on `session/start` and `session/resume`. The text is trimmed. A
nonblank value replaces the settings-derived developer instructions;
an omitted member is no override and keeps the full developer context.
Explicit `null` and blank text are the explicit clear (the Rust value
is an empty string): no override, and on a host that serves developer
instructions they also turn off the session's suppressible developer
context (the agent catalog and the memory snapshot). Any other type
fails the decode. A host that does not serve developer instructions
ignores a valid member.

maxToolOutputBytes.description:
Experimental (#76374): this session's tool-output byte budget, as
`muse exec --max-tool-output-bytes` sets it for a headless run. `0`
means no limit; a positive value must be at least 9. The budget
applies only on a host whose default-off `tool_output_budget` gate
serves it (ADR 76374 D2): there, each model-visible tool result, from
workspace and MCP tools alike, is bounded at this many bytes from the
runtime's construction. Other hosts accept a valid value and ignore it.

mcpServers.description: Native MCP servers added only to this session runtime.

modelEndpointTransportOverride.description:
Experimental (spec 70824 FR-021): the model endpoint transport
this session's model consumers resolve against at load.

settingsOverrides.description:
Experimental (spec 70824 FR-020): a flat settings patch composing
for this session's loads only. Secret-shaped keys fail the decode.

SessionContextUsageParams.description:
`session/contextUsage` params (tdd SS4.6.6, #14405): context-window
pressure — the counted-once occupancy at the latest provider-reported
durable fact, joined with the host's pressure basis. Replace wholesale;
emitted only when the `(windowTokens, usedTokens, pressure)` triple
changes value (identical adoptions emit nothing).

pressure.description: Server-computed pressure level over the basis thresholds.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

usedTokens.description:
Counted-once prompt tokens (#8803) plus output tokens of the driving
record, saturating — the honest occupancy floor.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

reason.description:
The host's label for what the session waits on, shown in the
session view while the declaration is live. Omitted when the
host has no label to show.

sessionId.description: The loaded session the declaration is for.

declared.description: Always `true` on a successful declare: a declaration is live.

reason.description:
The live declaration's reason, as declared (truncated by the
host runtime). Omitted when the host declared without one.

SessionDriveChangedParams.description:
`session/driveChanged` params (tdd SS2.16; spec 39851 amendment #58706
FR-58706-7; ADR 58706-drive-handover D3): the session's drive holder
changed. A command-plane broadcast on the `session/statusChanged`
pattern — delivered to every connection on the host, subscribed or not;
a connection's `optOutNotificationMethods` suppresses it — so the
previous holder and every observer learn who drives now. Not a view
event: no `viewCursor`, no `sourceRange` (it reflects live registry
state, no durable record). The embedded single-connection host never
emits it (ADR 58706-drive-handover D6). **Experimental tier** (served on
the experimental bundle; the hand-over record's slices ride #58706).

driveHolder.description:
The handshake `ClientInfo` (name and version, never `title`) of the
live connection that holds the drive after this change — the value
`Session.driveHolder` serves (ADR 58706-bridged-client-attribution
D2), so the read and the push are one shape. Omitted when nobody
holds it; never `null`.

previousDriveHolder.description:
The handshake of the connection that held the drive before this
change: the displaced holder on `requested`, the releaser on
`released`, the dropped holder on `lapsed`. Omitted when nobody held
(every `resumed` take included); never `null`.

reason.description: Why the holder changed (open enum).

youDrive.description:
Set per recipient copy: `true` exactly for the connection that now
holds the drive. A handshake is not a connection id (two windows of
one client send the same `clientInfo`), so a client never learns it
lost the drive by comparing `driveHolder` to its own handshake (spec
42713 FR-58706-4); it reads this flag.

SessionDurability.description:
Whether this host writes its sessions to disk (SS1.4.1, SS2.13). A
property of the host process, fixed at construction and identical for
every session and every connection it serves — never requested, granted,
or negotiated, which is why it is not a capability. Open: the
unrepresented degraded state (#14401) has candidate resolutions that add a
third value here, so closed would make that a breaking change.

SessionEndpointTransportAuthMode.description:
How a request to the overridden endpoint authenticates, mirroring the
`tbh-config` `TransportAuthMode` spellings. Closed: an undeclared
mode fails the decode rather than degrading to a default.

SessionEventLogDegradedParams.description:
`session/eventLogDegraded` params (ADR 72648 D1, D2, experimental): a
loaded session's durable event log took a degraded write, so a record may
be missing from it. Outside the view stream, like
`session/viewHealthChanged`: no `viewCursor` and no `sourceRange`, so it
never takes a view position. Pushed to the session's live connections when
the degraded record commits, and restated to a client whose
`session/resume` serves item history.

sequence.description:
The degraded record's log sequence (ADR 72648 D2): the live push and a
resume's restatement of one record carry the same value, the key a
client draws each record once by. Absent from a host that predates D2;
a client then draws every frame.

approvalRules.description:
Client-supplied shell prefix allow-rules override (tdd SS5.16,
ADR 47712 D3, ruled): omitted inherits the source session's rules,
present replaces with that set (an explicit empty array clears).
Explicit `null` is invalid params. Until the served-handler slice, a
host refuses any spelled `approvalRules` on
`session/start`/`fork`/`resume` with `-32602`; clients omit it
(`crates/session-server/src/session/approval_rules_unserved.rs::refuse_if_spelled`).
**Experimental**
(`session/fork.approvalRules`).

cutPoint.description:
Copy history through a completed turn, inclusive. Omitted means "all
completed turns" (tdd SS2.5.3).

excludeItems.description:
Skip inline history in the result and page it later — same as
`session/resume` (tdd SS2.5.3).

SessionForkResult.description:
`session/fork` result (tdd SS2.5.3): the `session/resume` envelope for the
**new** session, whose `session.forkedFrom` carries the provenance.

session.description: The new fork session, carrying `forkedFrom` provenance.

viewCursor.description: The new session's view head.

SessionGoalChangedParams.description:
`session/goalChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.2): the projected goal block's
value changed — identical adoptions emit nothing (the change gate), and
an explicit `null` clears. Replace wholesale; `null` never means
unchanged.

goal.description: The full current goal block, or `null` to clear.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionHistory.description:
The `history` envelope shared by `session/resume`, `session/fork`, and
`session/read` (tdd SS2.5.2).

checkpointBoundary.description:
The checkpoint-prune boundary (spec 13929 amendment FR-50042-1):
rows for served items at-or-before `through_item_id` in served
order predate the selected checkpoint. Additive-optional;
absence is a non-assertion (ADR 50042 D6).

items.description: The full folded item array when `mode` is `inline`; `null` otherwise.

mode.description: What was actually served — never what was asked for (tdd SS2.5.2).

noneReason.description:
Why no history was served — sent exactly when `mode` is `"none"`
(tdd SS2.5.2; D-050, spec 208 INV-19734-1).

snapshot.description:
The folded view state when `mode` is `snapshot` or `anchoredSnapshot`;
`null` otherwise.

SessionKind.description:
What kind of session this is (spec 42713 FR-001/FR-005, ADR 42713 D1/D4).

**Open**: a new kind is additive evolution, and a client MUST render an
unknown value as an unknown-but-present kind rather than rejecting the
row. Both v1 values are terms the tree already uses — the child log
directory is `subagent` and `ItemKind` already carries a `subagent`
variant — so no new vocabulary is minted.

SessionLeaveCompletedParams.description: Params of the protected, non-view leave terminal notification.

commandId.description: The leave command's id, matching the `session/leave` request.

outcome.description:
How the leave ended: `released` or `failed`. The set is open, so newer
hosts may add outcomes.

reason.description: Why the leave failed. Present when `outcome` is `failed`.

sessionId.description: The session the leave was for.

viewCursor.description:
The session's view cursor at release: everything up to it was folded
before the host let go. Present when `outcome` is `released`.

SessionLeaveFailureReason.description:
Current producer failure reasons for `session/leaveCompleted`;
receiver-open for additive future reasons.

sessionId.description: The exact loaded session whose ownership is to be released.

stop.description: Explicitly cancel unfinished work before leaving. Omitted is `false`.

status.description:
The admission status, `accepted` once the leave is admitted. The final
result arrives later as `session/leaveCompleted`. Sending the same leave
command again returns `accepted` and re-pushes the recorded result if
there is one, from the host that ran the leave (for as long as it runs,
even after the release) or from a host that has the session loaded
(after a host crash, `abandoned` among them). Any other host treats it
as a fresh leave: a durable host that has not loaded the session refuses
it with `sessionNotLoaded` until it is resumed there.

SessionLimits.description:
A five-axis limits report (tdd SS1.10): every `maxLimits` /
`currentLimits` member is this one definition, and every member is
required — reporting always fills all five, so readers never see
an absence.

workspaceTrusted.description: Loading the workspace's skills and rules (`--trust-workspace`).

SessionLimitsChoice.description:
The `session/start` `limits` choice (tdd SS1.10): every member is
optional — a start names only the axes it chooses, and an omitted axis
reads the daemon default: the daemon's own posture on the sandbox axes,
and on trust untrusted unless the daemon serves trusted by default
(ADR 59770 D4a). On a daemon whose default sandbox is off, turning the
sandbox on takes both `sandboxEnabled: true` and `sandboxNetwork`;
naming `sandboxEnabled: true` without `sandboxNetwork`, or a network
restriction (`restricted` or `proxy-only`) without naming
`sandboxEnabled`, is refused `-32602` (`data.reason:
"tighterSandboxUnserved"`) until #63513 settles how a session turns the
sandbox on there; a network restriction beside an explicit
`sandboxEnabled: false`, which never turns it on, is refused the same way
while #76053 is open, so drop the restriction. Where the ceiling allows
the sandbox off over a sandbox-on default, a network restriction beside
`sandboxEnabled: false` is admitted and restricts nothing: with the
sandbox off the network is not sandboxed, so the session runs and
reports `sandboxNetwork: "enabled"`.
Reports use `SessionLimits`, whose members are always present. A
`session/resume` names only `workspaceTrusted` here (ADR 73001 D6).

workspaceTrusted.description: Loading the workspace's skills and rules (`--trust-workspace`).

anyOf.description:
1–32 nonempty branch names, each 1–256 UTF-8 bytes, counted before
deduplication; `null` selects sessions with no branch.

SessionListChangedParams.description:
`session/listChanged` params (#33084, ADR 33084 D3): one changed row of
the `session/list` shape — the full SS2.4 Session object as the answering
host's list face serves it at emission (the ADR 29243 live-overlaid row),
a replace, never a delta. Emitted only on connections that negotiated the
`sessionListStream` capability at `initialize` (ADR 33084 D2); row birth
stays on `session/started`, unload pairs with `session/closed`.

session.description: The served list row for the changed session.

SessionListFilter.description:
The `session/list` filter (#42035, spec 207 FR-42035-2..5). Members are
ANDed with each other and with the top-level `workspaceRoot` and
`updatedAfter`; values inside each `anyOf` are ORed. The canonical form
the server echoes deduplicates and sorts every set, spells session IDs as
canonical UUIDs, lowercases text terms, and orders `text.fields` `name`
then `title`.

branch.description: Only sessions whose branch is one of these.

sessionId.description: Only sessions whose ID is one of these.

text.description: Only sessions whose served name or title matches these token prefixes.

SessionListParams.description: `session/list` params (tdd SS2.5.4). Read-only; never touches leases.

cursor.description:
Opaque page cursor from a prior result. Page cursors are a distinct
opaque-string family from view cursors and stream cursors, valid only
for re-issuing the same listing (tdd SS2.5.4). Omitted and explicit
`null` both mean "first page" (#23468).

filter.description:
Optional structured selection applied inside the bounded index query
before paging (#42035, spec 207 FR-42035-1). Present — including
`{}` — makes a supporting server echo its canonical form as
`appliedFilter`; omitted keeps the pre-#42035 behavior.

limit.description: Page size; default 50, max 200 — the schema publishes the cap.

updatedAfter.description: Only sessions with log activity after this RFC3339 instant.

workspaceRoot.description: Only sessions whose metadata workspace root equals this path.

SessionListResult.description:
`session/list` result (tdd SS2.5.4). The default order is content
activity: `lastActivityAt` descending, then `sessionId` ascending. The
order is the session index's key, so a row's displayed timestamps do not
always show its position: a row the index has not yet derived keeps its
`updatedAt` position, a derived row with no content orders by
`createdAt`, and a loaded row can show newer values. Do not re-sort or
validate a page from them. `updatedAfter` still filters on `updatedAt`.

appliedFilter.description:
The canonical filter the server applied, present exactly when the
request carried `filter` (#42035, spec 207 FR-42035-1). The probe is
per-predicate PRESENCE (ADR 42035 D6): a client that requires
filtering checks that every predicate it sent comes back as a member
here, and treats a missing member as unsupported. Value equality is
the wrong test — canonicalization trims, lowercases, NFC-normalizes,
dedupes and sorts, so the echoed values often differ from the sent
ones on a correctly filtered page.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor; `null` on the last page.

SessionListTextField.description:
A served session field `session/list` text search reads (#42035
FR-42035-3). The client selects it, so the set is closed.

SessionListTextFilter.description:
Name/title token-prefix search (#42035 FR-42035-3/FR-42035-4). Each term
is trimmed, lowercased with ordinary Unicode lowercase, then NFC-
normalized, and matches the beginning of an alphanumeric token,
accent-sensitively (`check` matches `Checkout`; `eck` does not). NFC
means a decomposed and a precomposed spelling of one term are the same
term, and the echo returns the composed form. Matching never reorders
rows.

allOf.description: Every term must match at least one selected field.

anyOf.description:
At least one term must match a selected field. `allOf` plus `anyOf`
carry 1–16 terms in total, each 1–128 UTF-8 bytes in its canonical
form (trimmed, lowercased, NFC) — the bytes `appliedFilter` echoes.
Lowercasing and NFC can both lengthen a term, so a term inside the
bound raw may still exceed it canonically.

SessionLogFlushDegradedParams.description:
`session/logFlushDegraded` params (ADR 78845 D1, experimental): a run's
turn-end session-log flush on the host left records failed or waiting for
retry, or failed itself. Outside the view stream, like
`session/eventLogDegraded`: no `viewCursor` and no `sourceRange`. Either
the counts (with an optional `cause`) or, exactly when the flush itself
failed, only `error`.

cause.description:
The lost log the result reports, else its missing log. Absent when
neither is reported or the flush failed.

error.description:
The failed flush's message, present exactly when the flush itself
failed.

failed.description:
Records the flush could not write, summed over the session's run, task
and approval logs. Absent when the flush failed.

unflushed.description:
Records still waiting for a retry, summed the same way. Absent when the
flush failed.

SessionMcpServerConfig.description:
One native MCP server supplied at session construction (ADR 32760 D1).

**Closed union** (#33295 owner ruling A1, extending D-033/D-050 to
`oneOf`): a validator MUST reject an undeclared `transport` arm — the
server fails `session/start` decode on an unknown transport, and a future
transport arrives as an explicit schema addition.

command.description: Executable name or path. Configuration diagnostics never echo it.

framing.description: Stdio framing mode; defaults to automatic detection.

mode.description: Required/optional startup posture; defaults to required.
Required/optional startup posture; defaults to required.

url.description: HTTP(S) endpoint. Configuration diagnostics never echo it.

SessionMcpServerMode.description: Startup failure posture for a session MCP server.

SessionMcpStdioFraming.description: Stdio framing choices exposed by session MCP configuration.

SessionModelChangedParams.description:
`session/modelChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.1): a durable model-selection
record landed (tdd SS3.8).

providerId.description: The selected provider; `null` when the selection names none.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionModelEndpointTransportOverride.description:
FR-021: the per-session model endpoint transport override, mirroring
the `tbh-config` `EndpointTransportConfig` fields under MSP camelCase
wire names (`base_url` -> `baseUrl`, `http_headers` -> `httpHeaders`,
and so on; the mTLS path fields travel as strings, paths being a host
concern). Every field is optional; all absent is the default
transport. Resolution against managed egress policy is a later slice.

allowOpenai.description: Closed grant allowing an explicit OpenAI URL to reuse this block.

auth.description: Auth mode. Absent = `bearer` (the default transport behavior).

baseUrl.description: Endpoint base URL. Configuration diagnostics never echo it.

caBundle.description: Optional CA bundle (PEM) to trust for the server side.

clientCert.description: Path to the mTLS client certificate (PEM).

clientKey.description: Path to the mTLS client private key (PEM).

envHttpHeaders.description: Provider header name -> environment variable name.

proxy.description: An explicit HTTP proxy URL. Diagnostics never echo it.

SessionModelRouteUnservedParams.description:
`session/modelRouteUnserved` params (#25603, ADR 25603 D1, spec 5469
Amendment 16): an accepted `login.credential_update` installed a provider
that cannot serve the session's STANDING model route. Disclosure only —
the standing selection is unchanged (no `session/modelChanged` fires) and
the repair path is a routable `session/setModel`. Folded from the durable
`runtime.provider_reconfigure.standing_route_unserved` record; additive —
clients that predate it skip the unknown method.

commandId.description: The command whose accepted swap installed the provider.

installedProviderId.description: The provider id the swap installed.

modelId.description: The standing (still bound, now unroutable) model.

providerId.description: The standing model's provider; `null` when the selection names none.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionNameChangedParams.description:
`session/nameChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.7, #27598): the fold of ANY
durable session-name record — the FIRST-NAMING automatic allocate as well
as an accepted `session/rename` (or the same in-process runtime command).
Replace-wholesale like every SS4.6 sibling.

generatedName.description:
The latest retained generated short title (tdd SS2.4/SS4.6.7,
#50048; ADR 50048-generated-name D1). **Additive-optional**: carried
at generated-pair publication and at settlement when a pair is
already published; omitted when no pair was ever published — absent
reads as unpublished, never fabricated. `name` stays canonical.

name.description: The new canonical name now in effect.

nameOrigin.description:
How the new name was set (tdd SS2.4/SS4.6.7, #50048; ADR 50048
D1/D2). **Additive-optional**: omitted when the emitting fold cannot
prove an origin — absent reads as unknown, never fabricated.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionNameOrigin.description:
How the served session name was set (tdd SS2.4/SS4.6.7, #50048; ADR
50048 D1). **Open enum** (`x-msp-openness: open`): v1 serves
`automatic` and `custom`; a client MUST read absent — and any value it
does not recognize — as unknown, never fabricated. Open: a future source
such as conversation-generated names (#35260) adds a value here, so
closed would make that a breaking change.

SessionPermissionProfileChangedParams.description:
`session/permissionProfileChanged` params (amendment 42624 FR-42624-5):
the fold of the durable profile-commit audit fact — fired on every accepted
POST-EPOCH-ONE profile commit, never for a mode-only change (that writes no
such fact and keeps folding `session/approvalModeChanged` from its own
reconfigure fact) and never for a reviewer-attachment change (live runtime
evidence, no durable fact, FR-42624-4). It folds on EVERY
`PermissionProfileCommittedV1` EXCEPT the epoch-one initialization fact and
fork/child derivation facts — their causes (`newSessionDefault`, `launchCli`
at start, `fork`, `childSpawn`, `legacyInitialization`, `launchOverrides`)
are unreachable on the wire until a later commit carries them — so an
omitted-profile start and an empty-cut fork fold nothing and their
`""`-cursor rules (SS2.5.1/SS4.1) hold byte-for-byte. A held id recommitting
under a changed definition or a managed refresh (FM-005) folds too (the
`profileId` may equal the prior), exactly as the approvalMode precedent folds
per accepted change. The `session/approvalModeChanged` member pattern with
`profileId` in place of `mode`; additive-optional (clients predating it
skip the unknown method); subscription-gated like every other view event.

clientName.description:
The requesting client's `clientInfo.name` (tdd SS1.4.1), read from the
committed fact's durable `PermissionCommandLinkV1.client_name` seat
(FR-42624-5, owner-accepted in the ADR 42197 D8 record; PR #44963).
`null` when no client recorded the change: the Initialization/
ManagedRefresh causes, native picker commits, and facts written before
the seat existed.

commandId.description:
The command that changed it; `null` on an Initialization- or
ManagedRefresh-kind fold that no accepted command produced (only the
`livePicker`/`resumeCli` causes carry it — the `lastCommandId: null`
precedent).

profileId.description:
The profile now in effect; `null` when the committed source is a launch
override (`LaunchOverrides` pins `id: None`) — FR-42624-4's served-site rule.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionPromptHintCandidate.description:
One `session/promptHint` candidate (ADR 50063 D1): the table row's
stable `id` plus its model-facing "relevant when …" description.
Display copy stays client-side; the wire never carries it.
Experimental: the stable bundle strips this until the surface
stabilizes (in-v1 row 346).

description.description: The model-facing relevance note for this row.

id.description: The table row id the model may echo back (`[a-z0-9-]+`).

SessionPromptHintParams.description:
`session/promptHint` params (ADR 50063 D1): the session plus the
client-filtered candidate table. A read-only query in the
`model/list` mold: no `commandId`, no durable record, no view
event — the INV-008 display-only side call over the wire.
Experimental: the stable bundle strips this until the surface
stabilizes (in-v1 row 346).

candidates.description: The candidates the model may pick from (client-filtered).

SessionPromptHintResult.description:
`session/promptHint` result (ADR 50063 D1): the picked table id,
or `None` when the model declines (the NONE arm) — never a copy
string, so the pinned table stays the single source of truth.
Experimental: the stable bundle strips this until the surface
stabilizes (in-v1 row 346).

hintId.description: The picked candidate id, if any.

sessionId.description: The session whose effective limits to read.

SessionReadLimitsResult.description: `session/readLimits` result (tdd SS1.10): one session's effective limits.

currentLimits.description:
The session's effective limits, clamped to the live ceiling;
`workspaceTrusted` is the trust the session runs with.

SessionReadParams.description:
`session/read` params (tdd SS2.5.5): read one stored session **without
attaching** — no writer lease, no load, no subscription, no
`SessionResumed` record.

excludeItems.description:
Metadata-only unless you ask: `false` carries the folded item history.
Same name and polarity as `session/resume`/`session/fork`; only the
default differs — here it is `true` (tdd SS2.5.5).

SessionReadResult.description:
`session/read` result (tdd SS2.5.5). The `viewCursor` is the fold head at
read time — a point-in-time read, immediately stale if a foreign host is
appending.

blockedPrompt.description: Same member as `session/resume` (tdd SS2.5.5, ADR 50074 D2).

deliveredInputs.description:
The inputs the read session's log delivered to its subagents
(tdd SS2.5.5, ADR 72596-delivered-inputs-on-read D2).
Absent-when-empty: a missing member means nothing delivered,
never an error.

lastTurn.description: Same member as `session/resume` (tdd SS2.5.5, ADR 36635 D2).

pendingRequests.description:
The same pointer shape as `session/resume`. Because `session/read`
never subscribes this is a point-in-time log read only: no requests
are re-issued after it (tdd SS2.5.5).

prunedSubagents.description:
One short record per child session the checkpoint boundary pruned
(tdd SS2.5.5, ADR 71910 D8). Absent-when-empty: a missing member
means the view is uncompacted or nothing pruned, never an error.

queuedInputs.description:
The inputs still queued for delivery to the read session (tdd
SS2.5.5, ADR 63254-queued-inputs-on-read D2). Absent-when-empty:
a missing member means nothing queued, never an error.

recoveryObservation.description:
Current local construction only; never inferred from retained history.
Absence establishes neither a choice nor supported recovery.

viewCursor.description: The fold head at read time.

worktree.description:
The facts of the runtime-owned worktree a child read session's
subagent runs in (tdd SS2.5.5, ADR 50042-child-worktree-on-read D2).
A root read serves it absent; absent means no worktree facts, never
an error.

SessionReasoningEffortChangedParams.description:
`session/reasoningEffortChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.9, ADR 31255 D1): a
durable reasoning-effort reconfigure record landed (tdd SS3.21). Replace
wholesale, latest wins; the snapshot carries the latest value (SS4.9.1).

reasoningEffort.description:
The new session default: the same closed eight-string tier vocabulary as
`turn/start`.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

sessionId.description: The loaded session whose drive the holder gives back.

SessionReleaseDriveResult.description:
`session/releaseDrive` result (FR-58706-6): `released` left the session
loaded with nobody driving (a duplicate release or a holderless session
answers it too, with no notice), `busy` changed nothing because a turn
runs, or the session is idle with a launch still queued or its launch
count unreadable (no `turn/completed` is promised on that arm). No
holder member: after a release nobody holds. The two typed
refusals (`sessionNotLoaded`, `sessionInUse`) are errors, not results.

SessionRenameParams.description:
`session/rename` params (tdd SS2.14.2, #27598): set or change the durable
allocated session name through the runtime `session_name` command. One
writer; withheld under the ephemeral profile.

name.description: The requested name; the runtime's normalization and validation apply.

SessionRenameResult.description:
`session/rename` result (tdd SS2.14.2, #27598): `name` is the canonical
(normalized) name the durable record settled.

name.description:
The settled canonical name. Omitted on the `RecoveryPending` arm, which
answers `{commandId, status: "accepted"}` and delivers the name via
`session/nameChanged` / `Session.name` (tdd SS2.14.2).

SessionReportStartupPhase.description:
`session/reportStartupPhases` span phase (ADR 50064 pick-1 D1):
the `StartupPhasesRecord` phase vocabulary in camelCase (INV-016;
D1 delegates member names to the lane). The host maps each value
onto the record's snake_case spelling at append.
Experimental: the stable bundle strips this until the surface
stabilizes (in-v1 row 348).

SessionReportStartupPhaseSpan.description:
`session/reportStartupPhases` span (ADR 50064 pick-1 D1): one
`StartupPhasesRecord` phase row in camelCase (INV-016; D1 delegates
member names to the lane). The host ignores unknown members and
fails closed (`invalidParams`) on an unknown phase or provenance
value; a `colorProvenance` on any other phase is stripped (spec
7221: the field never appears there). The host maps each row onto
the record's snake_case spelling at append.
Experimental: the stable bundle strips this until the surface
stabilizes (in-v1 row 348).

colorProvenance.description: The terminal color provenance (terminal-probe row only).

startMs.description: Milliseconds from the launch anchor to the row start.

SessionReportStartupPhasesParams.description:
`session/reportStartupPhases` params (ADR 50064 pick-1 D1): the served
session, the client-minted launch nonce (one UUID per process launch,
any textual UUID form), and the finished spans. No `commandId`: the
nonce is the idempotency key and the call is best-effort.
Experimental: the stable bundle strips this until the surface
stabilizes (in-v1 row 348).

launchNonce.description: The launch nonce (any UUID: hyphenated any-case or 32-hex simple).

SessionReportStartupPhasesResult.description:
`session/reportStartupPhases` result (ADR 50064 pick-1 D1): whether
this report appended. A duplicate nonce succeeds with
`recorded: false` and appends nothing.
Experimental: the stable bundle strips this until the surface
stabilizes (in-v1 row 348).

recorded.description: True when this report appended the durable record.

SessionReportTerminalColorProvenance.description:
`session/reportStartupPhases` terminal color provenance (ADR 50064
pick-1 D1): the durable `TerminalColorProvenance` vocabulary in
camelCase (INV-016; D1 delegates member names to the lane). The host
maps each value onto the record spelling at append.
Experimental: the stable bundle strips this until the surface
stabilizes (in-v1 row 348).

sessionId.description: The loaded session whose drive the caller asks for.

SessionRequestDriveResult.description:
`session/requestDrive` result (FR-58706-5, as amended by ADR 69811 D3
and ADR 58706-drive-handover D8): `granted` moved the drive to the caller
(or the caller already held it) and stopped nothing — no turn ran, or
another connection's turn runs or its input waits and now runs on under
the caller; `busy` left everything as it was — the caller's own turn
runs or its input waits, the live holder is idle and its queue cannot be
read, or the live holder is not quiet and has not opted into
`experimentalApi`, so it could not hear that it lost the drive; nothing
is parked, and the caller asks again later (after `turn/completed` when a
turn runs; a runtime that cannot report its queue promises none). An
unloaded session is the typed resume-first refusal, not a result.

driveHolder.description:
The handshake `ClientInfo` (name and version, never `title`) of the
live connection that holds the drive after the answer: the caller on
`granted`, the live holder on `busy`. Never `null`.

approvalRules.description:
Client-supplied shell prefix allow-rules override (tdd SS5.16,
ADR 47712 D3, ruled): omitted reinstalls the session's rules from
the audit fact, present replaces with that set (an explicit empty
array clears). Explicit `null` is invalid params. Until the
served-handler slice, a host refuses any spelled `approvalRules` on
`session/start`/`fork`/`resume` with `-32602`; clients omit it
(`crates/session-server/src/session/approval_rules_unserved.rs::refuse_if_spelled`).
**Experimental**
(`session/resume.approvalRules`).

commandId.description:
The SS2.5 idempotency handle (UUIDv7). A resume that loads a session
writes a durable `SessionResumed` record.

config.description: The same open construction-time extension object as `session/start`.

continuePausedSource.description:
D7's optional actor-bound explicit continuation object: the explicit
user Resume action supplies it for a loaded paused source; absent or
null keeps current resume behavior and does not release this
feature's loaded-source hold. Nullable (D7's null-tolerant set).
Standalone DTO (T-50280-074): the real effect is T-50280-084's.

cursor.description:
A view cursor previously observed by this client — or an observed
`summarizedThrough` compaction anchor. When it names an event the server
still holds, the server returns only the suffix and `history.mode` is
`none`. A cursor the server minted that names no event yet, such as the
empty start cursor of a session that had no events, is treated as no
cursor: the server serves what a resume without a cursor would. A cursor
older than the earliest event the server still holds gets a snapshot, or
`-32040` `viewTruncated` when none fits. A cursor this session's view
never minted is refused with `-32011` `notFound`, reason
`missingAnchor`, and a compaction anchor naming a boundary the server
has pruned is refused with `-32042` `boundaryPruned`. Omitted and
explicit `null` both mean "no cursor".

excludeItems.description:
Return only session metadata and live resume state; page history
separately with `view/page`. Default `false` (tdd SS2.5.2).

history.description:
History mode preference, default `auto`. A PREFERENCE, not a budget
override: when the requested mode does not fit the history budget the
server downgrades it and `history.mode` reports what was actually
served (tdd SS2.5.2). Ignored when `cursor` or `excludeItems` makes it
moot.

limits.description:
The SS1.10 trust ask for the session this resume loads (ADR 73001
D6): `session/start.limits`'s shape, of which a resume names only
`workspaceTrusted`. Naming another axis is invalid params: a resumed
session keeps its stored sandbox, write and shell limits. The ask
takes the place of the session's stored trust choice, made or not, and
the load records it as the session's choice; the host's ceiling bounds
it as it bounds a stored one (`tightenedAxes` names a clamp). Only the
resume that loads the session reads it; an attach ignores it.
**Experimental, served only by the per-run host a TUI run starts**
(`session/resume.limits`; unopted callers are refused `-32602`, as are
opted callers on every other host, where a session resumes with its
saved trust choice, which an earlier ask on a TUI run's host may have
replaced, a fork or side-chat child included (ADR 69811 D2 (c) as
amended by #83669)). Explicit `null` is invalid params.

missingInputAssets.description:
What a cold load does with a retained input image whose file is
missing or corrupt (tdd SS2.5.2, ADR 78319 D1). Omitted means `fail`;
explicit `null` is invalid params. Only the resume that loads the
session reads it; an attach ignores it. **Experimental**
(`session/resume.missingInputAssets`).

modelId.description:
The explicit MSP model override (T-51858-304; INV-51858-11 rank 1):
a model string the caller supplies at resume time. When present it
wins over the retained binding's recorded origin — over a stamped
label and over a stamped pin — and it recovers an
otherwise-unresolved label binding by sending the override as the
wire model instead of the unresolved refusal. Omitted preserves
arm (2): the retained binding resolves by recorded origin exactly
as without this member. Explicit `null` is invalid params (the
same closed null-tolerant set as at start). The override changes
the model within the retained provider; it never names a provider.
A resume that loads the session records it as a resume `--model`
records (ADR 24046 D7): nothing when it already is the session's
model, else one durable selection with the provider's profile for
that model. A resume that attaches to a loaded session switches
the model live. A model the host refuses, a blank one included,
leaves the session on its recorded model, which `session.modelId`
reports; a connection that opted into `experimentalApi` also gets
the reason in `modelIdRefusal`.

permissionProfile.description:
The launch permission-profile pick (amendment 42624 FR-42624-1,
#50054): a profile id the host catalog already admits. Select, never
create. Omitted restores retained authority only, with no override.
The host restores first, then applies the pick in the same pre-marker
step; over a declared lost record the restore is the never-wider reset,
committed before the pick, and where the reset cannot commit the pick
is committed alone as that reset (spec 11237 FR-57059-4). A pick that
fails admission refuses the
resume `commandRejected` (-32030; `permission_profile_unknown` /
`permission_profile_unavailable`) before any durable byte. Explicit
`null` is invalid params (the same closed null-tolerant set as at
start).

recoveryMode.description:
Cold-resume replacement choice; omission preserves the retained choice.
A warm attach rejects a different or unestablished choice as invalidParams.
Explicit null is invalid.

abnormalEnd.description:
The previous run's abnormal end this resume's own load adopted (tdd
SS2.5.2, ADR 68419 D1). **Experimental** (`session/resume.abnormalEnd`;
stripped for unopted connections); absence asserts nothing (an attach
to a loaded session, a clean prior end, or an older host). Clients may
show a one-time notice from it.

autoRecovery.description:
The auto-recover outcome of this resume's own load (amendment
26387/68619, G-23). **Experimental** (`session/resume.autoRecovery`;
stripped for unopted connections); absent unless the load ran with
the `resume_auto_recover` gate on and an effective `recoveryMode` of
ON, so a gate-off host's result is unchanged.

blockedPrompt.description:
The recallable blocked prompt's refill text (ADR 50074 D2).
**Additive-optional**; absence means no blocked prompt to recall
(an unblocked session, or a pre-feature host). Data only, never
a rendered row: clients seed cold recall from it (C-p refills
`text`) and MUST NOT display it as history.

cronQuarantine.description:
The cron quarantine this resume's own load adopted (tdd SS2.5.2,
ADR 72647 D1). **Experimental** (`session/resume.cronQuarantine`;
stripped for unopted connections); absence asserts nothing (an attach
to a loaded session, a healthy or missing store, or an older host).
Clients show the gate-off warning row once from it.

lastTurn.description:
How the last folded turn ended (tdd SS2.5.2, ADR 36635 D2).
**Additive-optional**; absence is a non-assertion.

missingPredecessor.description:
The declared predecessor whose retained log this resume's own load
found missing (tdd SS2.5.2, ADR 77295 D1). **Experimental**
(`session/resume.missingPredecessor`; stripped for unopted
connections); absence asserts nothing (an attach to a loaded session,
a root session, a present predecessor, or an older host). Clients show
the gate-off missing-predecessor notice once from it.

modelIdRefusal.description:
The `modelId` this resume carried and the host refused (ADR 24046
D7): the session opened on its recorded model, which `session`
reports. **Experimental** (`session/resume.modelIdRefusal`; stripped
for unopted connections); absent when the resume carried no
`modelId` or the host recorded or kept it. Clients show the model
kept and the reason once from it.

pendingRequests.description: The late-joiner pointer set; empty when nothing is pending.

prunedSubagents.description:
One short record per child session the checkpoint boundary pruned
(tdd SS2.5.2, ADR 71910 D8). **Additive-optional**, like
`queuedInputs` on the read: absent-when-empty, never stripped.

restartReceipts.description:
The manual-compaction restart receipts this resume's own load
scanned (tdd SS2.5.2, ADR 71350-B2 D1). **Experimental**
(`session/resume.restartReceipts`); absence asserts nothing (an
attach to a loaded session, no unserved restart arm, or an older
host). Absent when the scan found none — never an empty array. Each
entry mirrors the runtime `ManualCompactionReceipt`; clients
apply them through the shared receipt path.

tightenedAxes.description:
The SS1.10 axes this resume tightened (tdd SS1.10 Q3; ADR 39851-ss1-10
D2 Q3; ADR 59770 D4): when the stored choice exceeds the restarted
host's narrower ceiling, the resume clamps to fit, carries the
tightened `currentLimits` on the session, and names each tightened
axis here. **Experimental, same-user socket only**
(`session/resume.tightenedAxes`; stripped per-connection for unopted
callers). Absent when nothing tightened — never an empty array.

unavailableInputAssets.description:
The retained input images this resume's own `report` load replaced
with a marker (tdd SS2.5.2, ADR 78319 D1), one entry per distinct
digest (a provisional owner ruling) at its first occurrence: runs in
the log position of their accepted User Intent record (a run with
none at its first run record), then images by position in the run.
**Experimental** (`session/resume.unavailableInputAssets`; stripped
for unopted connections); absent when nothing was replaced, never an
empty array.

viewCursor.description:
The session view head; the connection is subscribed after it. A
still-loaded session a prior `view/unsubscribe` detached is
RE-ATTACHED by this resume (spec 208 FR-002a, #28920): live delivery
resumes from this head. Explicit-cursor re-attach with `(after, head]`
engine replay stays `view/subscribe` (SS4.7.1).

SessionRulesChangedParams.description:
`session/rulesChanged` params (tdd SS3.37, ADR 70236 D1): a rules
refresh replaced the `rules_file` block's listed sources. A live
host-state projection in the `skill/changed` mold — not a view event:
no `viewCursor`, no `sourceRange`, nothing written to the event log,
no transcript row, no ordering relative to view events, live-only
(resume does not restate it). Broadcast delivery (the
`session/driveChanged` pattern): every bound connection, with the
sink's own opt-out and experimental filters. **Experimental tier**.

sources.description:
The refreshed sources in precedence order, mirroring the refreshed
`RulesStatusSnapshot`: one entry per `<rules-file>` tag the
refreshed block lists. Empty when the block was removed.

SessionSetApprovalModeParams.description:
`session/setApprovalMode` params (tdd SS5.12): switch the session's
approval enforcement mode mid-session. A standard SS3 command.

**Select, never create.** A client may *select* a mode the host's
configuration already defines; it may not construct one, supply inline
rules, or otherwise describe a policy on the wire — which is why
[`ApprovalMode`] is closed.

mode.description:
The preconfigured mode to select. The requesting actor is recorded
from the connection's `clientInfo.name` (tdd SS1.4.1).

SessionSetApprovalModeResult.description:
`session/setApprovalMode` result (tdd SS5.12). Applies next-action — an
in-flight tool action's pending approval is not retroactively decided by a
mode change.

effectiveMode.description:
The folded effective-mode projection — the same object the `Session`
carries as `approvalMode` (tdd SS2.4, SS5.12).

SessionSetApprovalRulesParams.description:
`session/setApprovalRules` params (tdd SS5.16, ADR 47712 D2): replace the
session's client-origin rule set wholesale. A standard SS3 command, and —
following ADR 44483 D2 — only the driving connection may call it.
