rules.description:
The complete new set (an empty array clears it). The requesting actor
is recorded from the connection's `clientInfo.name` (tdd SS1.4.1).

SessionSetApprovalRulesResult.description:
`session/setApprovalRules` result (tdd SS5.16). Applies next-action — an
in-flight tool action's pending approval is not retroactively decided by a
rules change. The set itself reads back via `Session.permissionState`
(ADR 47712 D6), not echoed here.

SessionSetModelParams.description:
`session/setModel` params (tdd SS3.8): the model-picker gesture. The
selection is durable and applies to subsequent model calls.

SessionSetModelResult.description:
`session/setModel` result (tdd SS3.8). If a turn is running the selection
is admitted now and applied at the next model-call boundary; the ack does
not wait for that boundary.

SessionSetPermissionProfileParams.description:
`session/setPermissionProfile` params (amendment 42624 FR-42624-2): change
the profile of a loaded durable session through the existing authenticated
permission-controller transaction. A standard SS3 command; the actor
identity is the SS3 command attribution `session/setApprovalMode` already
uses.

**Select, never create.** A client selects a profile the host catalog
already admits (`ExecutionPolicyProjection::permission_profiles`); it may
not construct one or supply inline rules — there is no inline-rule member
and none may be added under this contract (INV-42624-2).

profileId.description:
The profile id to select — a stable native-catalog identifier
(`:auto-review`, `:ask-me`, `:read-only`, `:unrestricted`, or an
admitted user/managed definition).

SessionSetPermissionProfileResult.description:
`session/setPermissionProfile` result (amendment 42624 FR-42624-2). The
transaction, per-action authority combination, and blocked-state/recovery
semantics are the native controller's, not the adapter's (ADR 42197
D2/D6). A failure after a durable permission commit keeps the native
controller's existing blocked-state surface; the adapter fabricates no
rollback.

commandId.description:
Echoes the client's `commandId` — the SS3.1.2 ack id and the
FR-42624-5 join key (amendment 42624 § session/setPermissionProfile
result, line 203; the `session/setApprovalMode` precedent).

permissionState.description:
The committed permission snapshot after the change — the same object
the `Session` carries as `permissionState` (amendment 42624
FR-42624-4).

status.description:
Admission status — `accepted` for every admitted command (SS3.1.2),
exactly as `SessionSetApprovalModeResult` carries it.

SessionSetReasoningEffortParams.description:
`session/setReasoningEffort` params (tdd SS3.21, ADR 31255 D1): set the
session's standing reasoning-effort default. A turn carrying its own
`reasoningEffort` overrides it for that turn only; the default overrides
the host's configured default. Same accept/reject and `commandId`
idempotency shape as `session/setModel` (SS3.8).

reasoningEffort.description:
The new session default: the closed eight-string tier vocabulary
`turn/start` carries (SS3.2), spelled identically. Invalid tiers are
invalid params. A default of `max` rides provider requests verbatim,
never clamped (ADR 28621 D8, ADR 31131 D1).

SessionSetReasoningEffortResult.description:
`session/setReasoningEffort` result (tdd SS3.21). The default is durable
on ack and applies to turns launched after admission; a running turn keeps
the request options it already resolved.

SessionSettingsOverrideValue.description:
One `SessionSettingsOverrides` leaf: exactly the `settings/*` write
value domain — a string, a boolean, or `null` for clear-to-absent.

SessionSettingsOverrides.description:
FR-020: a flat settings patch for one session — dotted key paths in
file spelling verbatim (the `settings/*` key-path vocabulary) mapped
to their new absolute scalar values. `null` clears the member to
absent, exactly as a `settings/writeValue` edit does.

Credentials never travel here: a secret-shaped key (by key class, with
a fail-closed default for unrecognized secret-shaped spellings) fails
the decode at the wire boundary, before the value can reach any
settings composition.

SessionSideChatResult.description:
`session/sideChat` result (tdd SS2.5.7; ADR 45435 D2): the
`session/resume` envelope for the **new** side session, whose
`session.sideFrom` carries the provenance. The side opens empty.

history.description:
The served history (inline; SS2.5.7's empty-items half is #49416 —
inherited turns surface until the boundary-aware fold lands).

session.description: The new side session, carrying `sideFrom` provenance.

viewCursor.description: The new side session's view head.

SessionSpawnedBy.description:
Who opened a session (`Session.spawnedBy`, spec 42713 FR-69621-6, ADR
69621 D4).

parentSessionId.description:
The exact session that opened this one (ADR 69621 D2), except that any
`muse` started in a later pane of the worker's tmux session or Herdr
workspace names the worker's manager and carries the worker's
`project`/`thread` labels (ADR 69621 D8).

project.description: An opaque project label the spawner named, when it named one.

thread.description: An opaque thread label the spawner named, when it named one.

approvalMode.description:
The session's starting approval mode; server default when omitted or
explicit `null` — both spellings select the default (#23468).
Select, never create — the value names a mode the host's configuration
already defines (tdd SS2.5.1, SS5.12). This is the only surface that
declares a non-interactive run's policy (tdd SS5.11, D-008).

approvalRules.description:
The session's client-supplied shell prefix allow-rules (tdd SS5.16,
ADR 47712 D2): `{argvPrefix}` objects in the
`ShellPrefixSuggestion.argv_prefix` shape. Omitted means no client
rules. Explicit `null` is invalid params (the D-049 null-tolerant set
is closed and excludes this member); an empty array is an explicit
empty set. Until the served-handler slice, a host refuses any spelled
`approvalRules` on `session/start`/`fork`/`resume` with `-32602`;
clients omit it
(`crates/session-server/src/session/approval_rules_unserved.rs::refuse_if_spelled`).
**Experimental** (`session/start.approvalRules`).

commandId.description:
The SS2.5 idempotency handle (UUIDv7). Required; the server never
mints one.

config.description:
Reserved for future per-session overrides; only its `mcpServers` member
is admitted.

limits.description:
The SS1.10 per-session restriction (tdd SS1.10; ADR 39851-ss1-10 D2
Q1; ADR 59770 D4): the axes this session chooses, each at or below
the host ceiling. **Experimental, socket-only** (`session/start.limits`;
unopted callers are refused `-32602`, as are opted callers on hosts
with no limits regime). Absent means the default on every axis —
the daemon default for trust (untrusted, except trusted under
`--trust-workspace --listen`, ADR 59770 D4a), the daemon's own
posture for the sandbox axes (the ceiling, unless
`--allow-session-posture` widens the ceiling above it). A choice
wider than the ceiling on any axis refuses the
start `-32028 limitsAboveMax` naming every too-wide axis. An equal or
tighter choice is what the session runs and reports, with two
exceptions refused `-32602`: on a daemon whose default sandbox is
off, a start naming `sandboxEnabled: true` without `sandboxNetwork`,
or a network restriction (`restricted` or `proxy-only`) without
naming `sandboxEnabled`, until #63513 settles how a session turns the
sandbox on there, and a network restriction beside an explicit
`sandboxEnabled: false`, which never turns it on and stays refused
while #76053 is open: drop the restriction, since a sandbox-off
session has no network to restrict
(`data.reason: "tighterSandboxUnserved"` for all three); and under
`--trust-workspace --listen` without `--allow-session-posture`, an
explicit `workspaceTrusted: false`, naming the axis. Elsewhere a
network restriction beside `sandboxEnabled: false` restricts nothing:
with the sandbox off the network is not sandboxed (`sandboxNetwork`
reports `enabled`).

modelId.description: Initial model; server default when omitted.

permissionProfile.description:
The new session's initial permission profile (amendment 42624
FR-42624-1, ADR 42197 D2): a profile id the host catalog already
admits — the rows `permissionProfile/list` serves without
`sessionId`. Select, never create. Omitted means today's behavior: the
host's configured default under native admission, unchanged. An id
the catalog does not carry, or one it serves unavailable, refuses the
start `commandRejected` (-32030; `permission_profile_unknown` /
`permission_profile_unavailable`) before any durable byte, and an
ephemeral host refuses any id (`permission_profile_ephemeral_fixed`).
`session/fork` does not admit the member; `session/resume` admits it
as the launch pick (FR-42624-1, #50054). Explicit `null` is invalid
params: the set of members that tolerate `null` is
closed and excludes this one, exactly as it excludes `workspaceRoots`.

previousSessionId.description:
The `/new` predecessor link (spec 207 amendment 50054, FR-50054-1):
the outgoing session this start succeeds. Any syntactically valid
session UUID; there is no existence check, so a link to a session that
is gone still commits. Omitted means a true root. Explicit `null` is
invalid params.

providerId.description:
Initial provider routing; server default when omitted or explicit
`null` — both spellings select the default (#23468).

recoveryMode.description:
Recovery choice for this construction; omission keeps legacy behavior.
Explicit null is invalid.

sessionId.description:
Exact identity for this new root session. When omitted the server
mints a UUIDv7. This field never selects an existing session: a
retained or reserved id is rejected `commandRejected` with reason
`session_id_conflict` (tdd SS2.5.1).

spawnedBy.description:
The session that opens this one (spec 42713 FR-69621-8, ADR 69621 D7),
in the `Session.spawnedBy` shape: a spawner that starts a worker
session over MSP names its own session here. The host writes it once
into the new session's creation record, as a worker process records
its environment hand-over, and `session/list` / `session/read` serve it
back as `Session.spawnedBy`; `session/resume` never takes it.
**Additive-optional** and **provenance only** (INV-005). A value the
host cannot use (a `parentSessionId` that is not a session id, a
malformed member) records nothing and never refuses the start; an
unusable `project` or `thread` is dropped on its own. Hosts that
predate the member ignore it.

switchPolicy.description:
What happens to the `previousSessionId` predecessor's unfinished
background work (spec 207 amendment 70648, FR-70648-1, ADR 68412
D3). **Experimental** (`session/start.switchPolicy`; unopted
callers are refused `-32602`). `kill` cancels the predecessor's
unfinished work once the new start is durable, as the gate-off
`/new` does; `keep` ends its persistent monitors only. A policy
without the link is invalid params, and so is explicit `null`
(the D-049 null-tolerant set is closed and excludes this member).
Omitted means no policy: the start records `keep`, exactly as
today.

workspaceRoot.description: Absolute path, folded into the first metadata record.

workspaceRoots.description:
The session's initial runtime workspace-root set: ordered absolute
canonical existing directory paths; the first root is the CWD and
plays the primary-root role; every root receives the ADR 11237
`:workspace_roots` rules; extra roots grant no Project Trust. When
`workspaceRoot` is also present the two must name the same folder,
compared on canonical forms (the raw `workspaceRoot` is
canonicalized first; ADR 37313 D9), or the request is invalid
params, and so is explicit `null` (the D-049 null-tolerant set is
closed and excludes this member). Omitted preserves single-root
behavior (tdd SS2.5.1, ADR 37313, #37313).

worktree.description:
Ask for a created worktree or attach an existing one. **Experimental**
(`session/start.worktree`; unopted callers are refused `-32602`). Absent
means no worktree — the start proceeds exactly as today.

viewCursor.description:
The session view head after the start fold; the connection is
subscribed and receives every view event after this cursor. A
deduplicated retry returns this same result (tdd SS2.5.1).

SessionStartedParams.description:
`session/started` params (tdd SS2.6.1; enrolled by #33065): a session
became newly loaded on this host via `session/start`, `session/fork`, or
`session/sideChat` (never `session/resume` — Appendix C, OQ-F),
broadcast to every initialized connection.

The one member is the same `$defs/Session` object the
`session/start`/`session/fork` results carry, so the broadcast and the
result describe one fact through one type — the host builds the broadcast
payload as a `$defs/Session` — the fresh-start arm reuses the result's
`session` member, the start-replay arm builds the live attach snapshot —
and the emission is
parity-gated against this type at the producer
(`session-server` prod-assembly capture) and over the committed
transcript corpus (conformance `session_lifecycle_enrollment`).

session.description: The newly loaded session, as of the start/fork fold.

SessionStatusChangedParams.description:
`session/statusChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.10, ADR 31983 D2): a loaded
session's projected `(status, attention)` value flipped. A command-plane
broadcast — delivered to every connection regardless of its view
subscription set, never gated, no `sourceRange`; the same facts live on
the Session object, which is how a client seeds its table (no initial
burst on connect).

attention.description:
Attention flags after the transition; present only when at least one
flag is set (tdd SS2.4, ADR 31983 D3).

permissionState.description:
The folded effective permission state (amendment 42624 FR-42624-5) — the
same object the `Session` carries as `permissionState`. **Additive-
optional**: a loaded session carries it; a `"notLoaded"` unload frame and
an older host omit it (the `attention` precedent), and absence is unknown,
never active (INV-42624-1). A projection of the ONE stored attach face
`session/read` and the `session/list` rows serve, never a restatement.
Part of the change gate (FR-42624-5): a change in ONLY this answer — with
`(status, attention)` unchanged — is a publishable change, deduped only
when value-identical, carried on the next `session/statusChanged` frame.

status.description: Load state after the transition (the closed SS2.4 enum, unchanged).

viewCursor.description:
The causing record's view cursor (ADR 31983 D4). Required-nullable:
`null` exactly when the paired `session/closed`'s cursor is `null`
(the unload fold-failure arm); a definite cursor everywhere else.

SessionTodoListChangedParams.description:
`session/todoListChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.3): a `TodoSnapshotUpdated`
record landed. Replace the whole list on every event; an empty `items`
array is a cleared list, not a no-op.

items.description: The full todo list, replaced wholesale.

revision.description:
The snapshot revision. Diagnostics only, never an ordering guard —
`viewCursor` orders (tdd SS4.6.3).

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

sourceTool.description: The tool that produced the snapshot, verbatim.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionTokenUsageParams.description:
`session/tokenUsage` params (tdd SS4.6.5): one per model completion that
reports usage. Carries the raw counters verbatim plus the server-derived
counted-once `promptTokens`/`totalTokens` (#8803: clients display and sum
these and never re-derive the provider's cache convention) and the
session `cumulative` block. Accumulate-only: `cumulative` never goes
backward.

cumulative.description:
Session running totals at this cursor; the fold owns the
accumulation. Subagent/workflow-child usage is never folded in — it
rides the owning items (tdd SS4.6.5).

finishReason.description: Provider finish reason when reported (open vocabulary, verbatim).

modelId.description:
The effective model that produced this usage; `null` on pre-schema
records — never back-filled, an unpriced leg (tdd SS4.6.5).

promptTokens.description:
Prompt tokens counted exactly once under the provider's cache
convention (#8803). Server-derived; deterministic — the provider is
in the log.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

turnId.description: The turn whose model call completed.

usage.description: Raw counters verbatim from the durable record.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionUserShellParams.description:
`session/userShell` params (tdd SS3.9): run a user-initiated shell command
in the session's workspace — the TUI's `!` escape hatch.
**Capability-gated**: the connection must negotiate `userShell` at
`initialize`, and the whole justification is the SS1.10 spawn boundary.

SessionUserShellResult.description:
`session/userShell` result (tdd SS3.9): immediate. The shell runs off the
command worker so a long command cannot stall the command plane; the
output arrives as the `userShell` item's terminal view event.

SessionViewHealth.description:
The view-health state (tdd SS2.5.2 companion). Open enum (`x-msp-openness:
open`): a client MUST ignore an unrecognized value. `Healthy` is the
re-arm value reserved by ADR 32557 D1, emitted after a host re-load
(ADR 32557 D5, #60870);
openness still reserves additive room for the #14401 durable-degraded axis.

SessionViewHealthChangedParams.description:
`session/viewHealthChanged` params (ADR 32557; #32557): the named
session's live view stream became unavailable, and why, or (ADR 32557 D5)
it is back after the host re-loaded the view, so the client re-reads and
re-subscribes.

Best-effort: ordered after already-queued view frames and may be dropped
(for example when the connection is closing), so a client MUST NOT assume a
guaranteed push and still reads `history.noneReason` on its next
resume/read (FM-005).

health.description:
The new view-health state: `Unavailable`, or `Healthy` once the host
re-loaded a failed view (#60870).

noneReason.description:
Why the view is unavailable — the SAME typed `HistoryNoneReason`
vocabulary the pull path stamps on `history.noneReason` (tdd SS2.5.2,
D-050), so a client reuses one handler for push and pull.
`projectionUnavailable` when the view fails, then
`projectionRebuildFailed`, which the pull path never stamps: it rides
only a `session/viewHealthChanged` notification, after the host's one
re-load of a failed live view fails or right after a fork child's live
fail-close; present only when `health` is
`Unavailable`. Open on the client side: an unknown reason decodes
conservatively and renders generically.

sessionId.description: The session whose live view health changed.

SessionWorktree.description:
The Session `worktree` member (FR-31776-4, D9): path and origin only —
the branch stays in the existing `branch` member (INV-31776-2).

origin.description: Whether the host created or attached it.

path.description: Canonical worktree path the session runs in.

SettingsReadParams.description:
`settings/read` params (spec 70824 FR-022, wire half): an optional
`sessionId` addressing one session's effective values. Absent reads
the host's composed values exactly as today; in multi-tenant mode a
later slice requires it. Wire only — no serving change rides here.

sessionId.description:
The session whose effective values to answer; absent for the
host's composed values.

SettingsReadResult.description:
`settings/read` result: `{schemaVersion, values}` — the host's composed
effective values for exactly the host-owned keys (FR-43458-1, FR-43458-5).
TUI-local keys are never served.

schemaVersion.description: The settings wire schema version (`1` in this slice).

values.description:
Effective values keyed by persisted dotted key path verbatim.
Free-form (the key space grows by adding key paths), so
`JsonObject` — not `Value` — is the honest bound (the raw-log
`payload` precedent).

SettingsReadSchemaParams.description:
`settings/readSchema` params (spec 70824 FR-022, wire half): an
optional `sessionId` addressing one session's effective key shapes.
Absent reads the host's shapes exactly as today.

sessionId.description:
The session whose effective key shapes to answer; absent for the
host's shapes.

SettingsReadSchemaResult.description:
`settings/readSchema` result: `{schemaVersion, keys}` — for each
host-owned key (FR-43458-5), its allowed shape plus its enforced managed constraint
where one applies (FR-43458-4). Absent constraint means unmanaged.

keys.description:
Per-key shape entries keyed by persisted dotted key path verbatim.
Free-form like `values` above: `JsonObject` is the honest bound.

schemaVersion.description: The settings wire schema version (`1` in this slice).

keyPath.description: The persisted dotted key path verbatim.

value.description: The new absolute value, or `null` to clear the member to absent.

SettingsWriteManyParams.description:
`settings/writeMany` params: `{edits}` (FR-43458-3). All-or-nothing: one
invalid edit fails the whole call and writes nothing.

edits.description: The edits to apply atomically, in order.

sessionId.description:
The session whose patch the writes stage into (spec 70824 FR-022,
wire half); absent writes the host settings exactly as today.

results.description: The per-edit results, in edit order.

effectiveValue.description: The folded effective value after the write.

keyPath.description: The written key path, echoed verbatim.

SettingsWriteValueParams.description:
`settings/writeValue` params: `{keyPath, value}` — one persisted dotted
key path verbatim with its new absolute value (FR-43458-2). A `null`
value clears the member to absent and the built-in fallback applies, for
every key group. Values are absolute, so a retry is naturally idempotent
and the method carries no `commandId`.

keyPath.description:
The persisted dotted key path verbatim (file spelling, transmitted
as-is — a casing exemption in the `commandRejected`-reason sense,
not camelCase wire vocabulary).

sessionId.description:
The session whose patch the write stages into (spec 70824 FR-022,
wire half); absent writes the host settings exactly as today.

value.description:
The new absolute value, or `null` to clear the member to absent.
Free-form: the per-key shape is enforced at the config seam.

SettingsWriteValueResult.description:
`settings/writeValue` result: `{keyPath, effectiveValue}` — the folded
value after the write (FR-43458-2). A cleared explicit-only member
answers `null`, mirroring the `settings/read` map's absence.

effectiveValue.description: The folded effective value after the write.

keyPath.description: The written key path, echoed verbatim.

SideProvenance.description:
Side provenance folded from the durable side provenance
(`SideChatProvenance`, tdd SS2.4/SS2.5.7; ADR 45435 D2).

commandId.description: The `commandId` of the `session/sideChat` that created it.

cutCursor.description:
An **opaque provenance string** preserved verbatim from the durable
side provenance (`source_cut_cursor`). Display-only — not one of the
cursor families: clients MUST NOT parse it and no method accepts it
(tdd SS2.4).

sessionId.description: The source main session this side was opened from.

SkillActivationScope.description:
`skill/setActivation` activation target (tdd SS3.30.1). **Closed**: a
client-selected write vocabulary (ADR 45433 D2) — a write must fail a
scope the host does not implement rather than record activation against
an unknown target. Contrast the open read-side [`SkillSource`].

SkillActivationState.description:
The three-state skill activation (tdd SS3.30.1, ADR 10512 — no new
state). **Closed**: a client-selected write vocabulary (ADR 45433 D2).

SkillCatalogEntry.description:
One typed-invocable shortcut spelling (tdd SS3.22.1). A plugin skill may
contribute two rows: its bare-name winner and its qualified
`<pluginId>:<skillId>` form.

argumentHint.description: Present when the skill declares an argument hint.

displayName.description: The skill display name the first-party palette shows.

pluginId.description: The owning plugin's identifier; present when `source` is `plugin`.

selector.description:
The shortcut token without the leading slash — bare (`fix-bug`) or
plugin-qualified (`acme:deploy`) — the exact value a `skill` input
part submits. Unique within one response.

title.description:
The skill's declared human-readable name (`SKILL.md`
`metadata.display-name`), for clients to show where people read the
skill's name; absent when the skill declares none (ADR 56597 D2). The
palette keeps showing `displayName`.

SkillChangedParams.description:
`skill/changed` params (tdd SS3.22.2): the session's user-invocable set
changed; clients re-issue `skill/list`. Advisory — the host may coalesce
bursts and guarantees no ordering relative to view events (ADR 32471 D3).

SkillImportCounts.description:
The four receipt-list lengths (tdd SS3.30.2): a client renders counts
without walking lists.

SkillImportFailure.description:
One import candidate that could neither install nor quarantine (tdd
SS3.30.2): recorded so the run continues past it. `id` is null when
the candidate never yielded one — present-but-null, never omitted.

id.description: The candidate's id, or null when it never yielded one.

reason.description: Why the candidate failed.

SkillImportParams.description:
`skill/import` params (tdd SS3.30.2, #45433): import foreign skills
through the single `SkillsService::import_skills` seam.

commandId.description:
The SS3.1.1 idempotency handle (UUIDv7) — required even for
`dryRun` previews.

dryRun.description:
Preview for the consent UI; writes nothing. Additive-optional,
default false.

force.description:
Re-import over already-imported ids (the CLI `--force` twin).
Additive-optional, default false.

source.description: The foreign ecosystem to import from.

SkillImportQuarantine.description: One quarantined import candidate (tdd SS3.30.2): kept, not loaded.

SkillImportResult.description:
`skill/import` result (tdd SS3.30.2, #45433): the ack envelope plus
the service receipt projection.

failed.description:
Candidates that could neither install nor quarantine. Import never
aborts the whole run on one bad candidate.

installed.description: The ids the run installed, in pipeline order.

skipped.description:
Ids the run did not install: already-imported ids and in-run
duplicates, verbatim from the seam's `skipped` vec.

SkillImportSource.description:
`skill/import` foreign ecosystem (tdd SS3.30.2). **Closed**: a
client-selected write vocabulary (ADR 45433 D2) — a write must fail an
ecosystem the host does not implement rather than import from an
unknown dir. The host resolves its own foreign dir (the
`foreign_skills_sources` derivation); no client paths cross the wire.

SkillInvocationSource.description:
A `skill` input part's picked-copy source (tdd SS3.22.3; ADR 32471
D12): the D2 catalog-row `source` enum values, sent by the TUI on every
skill submit so the host resolves the exact `(selector, source)` row.
**Closed**: a client-selected write vocabulary (ADR 45433 D2) — an
unknown value is `invalidParams`, never a fall-through to the bare row.
Contrast the open read-side [`SkillSource`].

SkillListParams.description:
`skill/list` params (tdd SS3.22.1, SS3.30.3). Per-session because skill
scope follows the session's workspace and plugin state.

SkillListResult.description:
`skill/list` result (tdd SS3.22.1): one row per typed-invocable shortcut
spelling — exactly the invocations the first-party typed dispatch accepts
(spec 11352 INV-007 predicate and the shared shortcut layer's name
resolution, both by call-through; ADR 32471 D2).

SkillSetActivationParams.description:
`skill/setActivation` params (tdd SS3.30.1, #45433): turn one skill on
or off in any scope through the single
`SkillsService::set_activation` seam.

selector.description:
Names one skill: a bare or plugin-qualified token from the session's
full catalog (tdd SS3.30.3), the SS3.22.1 row vocabulary.

SkillSetActivationResult.description:
`skill/setActivation` result (tdd SS3.30.1, #45433): the ack envelope
plus the applied state.

previous.description:
The activation value in force for that `(selector, scope)`
immediately before the write: the same value a full-catalog
`skill/list` row would have carried in `activation` for it.

SkillSource.description:
A skill row's source scope (tdd SS3.22.1): the projection of the skills
crate's `SkillsSourceScope`. Open (server-produced result vocabulary,
the #22785 enum-openness rule): a future scope value is additive.

SnapshotAnchor.description: The compaction boundary an anchored snapshot is anchored at (tdd SS2.5.2).

boundaryCursor.description: The view cursor of the boundary's `compaction` event.

summarizedThrough.description: The boundary's opaque compaction anchor (tdd SS4.5.10).

SnapshotState.description:
The complete folded view at the snapshot cursor (tdd SS4.9.1).

Additive-optional evolution applies exactly as everywhere else; unknown
members MUST be ignored, and preserved if re-serialized.

activeTurn.description: The running foreground turn; `null` when none is running.

approvalMode.description:
The effective approval mode at this cursor — the same object the
`Session` carries (tdd SS2.4, SS5.12).

branch.description: Latest branch observation; `null` when no fact has landed.

contextUsage.description:
The latest `(windowTokens, usedTokens, pressure)` triple. The protocol
allows "`null`/absent" and its worked example OMITS the member; the
binary omits it too, so this is the absent arm — the four siblings above
are present-null in the same frame. A member is published as one or the
other, never both.

effectiveModel.description: Latest effective model; `null` when no fact has landed.

goal.description: Latest goal block; `null` when no fact has landed.

items.description:
Every item, in first-opened order, each at its latest revision at the
snapshot cursor. One schema per kind, shared with the notification
item object — which is what makes snapshot+suffix a pure splice
(tdd SS4.9.1).

monitorInbox.description:
The retained Monitor admissions at this cursor (tdd SS4.9.1,
FR-56492-7 as amended by #76729): every admission still awaiting
delivery, plus per task the newest 200 non-blank stdout lines and the
newest other admission, delivered or not, each with its drain and void
stamps; a pending cut of the history ladder (tdd SS2.5.2, ADR 56492 D4)
carries only the entries still awaiting delivery. A current host always
sends it (empty when no monitor admitted anything); absent means an
older host.

name.description:
The settled canonical session name; `null` when the session was never
named (#27598, tdd SS4.9.1 / SS2.14). Folds the same durable
`session/nameChanged` record `Session.name` reports.

pendingApprovals.description: The pending-approval half of the pending set.

pendingUserInputs.description: The pending-user-input half of the pending set.

queuedTurns.description: Admitted-but-not-launched submits, in launch order (tdd SS3.1.4).

reasoningEffort.description:
The latest session-default reasoning effort with its source; ABSENT
until a set lands (tdd SS4.9.1 `reasoningEffort`, ADR 31255 D1 — the
`contextUsage` absent arm, never present-null).

todoList.description: Latest todo list; `null` when no fact has landed.

tokenUsage.description:
The `cumulative` block of the last `session/tokenUsage` event; zeroes
when none (tdd SS4.9.1).

SourceRange.description:
The inclusive raw-record range a durable-sourced view event folded from
(tdd SS4.2) — the reconciliation token: re-folding the cited records from
the canonical fold state immediately before `first` — appended host-death
terminals seed from the end-of-records state — reproduces the event
(tdd SS7.5; spec 14653 T041/INV-009). In v1 it is an **opaque provenance
token**: no wire method reads what it points at (the SS6 raw-log altitude
is deferred, #13929).

Ephemeral-sourced events (`item/delta`, and an `item/started` that opens
on an ephemeral record) carry no `sourceRange` — ephemeral records may be
evicted by retention (tdd SS4.2; spec 14653 INV-009).

first.description: The first record of the inclusive range.

last.description:
The last record of the inclusive range; equal to `first` for an event
folded from one record.

stream.description:
The stream the folded records live on (run stream, or the session
stream's mirror of task/approval/subagent-control records — whichever
the fold actually consumed, tdd SS4.2).

StatusAttempt.description:
`toolCall.statusAttempt` (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448): the latest
`TaskExternalAttemptDetail`, field-for-field — countdown inputs the
client renders the tick from, so no event spam.

errorKind.description: The error kind (durable vocabulary, verbatim), when recorded.

nextAttempt.description: The scheduled next attempt, when known.

retryDelayMs.description: The retry delay in ms, when known.

level.description: The health level (the durable `TaskHealthLevel` vocabulary verbatim).

reason.description: The reason, when recorded.

StatusHealthLevel.description:
`toolCall.statusHealth.level` (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448): the durable
`TaskHealthLevel` vocabulary verbatim. Open — runtime vocabulary may
grow additively, and clients MUST render unknown levels generically.

StopFailure.description:
The known owner failure (D7): the failed/unconfirmed owner count and
the first canonical owner reason for the singular/plural Error row.

firstReason.description: The first canonical owner reason; an open string.

StopProgress.description:
Authoritative Stop selection progress (D7). `selectedCount` counts
logical groups (fixed); `endedCount` advances only on proven cleanup.

endedCount.description: Groups with proven terminal and cleanup.

StreamRef.description: One raw stream named by a [`SourceRange`] (tdd SS4.2).

kind.description:
The stream kind, verbatim raw-log vocabulary (e.g. `"run"`,
`"session"`). A free string, not an enum: `sourceRange` is an opaque
provenance token in v1 and the raw stream vocabulary is the deferred
SS6 altitude's to freeze (#13929).

SubagentControlStatus.description:
Subagent control status (tdd SS4.5.7, camelCased
`SubagentControlStatus`). Open; the generic item `status` is the terminal
authority.

SubagentInputParams.description:
Params for `subagent/sendMessage` and `subagent/followupTask` (SS3.16):
a child target plus the input body.

body.description:
The note/task text: trimmed with Unicode-whitespace semantics,
rejected when empty after trimming, delivered trimmed with multibyte
content byte-for-byte intact (SS3.16).

subagentId.description: Durable child id (the SS4.5.7 item's `subagentId`; opaque string).

SubagentInputPhase.description:
`subagentInput.inputPhase` (#70249): the record the item stands for.
Open: a client ignores an item whose phase it does not know.

SubagentListParams.description:
`subagent/list` params: the session whose subagent roster to read. A
read-only query in the `skill/list` mold: no `commandId`, no durable
record, no view event. Served by the loaded parent's runtime control
records, so its refusals (`-32020`/`-32021`/`-32022`/`-32024`, plus a retryable
`-32603` when the runtime source declines) are the `task/list` split.

sessionId.description: The target session (the parent whose children to list).

SubagentListResult.description:
`subagent/list` result: the session's roster rows. Empty only when the
parent's control records name no durable child; a declined source
refuses typed instead of answering empty.

subagents.description: The session's roster rows, ordered by `(agentPath, subagentId)`.

SubagentOwnerReasonParams.description:
Params for `subagent/interrupt`, `subagent/stop`, and `subagent/close`
(SS3.16): a child target plus an optional human-readable reason that is
preserved on the durable effect record.

reason.description: Optional reason, preserved on the durable owner-command record.

subagentId.description: Durable child id (the SS4.5.7 item's `subagentId`; opaque string).

drained.description:
`true` once the parent consumed the result (the inbox join fact the
gate-off drain arm folds into the `Finished` marker — tdd SS4.5.7).
Absent otherwise; never cleared once set. Clients mint the
`Finished` marker off this flag instead of re-deriving the join; a
client that knows `subagentResult` (tdd SS4.5.26) draws one
`Finished` member per consumed result instead, and keeps drawing from
this flag for a child with no such item, as on a host before the kind
(#88809).

errorKind.description: Error kind, verbatim durable vocabulary, when the child failed.

structuredData.description: Structured result data, verbatim, when present.

summary.description:
Result summary, bounded on the wire at the 64 KiB retained-text budget
(tdd SS4.5.4 and SS4.5.7, ADR 35691 D9); a cut sets the item's
`truncated`. The durable record stays verbatim.

text.description:
Result text, when present, bounded on the wire at the same 64 KiB
budget (ADR 35691 D9); a cut sets the item's `truncated`.

SubagentResultStatus.description:
`subagentResult.resultStatus` (#88809): the consumed attempt's outcome.
Absent when the host had not seen that attempt's result envelope at the
drain; a client then shows the child's current outcome (ADR 88809 D2).
Open: a client treats a value it does not know as an absent member.

SubagentRosterEntry.description:
One roster row: a durable child's identity, place, and state, projected
from its control records. Rows carry no result content — the transcript
stays on the child session / `subagent/readResult`.

agentPath.description: The agent definition path (`agent_path`), verbatim from the spawn.

childSessionId.description:
The child's own session id, readable via `session/read`/`view/page`.
**Additive-optional**: absent until the child's start is attested.

controlStatus.description:
The child's control status: `Accepted` at spawn, then the latest
`StatusUpdated` / `Closed` / `ResultReady` / `RecoveryAvailable` /
`RecoveryDecision` (`Accepted | Starting | Running | ResultReady |
Closing | Closed | RecoveryPending | ManualReconciliation`).

definitionName.description:
The granted definition's name (`definition_grant_audit`
`definition_name`). **Additive-optional**: absent on spawns without
a grant audit (historical records). The resolved definition id is
not persisted on the spawn record, so the name is what the roster
can truthfully carry.

depth.description: The spawn depth (1 = a root-session child).

durationMs.description:
The child's observed wall-clock duration in ms, when the runtime
observed one. **Additive-optional**: absent until first observation.

name.description:
The child's display name: the spawn `description`, falling back to
the spawn `role`. **Additive-optional**: absent when neither carries
one; never parsed from `agentPath`.

objective.description:
The spawn objective. **Additive-optional**: absent when the spawn
carried none.

parentPath.description:
The parent row's `agentPath`. **Additive-optional**: absent whenever
`parentSubagentId` is.

parentSubagentId.description:
The parent's `subagentId`: the roster row whose child session issued
this child's spawn. **Additive-optional**: absent when the parent is
the root session, or when the parent row is not in the roster or not
yet attested — never guessed, never derived from `agentPath`.

resultReady.description:
Whether the child's latest attempt's result is ready (a
`ResultReady` for the latest admitted attempt seen).

role.description:
The spawn role. **Additive-optional**: absent when the spawn
carried none.

subagentId.description:
The durable child identity (`subagent_id`). Rows without one are not
roster rows: a rejected spawn names no child.

terminalReason.description:
The terminal reason: the result envelope's `errorKind` when present,
else the cancel outcome's `reason`. **Additive-optional**: absent on
live rows and on terminals that carry no reason — never fabricated
from the close outcome's status word.

workflowRunId.description:
The owning dynamic workflow run id, when the child was
workflow-admitted. **Additive-optional**: absent for native spawns.

SubagentTargetParams.description:
Params for `subagent/resume`, `subagent/reopen`, and
`subagent/readResult` (SS3.16): the bare child target.

subagentId.description: Durable child id (the SS4.5.7 item's `subagentId`; opaque string).

SubmittedToolCall.description:
One call of a submitted batch: the `callId`, `tool` and `args` its
`toolCall` item carries once it starts, so a client matches the two by
`callId`.

SubscriptionUsage.description:
The one usage payload shape: the `usage/read` result's `usage` member and
the `usage/changed` params (ADR 32563 D2/D3). The numbers are
point-in-time — `observedAtMs` is the host's arrival stamp, so a client
renders "as of", never implies live data (spec 18742 US-FR-004).

observedAtMs.description:
When the host RECEIVED this observation (frame arrival or mint
request-send), epoch milliseconds.

tier.description: The provider's subscription tier id, verbatim.

SubscriptionUsageWeekly.description:
The rolling weekly block: same semantics as
[`SubscriptionUsageWindow`] without a duration (ADR 32563 D2).

resetsAtMs.description: When the weekly window resets, epoch milliseconds.

usedPercent.description: Percent of the weekly budget used (integer ≥ 0, may exceed 100).

SubscriptionUsageWindow.description:
The current usage window (the provider's 5-hour-class block): verbatim
provider percentages with the reset stamp normalized to epoch
milliseconds (ADR 32563 D2).

resetsAtMs.description: When the window resets, epoch milliseconds.

usedPercent.description:
Percent of the window's budget used: an integer ≥ 0, verbatim from
the provider — over-quota values above 100 are valid.

result.description:
Always a JSON object, possibly `{}`, never a bare scalar — so every
result can grow additive-optional members (SS1.2).

SwitchPolicy.description:
What happens to the `previousSessionId` predecessor's unfinished
background work. **Closed**: the client selects one of the two policies
the host applies.

TaskBackgroundParams.description:
`task/background` params (tdd §3.13): durably send a running foreground
tool task to the background.

taskId.description:
The task to background, exactly as the view names it: the `toolCall`
item's `itemId` IS the task id (SS4.5.5).

TaskCommandResult.description:
The `task/background` / `task/stop` ack (tdd §3.13/§3.14): admission-only,
echoing the targeted task.

TaskExecutionMode.description:
A task row's execution mode (tdd SS3.31, ADR 62268 D2). Open
(server-produced result vocabulary, the #22785 enum-openness rule):
clients MUST ignore unknown modes.

TaskListEntry.description:
One task inventory row (tdd SS3.31). The row is the stable
contract: `kind` and `status` stay open so a future state extends them
without breaking clients.

backgroundInitiator.description:
Who backgrounded the task, mirroring the item field.
**Additive-optional**: absent on pre-split records and
registry-only rows, never inferred.

command.description:
The raw command text: the joined `toolCall` item's `command`
argument verbatim (ADR 62268 D2). **Additive-optional**:
omitted when the row has no item or the item carries no
command. Monitors join raw — clients redact (INV-17544-6).

executionMode.description:
`"foreground" | "background"` (ADR 62268 D2).
**Additive-optional**: absent means `"background"` (only
pre-change hosts omit it, and those list background rows only);
never guessed.

kind.description:
What the workload is: `"tool"` or `"tool.*"` for item rows (the
recorded kind when the registry records one, else `"tool"`); the
recorded registry kind string verbatim for registry-only rows.
Open vocabulary — clients MUST ignore unknown kinds. A `String`,
not an enum: registry kind strings are unbounded.

startedAt.description:
The host-known task start, RFC3339. **Additive-optional**: omitted,
never guessed, when the host does not know it.

status.description:
`"inProgress"` — the only value at this increment, since every
listed row is non-terminal by construction.

taskId.description:
The `toolCall` item's `itemId` for item rows; the runtime registry
id for registry-only rows.

tool.description:
The short tool name on item-visible tool rows only; never a label,
never arguments. **Additive-optional**: absent elsewhere.

TaskListParams.description:
`task/list` params (tdd SS3.31): the session whose background-task
inventory to read. A read-only query in the `skill/list` mold: no
`commandId`, no durable record, no view event.

TaskListResult.description:
`task/list` result (tdd SS3.31): one row per live workload,
background and foreground (ADR 62268 D1), oldest first; empty when
nothing is running.

TaskListStatus.description:
A task row's status (tdd SS3.31). Open (server-produced result
vocabulary, the #22785 enum-openness rule): a future state is
additive, and clients MUST ignore unknown statuses.

TaskReadTailParams.description:
`task/readTail` params (ADR 70076 D1, experimental): the latest output of
one running background command, read from the host runtime's retained
tail. A read-only query in the `task/list` mold: no `commandId`, no
durable record, no view event.

taskId.description:
The task: a `task/list` row's `taskId`, which for a command is its
`toolCall` item's `itemId`.

tail.description:
The command's latest output, at most [`TASK_READ_TAIL_MAX_BYTES`]
cut at a character boundary, with invalid UTF-8 replaced. Raw
terminal text: clients sanitize it before display. Absent when the
session holds no output tail for the task: an unknown task, a task
that is not a command, or an ended command whose tail the runtime
released.

TaskStopAllParams.description:
`task/stopAll` params (tdd §3.15): stop every stoppable background
workload live at admission.

TaskStopAllResult.description:
The `task/stopAll` ack (tdd §3.15): always `accepted`, including over an
empty set — a blanket stop over nothing is a satisfied gesture. The ack
deliberately carries no stopped-task list; count the kills from the view.

TaskStopParams.description:
`task/stop` params (tdd §3.14): stop one named background task. Required
target, never "whichever is loudest" — §3.15 is the blanket verb.

taskId.description: The task to stop, the `toolCall` item's `itemId` (SS4.5.5).

activeForm.description: Present-tense active form, when the tool supplied one.

TodoListState.description: The latest todo-list fact in the snapshot (tdd SS4.6.3, SS4.9.1).

revision.description: The snapshot revision. Diagnostics only, never an ordering guard.

sourceTool.description: The tool that produced the snapshot, verbatim.

TodoStatus.description: Todo status (tdd SS4.6.3): closed in the runtime, wire-open.

TokenUsage.description:
Raw token counters, verbatim from the durable record (tdd SS4.6.5, the
runtime's `Usage`, camelCased). Not directly summable across providers —
sum the counted-once derivations instead (#8803).

cacheReadTokens.description: Cache read tokens, only when the provider distinguishes writes/reads.

cacheWriteTokens.description:
Cache write tokens, only when the provider distinguishes
writes/reads.

cachedTokens.description:
Provider-reported cache tokens (inside or beside `inputTokens`,
provider-convention-dependent — the reason `promptTokens` exists).

reasoningTokens.description: Output tokens spent on reasoning, when the provider reports it.

ToolDisplayLabel.description:
`toolCall.displayLabel`: the call's words in three forms, each one line of
plain text, always present together. The item's `status` picks the form.

active.description: Shown while the call runs (`inProgress`), e.g. "Setting up Computer Use".

done.description: Shown after the call succeeds (`completed`), e.g. "Set up Computer Use".

neutral.description:
Shown for every other status (failed, rejected, timed out, cancelled),
beside that status; never implies success.

ToolReceiptOperation.description:
Which operation within the family the receipt describes (ADR 43399
D1/D2). Open — registered per family, never derived from the tool name.

ToolReceiptOutcome.description:
What the operation did (ADR 43399 D1/D2). Open, and a **single shared
vocabulary**: a value appearing in two families means the same thing in
both, which is why the permitted `status` values are bound to the value
here rather than per family.

TraceContext.description:
Optional W3C trace context, on requests in both directions only — never on
responses or notifications (SS1.8).

traceparent.description: W3C `traceparent` string; receivers that do not trace ignore it.

TurnCancelParams.description:
`turn/cancel` params (tdd SS3.5): plain cancellation on the normal command
lane. Same shape as `turn/interrupt`, **without** `retract` — pairing a
retract with a plain cancel is durably rejected `not_paired_interrupt`.

turnId.description:
The exact turn to cancel; omit to target the current foreground turn.
Any syntactically valid UUID: a turn from an older session may carry a
v4 or v5 id. A malformed id is `invalidParams`.
The cancelled turn.

TurnCompletedParams.description:
`turn/completed` params (tdd SS4.5.1): the run's durable terminal record
landed.

byClient.description:
The client whose wire stop was the first one accepted for this turn,
when a wire stop ended it and its client was recorded (ADR 73001 D4).
Absent otherwise, including on older logs.

durationMs.description: Turn duration; absent means unmeasured, never fabricated.

error.description:
Present when `terminal` is `"failed"`, except on a synthesized
host-death terminal, which carries `reason` instead (tdd SS4.5.1,
ADR 36635 D2): mid-turn failures reach the client here — never as a
JSON-RPC error.

reason.description:
The runtime's free-text terminal reason, verbatim. Display and
diagnostics only; never branch on it.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

timeToFirstTokenMs.description: Time to first token, when measured.

turnId.description: The terminated turn.

usage.description:
The turn's aggregate token usage, summed across the turn's model
completions (same shape as `session/tokenUsage.usage`).

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnError.description:
The settled turn-failure object (tdd SS4.5.1): `{kind, message,
retryable}`.

kind.description:
The failure class (open camelCase enum grounded in the runtime's
terminal failure classification).

quota.description:
Typed quota-exhaustion detail (ADR 50047 D2/D3): present iff the
stopping failure was the quota class. Clients branch on presence,
never by parsing `message`.

requestDenied.description:
`true` when the provider refused this request. Present only on the
live `turn/completed`: replayed, snapshot-served and `workflow/resume`
terminals omit it, so absence does not mean the request was not
denied. Never `false`. (ADR 39289 D2/D3)

retryable.description: The server's judgment that resubmitting the same input may succeed.

TurnErrorKind.description:
Turn failure classes (tdd SS4.5.1, `TerminalErrorKind` plus the
model-task failure class). Open.

TurnForegroundCompletedParams.description:
`turn/foregroundCompleted` params (tdd SS4.5.12): the turn's foreground
work is done and named background reminder checks hold the turn open.
Explicitly non-terminal: the turn ends only at `turn/completed` /
`turn/unqueued`.

blockingAgents.description:
`reminderAgentId`s of the firing's blocking set, never empty; agent
ids, never display names. Live-best-effort: reads, resume, and
replay may narrow it to the linked subset.

sourceRange.description:
The durable records this event folded from, anchored at the first
blocking link of the firing window.

turnId.description: The turn whose foreground completed.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnInputPart.description:
One ordered content part of a turn submission (tdd SS3.2). File mentions
are text, not a part type: write `@relative/path` in a text part. A
structured `mention` part is reserved and currently rejected, and an
unknown part type is `invalidParams` (tdd SS3.1.2, SS3.2) — which is what
closes [`TurnInputPartType`].

Modelled as a discriminated flat object rather than a Rust `enum`, the
convention [`crate::view::approval::ApprovalSubject`] already established
for a wire union in this crate: the v1 schema model names no
object-variant union shape and fails closed on one. The serialized JSON is
the same either way; what a flat object cannot express is "`mediaType` is
required exactly when `type` is `image`".

arguments.description:
Free-text skill arguments, optional on a `skill` part — the wire twin
of what the TUI accepts after the shortcut token (tdd SS3.22.3).

base64Data.description:
Base64 payload, required on an `image` part. Invalid base64 or an
empty payload is rejected with invalid params.

clientRef.description:
The client's own name for this image, optional on an `image` part
(tdd SS3.2, ADR 78319 D2): `{ "name" }`, 1 to 256 bytes of UTF-8 with
no character restriction; an empty or longer name is invalid params.
Other part types ignore it. Returned verbatim in
`session/resume.unavailableInputAssets` and the lost-image marker
once the host records it. **Experimental** (`TurnInputPart.clientRef`).

height.description:
Pixel height; must be provided together with `width` or not at all
(tdd SS3.2, #22785 E6c).

mediaType.description: Media type, required on an `image` part.

selector.description:
The skill to invoke, required on a `skill` part (tdd SS3.2, SS3.22.3;
ADR 32471 D4): a bare or plugin-qualified shortcut token from
`skill/list`. The HOST resolves and expands; an unknown selector is
the typed `-32032 skillNotFound` request error.

source.description:
The picked copy's source, optional on a `skill` part: one of the catalog
rows' `source` values. When present the host resolves the exact
`(selector, source)` row; when absent it resolves the selector, bare or
plugin-qualified, against the session's skill catalog, as the TUI
shortcut does. Closed: an unknown value is `invalidParams`, never a
fall-through.

text.description:
User prompt text, on a `text` part. Multiple text parts are joined in
order into the turn's prompt.

uploadId.description:
The upload receipt, required on a `video` part (tdd SS3.2, SS3.33;
ADR 45443 D5): the client-minted id `media/upload` echoed.

width.description:
Pixel width; must be provided together with `height` or not at all.
Published as a `dependentRequired` pair.

TurnInputPartType.description:
The `type` discriminator of a turn input part (tdd SS3.2). Closed: an
unknown part type is `invalidParams` (tdd SS3.1.2).

TurnInterruptParams.description:
`turn/interrupt` params (tdd SS3.4): the "user pressed stop" gesture, on
the runtime's priority lane.

retract.description:
Pair a retract intent with the interrupt: if the turn is cancelled
before any assistant output committed, the submission is durably
retracted (view event `turn/retracted`) so the client may restore the
prompt text. A rejected retract does not undo the interrupt. Default
`false` (tdd SS3.4).

turnId.description:
The exact turn to interrupt. Omit to target the session's current
foreground turn, resolved at admission; prefer passing the explicit id
when you have one (tdd SS3.4). Any syntactically valid UUID: a turn
from an older session may carry a v4 or v5 id. A malformed id is
`invalidParams`.

TurnInterruptResult.description:
`turn/interrupt` result (tdd SS3.4). Acceptance means the interrupt was
admitted, **not** that the turn is already stopped: the turn is over when
you fold its `turn/completed` with terminal `cancelled`.

turnId.description: The interrupted turn.

TurnModelAttemptStartedParams.description:
`turn/modelAttemptStarted` params (tdd SS4.5.1; ADR
`68644-model-attempt-started` D1): a turn's model provider task recorded
its opening status — one model attempt is starting (before the provider
dials), retries and later model steps included. Clients raise their
thinking state here, the point a switch-off TUI flips on model-task
activity. Non-terminal: it never resolves a turn-wait. `sourceRange`
cites the session stream's mirror of the task-lifecycle record (tdd
SS4.2).

sourceRange.description:
The durable record this event folded from (the session stream's
mirror of the model task's opening status; `first == last`).

turnId.description: The running turn whose model attempt is starting.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnModelRetryScheduledParams.description:
`turn/modelRetryScheduled` params (tdd SS4.5.1; ADR
`50047-model-retry-scheduled-members` D1): a durable model-stream
retry-scheduled fact folded — the provider backoff behind one model
attempt is observable BEFORE the turn terminates, so a streaming
client can render "system words · retrying in Ss · attempt N/M"
instead of dead air. Non-terminal: it never resolves a turn-wait.
The sibling `turn/retryScheduled` shape at the model layer: same
member names and semantics (attempt/nextAttempt/maxAttempts/
retryDelayMs/system/errorKind/httpStatus), minus `reason` — the
row's words derive from `errorKind` through the shared gate-off
mapping, and the recorded machine message is not user text. The
delay is the recorded scheduled backoff, never an absolute fire
time — clients derive any countdown locally. `sourceRange` cites
the session stream's mirror of the task-lifecycle record (tdd SS4.2).

errorKind.description:
The failing model attempt's durable kind, verbatim (ADR 50047
D2) — a plain string: the durable vocabulary is open-ended.

httpStatus.description: The failing model attempt's HTTP status (ADR 50047 D2).

nextAttempt.description:
The scheduled model attempt (producer contract: attempt <
nextAttempt <= maxAttempts; not a schema constraint).

retryDelayMs.description:
The scheduled backoff delay in milliseconds, verbatim from the
durable fact.

sourceRange.description:
The durable record this event folded from (the session stream's
mirror of the scheduled model task status; `first == last`).

system.description:
The failing model attempt's provider system, verbatim
(ADR 50047 D2) — e.g. `"meta"`. Always present from this producer
(the durable `system` is a required `String`); optional on the wire
so a future omission folds absent instead of failing the frame.

turnId.description: The running turn whose model attempt is being retried.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnRef.description: A turn named by the snapshot's active/queued lists (tdd SS4.9.1).

commandId.description: The `commandId` of the submit that minted it.

displayText.description:
`queuedTurns[]` only (#45455; ADR 45443 D7): the queued submit's
presentation text, so a late joiner can render it without waiting for
launch. A current host sets it on every entry it admits; absent means
an older host (or a pre-feature restored entry). Never set on
`activeTurn`: the running turn's text is its `userMessage` item.

truncated.description:
`queuedTurns[]` only: set when `displayText` was cut to the
committed-surface budget, mirroring `userMessage.truncated`
(tdd SS4.5.2). Absent unless `true`.

turnId.description: The turn's id, minted at admission.

TurnRetractedParams.description:
`turn/retracted` params (tdd SS4.5.1): an interrupt-paired retract
durably settled, accepted or declined (ADR 50074 D1). On `"accepted"`
the retracted user-message item is re-emitted via `item/updated` with
`retracted: true`; on `"declined"` the client folds the legacy declined
rollback instead and no item is re-emitted.

outcome.description:
The retract settlement outcome (tdd SS4.5.1, ADR 50074 D1).
Additive-optional: absent reads as `"accepted"` — pre-feature hosts
emit the event only for accepted retracts — and so does an
unrecognized value (open enum, D-033).

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

turnId.description: The turn whose submission was retracted.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnRetryScheduledParams.description:
`turn/retryScheduled` params (tdd SS4.5.1, spec 14412; D-026): a durable
turn retry-scheduled fact folded — the failing model attempt's scheduled
retry is observable BEFORE the turn terminates, so a streaming client can
render "attempt N/M · retrying in Ss · reason" instead of dead air.
Non-terminal: it never resolves a turn-wait (tdd SS3.1.4). The delay is
the recorded scheduled backoff, never an absolute fire time — clients
derive any countdown locally. `sourceRange` cites the session stream's
mirror of the task-lifecycle record (tdd SS4.2).

errorKind.description:
The failing model attempt's durable kind, verbatim (ADR 50047
D2/D3) — a plain string: the durable vocabulary is open-ended.

httpStatus.description: The failing model attempt's HTTP status (ADR 50047 D2/D3).

nextAttempt.description:
The attempt about to run (producer contract: attempt < nextAttempt
<= maxAttempts; not a schema constraint).

reason.description:
The recorded stopping reason through the shared task-detail
normalization (non-empty; capped at 160 characters).

retryDelayMs.description:
The scheduled backoff delay in milliseconds, verbatim from the
durable fact.

sourceRange.description:
The durable record this event folded from (the session stream's
mirror of the retry-scheduled task status; `first == last`).

system.description:
The failing model attempt's provider system, verbatim
(ADR 50047 D2/D3) — e.g. `"meta"`. Absent when no model-attempt
facet precedes the retry status on the task (old logs).

turnId.description: The running turn whose model attempt is being retried.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnStartDisposition.description:
What `turn/start` did with the input (tdd SS3.2). Resolves OQ-H in v1:
since `queue` is the default `ifBusy`, clients need to distinguish these
without folding history.

TurnStartParams.description:
`turn/start` params (tdd SS3.2).

`turn/start.providerRequestOptions` is deliberately absent: **RULED
(#22785 E3, owner, 2026-08-26) to stay off the published schema.** The
schema is the contract, and a free-form-object node kind is revisited only
if the experimental field graduates.

commandId.description:
The SS3.1.1 idempotency handle (UUIDv7). The fresh turn's `turnId`
derives from it (tdd SS3.1.4).

displayText.description:
Presentation form of the prompt for transcripts. Durable; carried on
the resulting user-message view item. Never model-visible (tdd SS3.2).

ifBusy.description: Disposition when a turn is already running; default `queue`.

input.description: Ordered content parts; required and non-empty.

reasoningEffort.description: Reasoning tier sampled at submission for this turn.

tokenBudget.description:
This turn's token budget in tokens: an integer floor of 1, riding to
workflow-launch admission and inert when no workflow launches. Omitted
means no budget; 0 or a non-integer is invalid params, as is explicit
`null`. No wire upper bound beyond the integer type. Experimental: only
the name and shape are settled, not v1 membership, so the member ships
off the stable bundle until it graduates.

userShell.description:
A queued `!` shell action riding this turn (tdd SS3.2, ADR 50034):
the `!cmd` typed while a turn runs, executed at the next
model-call boundary before any later steer. Exclusive with `text`
and `skill` input; `input` may be empty only when this member is
present. Capability-gated on `userShell`: a carrying turn on a
connection without the grant fails `-32010 capabilityRequired`.
Explicit `null` is invalid params (the null-tolerant set is
closed). A v1 stable member.

workspaceRoots.description:
A sticky REPLACEMENT of the session's runtime workspace-root set,
binding at this turn's launch and persisting for subsequent turns
until replaced again — unlike `reasoningEffort`, which is
this-turn-only. Same shape and validation as
`session/start.workspaceRoots`; invalid params on an explicit
`ifBusy: "steer"` submit and so is explicit `null` (the D-049
null-tolerant set is closed); omitted means "unchanged", never
"reset" (tdd SS3.2, ADR 37313 D3, #37313).

queuedAtUs.description:
`queued` and `steered` (#72279, #80837): the queued input
record's `recorded_at` in Unix microseconds — the host clock the
client's optimistic row must sort by, so the row lands where the
host's queue holds it. Present on a fresh queued or steered
admission via the enqueue arm (both append an inbox record);
absent on `started`, on hosts that predate the member, on
post-restart recovery replays (D2 exception), on the replace and
park arms' Queued acks, and on unopted connections (stripped per
SS1.5.1). A client that sees no member falls back to its wall
clock (today's behavior).

startedNewTurn.description:
`true` iff `disposition` is `started`; retained as the boolean
shorthand — `disposition` is authoritative (tdd SS3.2).

turnId.description:
The turn that will carry (or absorbed) this input. Authoritative:
always take it from the ack rather than deriving it (tdd SS3.2).

TurnStartedParams.description:
`turn/started` params (tdd SS4.5.1): a foreground turn began running —
fresh submits immediately, queued submits at their launch boundary, never
steered submits.

commandId.description:
The submitting command; `turnId == commandId` for fresh turns (tdd
SS3.1.4).

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

turnId.description: The started turn.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnSteerParams.description:
`turn/steer` params (tdd SS3.3): exact-target steering into the currently
running turn.

expectedTurnId.description:
The turn you believe is running. Closes the race where the turn
completes or is replaced between your read and your steer: input meant
for turn A can never leak into turn B (tdd SS3.3). Any syntactically
valid UUID: a turn from an older session may carry a v4 or v5 id. A
malformed id is `invalidParams`; an id that is not the running turn is
refused.

reasoningEffort.description:
Reasoning tier for the model calls this steer's input reaches. Applies
forward, never backward; absent means unspecified, not "reset"
(tdd SS3.3, D-024).

tokenBudget.description:
This steer's token budget in tokens. Same vocabulary as the
`turn/start` member: an integer floor of 1, omitted means
unspecified (never a reset of the running turn's budget), 0 or a
non-integer is invalid params, as is explicit `null` (tdd SS3.3,
ADR 45443 D6). Experimental like its twin: v1 membership stays
open, so the member ships off the stable bundle until a v1
ruling graduates it.

turnId.description: The running turn that absorbed the input.

TurnTerminal.description:
Turn terminal vocabulary (tdd SS4.5.1): exactly the runtime's
`RunTerminalKind` — closed in the runtime, wire-open for evolution.

TurnToolBatchSubmittedParams.description:
`turn/toolBatchSubmitted` params: one model tool-call batch of two or more
calls at submission. Ephemeral-sourced like `item/delta`, so it has **no**
`sourceRange`: it is never journaled and never paged back.

calls.description: Every call of the batch, in model order.

turnId.description: The turn whose model response submitted the batch.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnUnqueueParams.description:
`turn/unqueue` params (tdd SS3.6): reclaim a queued submit before it
launches. It is **not** a stop — a reclaim that arrives after its target
launched is durably rejected, never silently upgraded into a cancel.

turnId.description:
The queued turn to reclaim, exactly as the queueing `turn/start`'s ack
minted it and as snapshot `queuedTurns` lists it. Required, and never
"whichever is newest" (tdd SS3.6). Any syntactically valid UUID: a
turn from an older session may carry a v4 or v5 id. A malformed id is
`invalidParams`.

TurnUnqueueResult.description:
`turn/unqueue` result (tdd SS3.6). Admission only — but for this command
admission *is* the race: an admitted reclaim implies the turn will not
launch. The authoritative removal is the `turn/unqueued` view event.

turnId.description: The reclaimed turn.

TurnUnqueuedParams.description:
`turn/unqueued` params (tdd SS3.6, SS4.5.1): a queued submit's reclaim
durably won; its pre-minted turn never runs. Carries the reclaimed
`turnId` and the `commandId` of the `turn/start` that queued it, so a
client can restore the submission's text exactly as for
`turn/retracted`. No `turn/started`/`turn/completed` is ever emitted for
this `turnId` (SDK turn-waits settle on this event too, tdd SS3.1.4).
`sourceRange` cites the SESSION stream's reclaim record — a reclaimed
turn never had a run stream.

commandId.description: The `commandId` of the `turn/start` that queued the reclaimed turn.

sourceRange.description:
The durable records this event folded from (the session stream's
reclaim record).

turnId.description: The reclaimed turn: pre-minted at admission, never launched.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnUserShell.description:
The queued `!` shell action a `turn/start` carries (tdd SS3.2,
ADR 50034): the `!cmd` typed while a turn runs. The shell's command id
derives from the carrying turn's `commandId`, exactly as the app's own
queued submit does; the params' sibling `displayText` carries the `!…`
presentation form.

commandText.description: The shell command text, without the leading `!`.

UnavailableInputAsset.description:
One retained input image a `report` load replaced with a marker. It
names no run (ADR 78319 D1 owner amendment): each digest is listed once.

clientRef.description: The client's own name for the image, when its part carried one.

digest.description: The sha256 of the stored image bytes, lowercase hex.

UnavailableInputAssetReason.description:
Why the image was replaced. Open: a newer host's word decodes to
`Unknown` (tdd SS1.9).

UnframedViewNotification.description:
One element of a `view/page` result's `events` array: an **unframed view
notification** — the nested pair `{"method", "params"}`, which is the live
notification minus `jsonrpc` and `emittedAtMs`, with nothing lifted out of
`params` and nothing spliced into it. `view/page` and `muse exec --json`
share this one definition, so the two surfaces cannot drift.

method.description:
The event type — the live notification's method name, retained because
the type lives only in the notification name and would otherwise be
lost (tdd SS4.2.1).

UnframedViewNotificationParams.description:
The `params` of an unframed view notification (tdd SS4.2.1, SS4.2).

Declares the base members every view notification carries, and stays
**open** for the event-specific fields each event type adds. The v1 schema
model names no method-correlated union (the `events` element's `params` arm
is selected by its sibling `method`), so the per-event arms cannot be
expressed here without one, and an uncorrelated union of them could reject a
real page element, which a published schema must not do.

`sourceRange` is required here and not optional: `view/page` serves
durable-sourced events only (tdd SS4.7.3), and durable-sourced is *defined*
as carrying a `sourceRange` — the SS4.2 ephemeral-sourced exemption applies
to `item/delta`, which `view/page` never replays.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from (tdd SS4.2, SS6.8).

viewCursor.description:
The event's opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor. It stays **inside**
`params`, where every live notification already carries it (tdd
SS4.2.1) — nothing is spliced beside `method`.

UnknownModelReasoningEffortVariants.description:
The only scalar alternative to a known effort array. Kept as a closed
singleton so arbitrary strings and uppercase spellings fail decoding.

UsageReadResult.description:
`usage/read` result: `{usage?}` — omitted, never `null`, when the host
has observed nothing (ADR 32563 D2: truthful absence, no
"nothing observed" error).

usage.description: The last-observed subscription usage window, when one exists.

UsageRefreshResult.description:
`usage/refresh` result (experimental, ADR 32563 D6): the same `usage`
member as `usage/read` after ONE fresh read, plus the mint's tier display
name. A sibling method, not a `usage/read` param: a stable method cannot
reference an experimental params type, so a param would change the
stable surface.

subscriptionActive.description:
Whether the refresh mint stamped an active subscription. With `usage`
omitted, `false` is a login with no subscription (pay-as-you-go or
none) and `true` is a subscriber whose mint carried no usage object,
which a client reports as "no usage data", never as no allowance
(ADR 32563 D6 item 6).

usage.description: The observation after the refresh, when one exists.

UserInputAnswer.description:
One question's answer, as sent in `userInput/answer` or
`userInput/interrupt` and as recorded in `userInput/settled`.

freeText.description: A free-form answer, at most 500 characters.

note.description: An optional comment the user adds to the answer, at most 500 characters.

questionId.description: The `id` of the question this answers.

selectedLabel.description: The label of the chosen option, for a `single` question.

selectedLabels.description:
The labels of the chosen options for a `multiple` question, within its
selection bounds; omitted when empty.

UserInputAnswerParams.description:
`userInput/answer` params (tdd SS5.10.2): answer every question.

Each answer carries `questionId` then exactly one of `selectedLabel`
(single mode), `selectedLabels` (multiple mode, within min/max bounds), or
`freeText` (<=500 chars); plus an optional `note` (<=500). Answers that do
not match the prompt fail -32057 `userInputAnswerInvalid`. Image
`attachments` are a **reserved** field in v1, rejected if sent, because
the blob-upload path they reference is also reserved.

UserInputCancelParams.description:
`userInput/cancel` params (tdd SS5.10.2): decline to answer; the tool call
resolves with a cancelled result the model sees.

reason.description: Why the prompt was declined.

UserInputClarification.description:
A free-form reply the user gives instead of choosing from the options; the
model reads it and decides again.

content.description: The clarification text, at most 500 characters.

format.description:
