Vcs.description: Version-control system of a branch observation (tdd SS4.6.4). Open.

ViewGapParams.description:
`view/gap` params (spec 208 SS4.8, FM-001): push delivery dropped events,
and this names the hole.

The bracket is deferred (D-16487-2): it flushes at the subscription's next
ACCEPTED delivery, never at enqueue time, so `next` always names an event
whose own delivery is proven. A run of consecutive undelivered events
coalesces into one bracket keeping the FIRST range's `after` (D-16487-1).
The gap rides the protected reserved queue, so no wire-interleaving order
against neighbouring deliveries is promised — the cursors carry the
semantics (INV-002, D-16487-3).

On receipt a client may take either sanctioned recovery (D-030, FR-013):
splice-fill — buffer live events at cursors >= `next`, page `(after,
next)` forward, discard the overlap, splice — or re-anchor through the
anchored read surface. The server requires neither, cannot distinguish
clients by their choice, and holds no partial-fill state.

after.description:
The last cursor delivered before the hole — the exclusive lower bound
of the undelivered range. An **opaque** view cursor: clients relay it,
never parse it (tdd SS4.1).

next.description:
The first cursor delivered after the hole — the exclusive upper bound
of the undelivered range, and the position delivery continues from. An
**opaque** view cursor: clients relay it, never parse it (tdd SS4.1).

sessionId.description: The session whose subscription dropped events.

ViewPageAnchor.description:
The `view/page` request-mode anchor. Declared **open**: the protocol spells
it "open string enum, v1 value `latestCompaction`".

ViewPageDirection.description:
The `view/page` paging direction. Closed: the protocol spells exactly two
values and a third would change the paging contract.

ViewPageParams.description: `view/page` params (tdd SS4.7.3): cursor-paged reads of the session view.

anchor.description:
The cold-client request mode (D-029; spec 208 FR-008), resolved at
call time to the latest installed compaction boundary. The one named
exception to the SS4.1 observed-only rule.

cursor.description:
The exclusive anchor. Forward: the page starts strictly after it;
omitted means from the beginning of the view. Backward: the page ends
strictly before it; omitted means from the head. Mutually exclusive
with `anchor` (tdd SS4.7.3; spec 208 FR-008a).

limit.description:
Maximum events to return, 1–1000. The server MAY return fewer.

The 1–1000 range is ratified and **published**: the model carries the
bound and the bundle renders `minimum`/`maximum` instead of a bare
`integer`.

maxBytes.description:
The caller's page byte cap (kt-dvw5, additive-optional). The page
serves under `min(server budget, maxBytes)`, so a Console page stays
under its own budget without the server's frame cap alone deciding.
Absent means the server budget governs. `0` is refused typed
(`invalid_params`): a 0 cap admits no progress. A single event over
the cap is truncated (marked) instead of erroring, except verbatim
and fetch-key content (`item.args`, `structuredData`, `outputRef`/
`patchRef`), which is never cut and still answers typed
`PageEventTooLarge`.

ViewPageResolvedAnchor.description:
The `resolvedAnchor` echo (tdd SS4.7.3): subsequent pages pass ordinary
cursors, so the anchor never needs re-resolving.

boundaryCursor.description: The view cursor of the resolved boundary's `compaction` event.

events.description:
The page's events, always ascending by `viewCursor` in both
directions. Durable-sourced only; pages are contiguous and can never
skip a cursor.

nextCursor.description:
The anchor for the next page in the same direction: forward, the last
event's cursor; backward, the first's. `null` at the end of the view
in that direction — never omitted.

resolvedAnchor.description:
The resolution echo, present exactly when the request used `anchor`
(tdd SS4.7.3; spec 208 FR-008).

schemaVersion.description:
Snapshot schema version. A client whose generated types are older than
this must fall back to inline/paged history (tdd SS4.9.2, SS2.5.2).

state.description: The complete folded view at `viewCursor` (tdd SS4.9.1).

viewCursor.description:
The cursor the state is folded at; every event after it streams as the
suffix (tdd SS4.9).

ViewSubscribeParams.description:
`view/subscribe` params (tdd SS4.7.1): attach this connection's live view
subscription for a session at an explicit cursor — the fine-grained
counterpart of the SS2 auto-subscribe, and the gap-free re-attachment
path after `view/unsubscribe`. It never loads a session, takes no lease,
writes nothing.

after.description:
Resume cursor. When present, the server replays `(after, head]` as
ordinary view notifications before any live event — one gapless
cursor sequence. Omitted means "from now": no historical replay
(tdd SS4.7.1).

viewCursor.description:
The view head at subscribe time; the client knows it is live once
cursors pass it.

ViewUnsubscribeParams.description:
`view/unsubscribe` params (tdd SS4.7.2): remove this connection from the
session's view subscription set — the protocol's single unsubscribe
operation, at the altitude that owns subscriptions (tdd SS2.5.6 points
here). It does not unload the session; unloading is the idle policy
(tdd SS2.8).

ViewUnsubscribeResult.description:
`view/unsubscribe` result (tdd SS4.7.2): the empty object. Idempotent —
unsubscribing while not subscribed returns `{}`.

WebSearchHit.description:
`webSearch`: one typed result hit — result schema v1 (tdd SS4.5.15,
spec 13929 amendment #45444 FR-45444-3, **experimental**).

title.description: The hit title, verbatim (empty when the provider omits it).

url.description: The hit URL, verbatim (empty when the provider omits it).

WorkflowCancelParams.description: `workflow/cancel` params (tdd SS3.19): cancel a live workflow run.

workflowRunId.description:
The run to cancel, exactly as the `workflow` item names it (SS4.5.8);
required, non-empty.

WorkflowChild.description:
One workflow child's folded state (tdd SS4.5.8,
`WorkflowChildLifecycleFact`), keyed by `(childId, attempt)`.

childId.description: The child's id within the run.

durationMs.description: The child's observed duration, when recorded.

failureKind.description:
The attempt's machine failure class, verbatim when recorded (open,
snake_case durable runtime vocabulary — the SS1.6 casing exemption).
The attempt's outcome (`terminal`, else `status`) stays authoritative,
except that `"completed"` with `failureKind` present means it failed
(#17769).

failureReason.description:
The attempt's failure reason text, verbatim when recorded except cut
to at most 2,048 UTF-8 bytes ending in U+2026 when longer.

label.description: The child's display label, when recorded.

resultRef.description:
The child's recorded result reference, verbatim, when present — an
opaque string, matching the durable owner.

terminal.description: The child's terminal, turn vocabulary (tdd SS4.5.8).

usage.description: The child's observed usage, when recorded.

WorkflowChildAction.description:
Which control to apply to the child's current attempt (tdd SS3.20).
Closed on the wire: an unknown value is `-32602 invalidParams`.

WorkflowChildControlParams.description:
`workflow/childControl` params (tdd SS3.20): skip or retry one workflow
child, keyed by the `(childId, attempt)` pair the `workflow` item's
`children[]` carries.

attempt.description:
The child's CURRENT attempt (integer >= 1). A stale value rejects
`"stale_attempt"`; re-read the item and re-key — never guess.

childId.description: The child, from the item's `children[]`; required, non-empty.

workflowRunId.description: The run owning the child (SS4.5.8); required, non-empty.

WorkflowControlResult.description:
The shared SS3.19/SS3.20/SS3.32 admission-only ack: deliberately bare
`{commandId, status}` — settlement arrives as the workflow item's view
events, never through the ack.

WorkflowPauseParams.description:
`workflow/pause` params (tdd SS3.32, ADR 45437 D2): pause a live
workflow run, shaped exactly like `workflow/cancel`.

workflowRunId.description:
The run to pause, exactly as the `workflow` item names it (SS4.5.8);
required, non-empty.

WorkflowResumeParams.description:
`workflow/resume` params (tdd SS3.34, ADR 45437 D3): resume a paused
workflow run, host-driven.

workflowRunId.description:
The paused run to resume, exactly as the `workflow` item names it
(SS4.5.8); required, non-empty.

WorkflowResumeResult.description:
`workflow/resume` result (tdd SS3.34): admission-only plus the driven
turn — always present, since resume always drives (idle fresh turn or
busy steer).

turnId.description:
The turn the host drove: the fresh resume turn on an idle session,
the admission-time active turn on a busy session (a routing fact
like the SS3.18 wake-gate's, not settlement).

WorkflowTokenBudget.description: `workflow`: the run's launch token budget (tdd SS4.5.8, #45449).

total.description: The effective launch budget in tokens, verbatim from the launch fact.

WorktreeListEntry.description:
One listed worktree (FR-31776-3/FR-31776-6): where the checkout is,
which branch it holds, whether it is the main checkout, and which
live sessions use it — the visibility two-sessions-in-one-folder
warns through (D6).

branch.description:
Short branch name; omitted when detached, bare, or Sapling
(Sapling checkouts carry no branch on this surface, exactly as
`Session.branch` omits them).

isMain.description: Whether this is the repository's main checkout.

sessionIds.description:
Ids of the sessions loaded on the answering host whose worktree
(effective root) is this path.

WorktreeListParams.description:
`worktree/list` params (FR-31776-3): any in-repo path — the main
checkout, a linked checkout, or a subdirectory spelling — which the
host canonicalizes and resolves to its repository before listing.

workspaceRoot.description: The path to resolve to a repository and list.

WorktreeListResult.description:
`worktree/list` result (FR-31776-3): every worktree of the resolved
repository, main first, in tool order.

WorktreeOrigin.description:
Where a session's worktree came from: `created` means the host
allocated it for the session, `attached` means the host bound a
caller-provided worktree.

WorktreeStartRequest.description:
`session/start` `worktree` param (FR-31776-1/FR-31776-2, D9): absent
means no worktree — the start proceeds exactly as today (INV-31776-4).
Adjacently tagged on `mode`: a create carries an optional `baseRef`,
an existing carries a required `path` (omitted `path` fails decode —
the pre-existing invalid-params class, never a new message).

baseRef.description: The base to create from; omitted means `HEAD`.

path.description: The caller-provided worktree path to validate.

description: Muse Session Protocol (MSP) v1 wire schema bundle, rendered from the tbh-protocol schema model (spec 206). Generated; do not edit.

account/loginCancel.description: Cancels the pending login flow, abandoning the device code to server-side expiry; cancelled is false when nothing was pending (spec 28091 FR-29535-5).

account/loginStart.description: Starts a host-owned login flow: the RFC 8628 device-code flow (result carries the verification URL and user code for native rendering) or the apiKey type (stores the carried key; completes synchronously). Supersedes a pending flow (spec 28091 FR-29535-1/INV-29535-2).

account/logout.description: Clears the stored credential (with the best-effort pre-clear session revoke) and answers the fresh projected state (spec 28091 FR-29535-6).

account/read.description: Reads the host's projected credential state: which credential lane is in effect, an optional display label, and whether the deployment needs a credential at all (spec 28091 FR-001).

admission/decide.description: Decides an open peer-admission request; every decide is terminal for its request, first durable wins (amendment 45445 FR-45445-7).

admission/listPending.description: Lists the session's open peer-admission requests with full request payloads (amendment 45445 FR-45445-8).

approval/decide.description: Decides a pending approval, guarded by the current requirement id against the multi-stage race (SS5.4).

approval/listPending.description: Reads the full pending approval and user-input payloads for a session; a lease-free fold read (SS5.7).

computerUseSettings/read.description: Reads the computer-use Settings: each capability's Always allow switch and the user's blocked apps from the approval policy store, plus the built-in blocks as locked rows when asked; computerUseUnavailable while the CUA gate is off (ADR 630 D18.17).

computerUseSettings/update.description: Applies one Settings patch (capability dropdowns, blocked apps to add or remove) all-or-nothing and answers the user's Settings after it; a built-in block is refused in either list; computerUseUnavailable while the CUA gate is off (ADR 630 D18.17).

computerUseSetup/check.description: Reads the host's three macOS grants with no prompt: starts the computer-use helper only long enough to check them, reports each as granted or missing, and ends it; never requests a grant or opens System Settings. Needs computerUseHostSetup; commandRejected runtime_busy while a setup attempt holds the host.

computerUseSetup/read.description: Reads one session's computer-use setup state and permissions by running cua_setup status for it as a host command: no model turn, no prompt, no spawn; computerUseUnavailable while the CUA gate is off (#52381). Without sessionId it reads the host's own setup, with computerUseHostSetup.

computerUseSetup/start.description: A human command: runs cua_setup start for one session, between turns, exactly as the TUI's /cua on does, and answers the state it settles in, with the refusal code when setup refused; computerUseUnavailable while the CUA gate is off (#52381). Without sessionId it starts the host's own setup under one host owner, with computerUseHostSetup.

feedback/submit.description: Submits a first-party feedback report through the host, reusing the TUI submitter seam (consent, bundle-first persistence, redaction), and answers the upload receipt (ADR 42691 D2).

goal/clear.description: Clears the session goal; never wakes and its ack never names a turn (tdd SS3.18, spec 14408; enrolled by #33066).

goal/edit.description: Replaces the current goal's objective under the same wake gate as goal/set (tdd SS3.18, spec 14408; enrolled by #33066).

goal/pause.description: Pauses the session goal; never wakes and its ack never names a turn (tdd SS3.18, spec 14408; enrolled by #33066).

goal/resume.description: Resumes a paused goal under the same wake gate as goal/set (tdd SS3.18, spec 14408; enrolled by #33066).

goal/set.description: Sets the session goal objective; wakes a goal-driving turn iff idle and the resulting goal is unfinished (tdd SS3.18, spec 14408; enrolled by #33066).

hook/declare.description: Declares the plugin hooks of the plugins the client hosts; the call replaces the connection's whole hook set, `{ "hooks": [] }` removes it, and the host forgets the set when the connection closes. No `commandId`, no durable record (SS3.41.1).

hook/list.description: Reads the session's installed hook rows — one per installed handler per event, config-file handlers plus plugin-contributed hooks; a query, not a command (SS3.26.1).

host/readLimits.description: Reads the host's posture ceiling as a limits object — experimental, same-user socket only (SS1.10).

host/shutdown.description: Stops the host: long-running, drains every loaded session and exits when drained. `park: true` drains parked (pending prompts stay pending for the next resume), except on an ephemeral host, which has no resume and aborts; otherwise drains with today's abort semantics (ADR 73975 D2). The reply means only "shutdown accepted" (the wire layer writes it before the drain); the caller waits for serve exit (EOF) for drain completion before powering down. Served only when `GateId::PendingParkOnShutdown` is OPEN; otherwise the verb is absent.

initialize.description: Opens the connection: client identification, capability requests, and the experimental opt-in; the reply carries the envelope schema version and the stable-surface fingerprint (SS1.4.1).

item/readOutput.description: Byte-ranged read of stored full output the view truncated; works on loaded and unloaded sessions and takes no lease (SS4.7.4).

journal/admissionContext.description: Receiver-owned admission inputs (conditions, negotiated limits, initial anchor) for one journal source.

journal/commitBatch.description: Atomically commits one frozen batch to the client store, idempotent by source plus meaning.

journal/observeOriginal.description: Resolves an original transition key to its recorded disposition or unknown.

journal/readPage.description: Bounded anchored page of the qualified journal prefix.

log/page.description: Reads a contiguous, gap-free page of a stream's stored rows after a position, each as written to disk: envelopes and stored omitted_live_only markers (SS6.4).

log/physicalFiles.description: Lists every log file in a session home with its size (ADR 58371 D4).

log/physicalSubscribe.description: Follows one retained log file byte-exactly from a line-boundary cursor (ADR 58371 D4-D6).

log/physicalUnsubscribe.description: Ends a physical subscription; idempotent (ADR 58371 D4).

log/streams.description: Enumerates a session's raw streams with tails and earliest-available positions (SS6.3).

log/subscribe.description: Attaches a live tail to one stream, optionally resuming after a cursor position (SS6.5).

mcpServer/list.description: Projects the effective MCP server set: without sessionId the host-global rows (settings + plugin), with sessionId that loaded session's effective set (host rows plus its frozen ADR-32760 additions); every row carries its D5 ladder state (spec 28364 FR-005).

mcpServer/oauthLogin.description: Starts a host-owned MCP OAuth login flow for one server: the result carries the provider authorization URL the client opens in a browser; completion arrives as mcpServer/oauthLoginCompleted. Supersedes a pending flow (spec 28364 FR-001).

mcpServer/oauthLoginCancel.description: Cancels the pending login flow for one server binding; cancelled is false when nothing for that binding was pending (spec 28364 FR-002).

mcpServer/oauthLogout.description: Deletes one server's stored MCP OAuth credential (best-effort upstream revocation, authoritative local delete) and answers what was removed (spec 28364 FR-003).

mcpServer/readDisplayCatalog.description: Reads the addressed loaded session's retained MCP display catalog, preserving pinned identities without MCP discovery (ADR 79187 D3).

mcpServer/readInventory.description: Reads the addressed loaded session's MCP runtime snapshot; includeTools selects raw tool names. Performs no MCP discovery (ADR 79187 D2).

mcpServer/reconnect.description: Reconnects one forfeited stdio MCP server in one loaded session, on the holder's explicit instruction (ADR 74052 D3): serve reconnects only when told. Idempotent: an already-live server answers reconnected false without restarting. The timed-out call is never replayed (ADR D5); the reconnect never refills the retry allowance (#59887).

media/upload.description: Moves one video chunk into the session's video store; answers the `uploadId` receipt on every chunk (tdd SS3.33, ADR 45443 D5).

model/cancel.description: Cancels the sending connection's `model/complete` call, which settles `cancelled`; any other id answers `{}` and changes nothing (ADR 90352 D4/D6, tdd SS3.40).

model/complete.description: Runs one model completion with no session on the host's model; acks `accepted` and settles exactly once on `model/completed` — 4 in flight per connection, host-enforced 45s timeout (ADR 90352 D1-D4, tdd SS3.40).

model/list.description: Reads the catalog of models the host will accept in `session/setModel`; a query, not a command (SS3.10).

peer/list.description: Lists the viewing session's live local peers from the registry snapshot, minus the viewer, ordered by session id — one row per live entry with its authority-joined name, label, status, age, and eligibility (amendment 45445 FR-45445-1).

peer/settlements.description: Reads one page of the receiving session's peer-admission settlements after a cursor, ascending, in the shape the receiver timeline folds (amendment 45445 FR-45445-16).

permissionProfile/list.description: Reads the selectable permission profiles for a session; a lease-free read (SS3).

plugin/install.description: Install one plugin from a marketplace pair or a host local path with scope (per-session, `commandId`-idempotent, hold-open; answers the installed receipt) (SS3.29.1).

plugin/list.description: Reads the installed plugin records — one row per installed plugin; a query, not a command (SS3.26.2).

plugin/marketplaceAdd.description: Add a marketplace from `owner/repo`, git URL, `file://` URL, or local path (per-session, `commandId`-idempotent; answers the stored record) (SS3.29.2).

plugin/marketplaceRemove.description: Remove a marketplace (per-session, `commandId`-idempotent; answers the removed name) (SS3.29.4).

plugin/marketplaceUpdate.description: Refresh a marketplace in place (per-session, `commandId`-idempotent; answers the stored record) (SS3.29.3).

projection/list.description: Lists the registered server-side read projections (SS6.6).

projection/read.description: Reads one named projection's snapshot with its fold basis (SS6.6).

recap/cancel.description: Cancels the session's in-flight recap, which settles `cancelled`; idle is an accepted no-op (ADR 45447 D5, tdd SS3.28.5).

recap/request.description: Requests a "while you were away" recap for a loaded session; acks `accepted` and settles exactly once on `recap/completed` — one in flight per session, host-enforced 45s timeout (ADR 45447 D1/D5, tdd SS3.28.1).

schedule/list.description: Reads the session's live schedule rows — one per active or firing job in server store order; a query, not a command (SS3.38).

serve/isIdle.description: Answers whether serve can shut down for now: true iff no session has running work. Sessions that only wait for input count idle; monitors, running subagents and other live processes count as running, not idle. Armed-but-not-firing cron/reminders are waiting, not running; a firing tick is running. Also carries nextWakeAt, the earliest armed fire time in epoch milliseconds (a runtime scheduled delivery or an active cron/reminder job), or null when nothing is armed. A lease-free read; no params. Experimental.

session/clearExternalWait.description: Clears a live host-declared external wait: no declaration is live afterwards, and the end-of-turn reminder boundary returns to today's behaviour at once. Clearing a session with no declaration is a no-op that still answers `declared: false`.

session/compact.description: Compacts the session's conversation context; runs asynchronously, so the ack is admission only (SS3.7).

session/declareExternalWait.description: Declares that a loaded session is waiting on an external event: the end-of-turn reminder boundary parks a blocking reminder instead of re-verifying until the next input arrives (ADR 66573 amendment). Live-only: a serve restart, unload, or resume loses the declaration; the next user input or an explicit clear ends it.

session/fork.description: Branches a session into a new id whose log copies the source through a cut point, with durable provenance (SS2.5.3).

session/leave.description: Admits release of one loaded session; final release or failure is pushed through session/leaveCompleted (SS2.15).

session/list.description: Pages through stored sessions under the sessions root for history and picker UIs; read-only, never touches leases (SS2.5.4).

session/promptHint.description: Picks one feature-tip table id over the client-supplied candidates; display-only, nothing is logged (ADR 50063 D1).

session/read.description: Reads one stored session without attaching: no lease, no load, no subscription, no resume record (SS2.5.5).

session/readLimits.description: Reads one session's effective limits — experimental, same-user socket only (SS1.10).

session/releaseDrive.description: The holder gives a loaded session's drive back without ending the load: `released` (nobody drives until a request or resume takes it; `session/driveChanged` tells every connection), `busy` while a turn runs, or the session is idle with a launch still queued or its launch count unreadable (no `turn/completed` is promised on that arm) (SS2.16).

session/rename.description: Sets or changes the durable allocated session name through the runtime session_name command; withheld under the ephemeral profile (SS2.14.2, #27598).

session/reportStartupPhases.description: Reports the client's measured startup spans once per launch; the host appends the durable phases record as single writer (ADR 50064 pick-1 D1).

session/requestDrive.description: Asks for a loaded session's drive: `granted` at once and stopping nothing — when no turn runs, and to another connection while a turn runs or input waits, which run on under the caller (the drive moves and `session/driveChanged` tells every connection); `busy` while the caller's own turn runs or its input waits, while a live holder is idle and its queue cannot be read (no `turn/completed` is promised then), or for a live holder not opted into `experimentalApi` while it is not quiet (a result; nothing parked; ask again later, after `turn/completed` when a turn runs) (SS2.16).

session/resume.description: Loads a stored session on this host, auto-subscribes this connection, and returns the history needed to render it (SS2.5.2).

session/rewindRead.description: Reads rewind availability/source state, with an optional work census and passive attempt observation: no lease, no load, no resume, no selection change (ADR 50280 D7).

session/setApprovalMode.description: Selects a preconfigured approval enforcement mode mid-session; select, never create (SS5.12).

session/setModel.description: Reconfigures the session's model; the selection is durable and applies to subsequent model calls (SS3.8).

session/setPermissionProfile.description: Selects a preconfigured permission profile mid-session; select, never create (SS3).

session/setReasoningEffort.description: Sets the session's standing reasoning-effort default; a turn carrying its own tier overrides it for that turn only (SS3.21, ADR 31255 D1).

session/sideChat.description: Opens a side chat from a loaded main session, with durable provenance (SS2.5.7; ADR 45435 D2).

session/start.description: Creates a brand-new session, loads it on this host, durably records the start, and auto-subscribes this connection (SS2.5.1).

session/userShell.description: Runs a user-initiated shell command in the session's workspace; capability-gated on `userShell` (SS3.9).

settings/read.description: Reads the host's composed effective values for exactly the host-owned keys, re-read under the advisory lock on every call; a corrupt file fails the single call, never the host (spec 13929 amendment 43458 FR-43458-1).

settings/readSchema.description: Reads each host-owned key's allowed shape plus its enforced managed constraint where one applies; absent constraint means unmanaged (spec 13929 amendment 43458 FR-43458-4).

settings/writeMany.description: Writes several host-owned key paths atomically — one invalid edit fails the whole call and writes nothing; answers the per-edit folded values in edit order (spec 13929 amendment 43458 FR-43458-3).

settings/writeValue.description: Writes one host-owned key path's absolute value (null clears the member to absent); answers the folded effective value (spec 13929 amendment 43458 FR-43458-2).

skill/import.description: Imports foreign skills from the host's own `claude | codex` dirs through the single `SkillsService::import_skills` seam; answers per-skill installed/quarantined/skipped/failed plus counts. `commandId`-idempotent (including `dryRun` previews); each successful write is a `skill/changed` detection point (tdd SS3.30.2, ADR 45433 D2/D4/D5, #45433).

skill/list.description: Reads the session's user-invocable skill rows — one per typed-invocable shortcut spelling, the INV-007 predicate and shared name resolution by call-through; a query, not a command (SS3.22.1).

skill/setActivation.description: Writes one skill's activation in any scope through the single `SkillsService::set_activation` seam; answers the applied state plus `previous`. `commandId`-idempotent; each successful write is a `skill/changed` detection point (tdd SS3.30.1, ADR 45433 D2/D4/D5, #45433).

subagent/close.description: Owner-close a child; the terminal mapping folds per SS4.5.7 (SS3.16).

subagent/followupTask.description: Queue a follow-up task for a child; admission-only ack, the task settles on the child session's view stream (SS3.16).

subagent/interrupt.description: Ask a child to yield at its next boundary; outcome folds to the parent's subagent item (SS3.16, SS4.5.7).

subagent/list.description: Lists the session's subagent roster: one row per durable child, running and finished, projected from the loaded parent's runtime subagent control records (kt-o155).

subagent/readResult.description: Consume a ready child result (state-changing; the content is already the subagent item's result field) (SS3.16).

subagent/reopen.description: Reopen a stopped/closed child as a durable later attempt (SS3.16).

subagent/resume.description: Resume a paused/recoverable child as a durable later attempt (SS3.16).

subagent/sendMessage.description: Queue a user note into a running child; admission-only ack, the note settles on the child session's view stream (SS3.16).

subagent/stop.description: Stop a running child; outcome folds to the parent's subagent item (SS3.16, SS4.5.7).

task/background.description: Durably sends a running foreground tool task to the background; the `TaskBackgrounded` record lands before the ack and the `toolCall` item's `item/updated` folds the flip (tdd §3.13, #14411; enrolled under the #33065 T1 ruling).

task/list.description: Lists the loaded session's background-task inventory: one row per stoppable workload at admission, ordered oldest-start first (tdd §3.31, #45144; enrolled under the #33065 T1 ruling).

task/readTail.description: Reads the latest output of one running background command, at most 128 KiB from the host runtime's retained tail, so a follow view keeps showing output past the 64 KiB streamed budget (ADR 70076 D1).

task/stop.description: Stops one named background task; the kill settles durably and the item folds a terminal (tdd §3.14, #14411; enrolled under the #33065 T1 ruling).

task/stopAll.description: Stops every stoppable background workload live at admission; always accepted, one item terminal folds per stopped item-visible task (tdd §3.15, #14411; enrolled under the #33065 T1 ruling).

turn/cancel.description: Cancels a turn on the normal command lane, recording no priority interrupt intent (SS3.5).

turn/interrupt.description: Stops the running turn on the runtime's priority lane, optionally pairing a durable retract intent (SS3.4).

turn/start.description: Submits user input to a session; the optional disposition controls queue, steer, or replace when a turn is already running (SS3.2).

turn/steer.description: Injects input into the turn the caller names, failing if that turn is no longer active (SS3.3).

turn/unqueue.description: Reclaims a queued submit before it launches; never upgrades into a cancel once the target is running (SS3.6).

usage/read.description: Reads the host's last-observed subscription usage window (5h-class and weekly percent blocks, tier, arrival stamp) without a model call; the usage member is omitted when nothing has been observed (ADR 32563 D2).

usage/refresh.description: Issues ONE rate-bounded fresh subscription-usage read (a key mint, at most one per host per 60 s), records it in the usage cache when one is composed, and answers the usage/read shape plus the mint's tierName (ADR 32563 D6).

userInput/answer.description: Answers every question of an open user-input prompt (SS5.10.2).

userInput/cancel.description: Declines an open user-input prompt; the tool call resolves with a cancelled result the model sees (SS5.10.2).

userInput/clarify.description: Answers an open user-input prompt with a free-form clarification the model re-decides against (SS5.10.2).

userInput/interrupt.description: Interrupts an open user-input prompt carrying confirmed partial answers, then stops the turn (SS5.10.2, ADR 45450 D1).

view/page.description: Cursor-paged reads of the session view, forward or backward; each result element is an unframed view notification, the nested {method, params} pair of SS4.2.1 (SS4.7.3).

view/subscribe.description: Attaches this connection's live view subscription for a session at an explicit cursor, replaying `(after, head]` before any live event; the re-attach path after `view/unsubscribe` (SS4.7.1).

view/unsubscribe.description: Removes this connection from the session's view subscription set; does not unload the session (SS4.7.2).

workflow/cancel.description: Cancels a live workflow run; admission-only bare ack, the cancellation's truth arrives as the workflow item's view events (tdd SS3.19, spec 14410; enrolled by the #33065 sweep).

workflow/childControl.description: Skips or retries one workflow child keyed by the item's (childId, attempt) pair; admission-only bare ack (tdd SS3.20, spec 14410; enrolled by the #33065 sweep).

workflow/pause.description: Pauses a live workflow run; admission-only bare ack, the pause folds as the workflow item's `paused` member (tdd SS3.32, ADR 45437 D2).

workflow/resume.description: Resumes a paused workflow run, host-driven; the reply names the driven turn, the resumed launch folds as a new workflow item whose `resumeFromRunId` names the paused run (tdd SS3.34, ADR 45437 D3).

worktree/list.description: Lists the worktrees of the repository at `workspaceRoot`: each checkout's path, branch (omitted when detached, bare, or Sapling), main-checkout flag, and live session ids, so apps can warn on sharing (#31776 FR-31776-3/FR-31776-6).

account/changed.description: The host's projected credential state changed — including out-of-band changes such as a terminal `muse logout` — with the same payload shape as account/read (spec 28091 FR-002).

account/loginCompleted.description: A login flow reached a terminal outcome (granted, denied, expired, cancelled, or failed); a granted flow's account/changed follows (spec 28091 FR-29535-4; ADR 28091 D3). Never carries the device-code artifacts or any key material.

admission/requested.description: View event: a peer-admission prompt opened (fold of the owner's `Requested` record, FR-45445-6).

admission/resolved.description: A peer admission settled (protected view event, FR-45445-8).

approval/requested.description: An approval opened: the fold of its durable Requested record (SS5.5.1).

approval/resolved.description: The first durable approval terminal landed; protected delivery (SS5.5).

approval/reviewing.description: The native reviewer holds an approval: the fold of a Requested whose phase is automated_reviewing; typed activity, not a request (SS5.5.1, spec 209 FR-52080-1).

approval/updated.description: A non-terminal approval record changed the pending view (SS5.5.1).

backgroundTerminal/inboxItemDrained.description: One background-terminal inbox drain with its recorded stamp; the admission rides the `backgroundTerminalCompletion` item (#83474).

computerUseSetup/changed.description: A computerUseSetup/read or /start observed a session's setup state differ from the last one sent for it, including inProgress when a start begins and the state it settles in (#52381). Without sessionId it carries the host's own setup state, delivered only with computerUseHostSetup.

cua/lockChanged.description: A session lost or acquired the per-Mac Computer Use lock: lost (takenOver, reaped, released or lapsed) to the old owner's session, acquired to the new owner's, each with the lock epoch. Only computerUseSetup holders that follow the session receive it (#73131).

initialized.description: Client-to-server notification closing the handshake; no params (SS1.4.2).

item/completed.description: An item reached its terminal state: the authoritative final object (SS4.3).

item/delta.description: Streaming append to an open item's field path (ephemeral-sourced, no sourceRange; opt-out-able) (SS4.3.1).

item/started.description: An item opened on the transcript (SS4.3).

item/updated.description: An open item changed non-terminally: full re-emission at a higher revision (SS4.4.2).

journal/confirmThrough.description: The client store reports its confirmedThrough (qualified) position; coalesced watermark hint, never evidence.

log/gap.description: Raw backlog collapsed for one subscription; fill (after, next) via log/page (SS6.5, protected).

log/physicalLine.description: One chunk of one complete physical line for a physical subscription (ADR 58371 D6).

log/physicalReset.description: Ends a physical subscription after a fault, naming the last fully delivered boundary (ADR 58371 D7).

log/record.description: One raw record for an active subscription, in sequence order (SS6.5).

mcpServer/forfeited.description: A stdio MCP server's connection was forfeited in one loaded session (deadline, framing desync, notification-write timeout, or cancel-write failure). Delivered to every experimental connection that has not opted the method out, initiator or not. The holder decides the strategy; the reconnect capability is the independent mcpServer/reconnect verb (ADR 74052 D2).

mcpServer/oauthLoginCompleted.description: An MCP OAuth login flow reached a terminal outcome (granted, denied, expired, cancelled, or failed). Delivered to every experimental connection that has not opted the method out, initiator or not; never carries the authorization URL or any key material (spec 28364 FR-004; ADR 28364 D4).

model/completed.description: A model/complete call settled exactly once: `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `timedOut`, to the requesting connection only (ADR 90352 D2, tdd SS3.40).

monitor/inboxItemAdmitted.description: One monitor inbox admission: the fold keys gate-off consumes (SS4.5.18).

monitor/inboxItemDrained.description: One monitor inbox drain with its recorded stamp, the drain-side operand of latest-wins (SS4.5.18).

monitor/inboxItemVoided.description: One wake-missed void with its recorded stamp; count-only, no transcript row (SS4.5.18).

peer/inboxItemDrained.description: One peer inbox drain with its recorded stamp; peer admissions ride `peer/settlements` (#72279).

peer/settlementsChanged.description: A peer-admission settlement committed in the receiving session; read `peer/settlements` from your cursor (FR-45445-17).

plugin/changed.description: An install landed; carries the installed-row summary and clients re-issue `plugin/list` (ADR 45434 D5).

plugin/marketplaceChanged.description: A marketplace was added, updated, or removed; carries the change summary (ADR 45434 D5).

recap/completed.description: A recap request settled exactly once — `completed` (with `text` plus optional `title`), `failed` (`providerFailed`), `cancelled`, or `timedOut` — delivered to the requesting connection outside the view stream (ADR 45447 D2, tdd SS3.28.2).

session/approvalModeChanged.description: The approval enforcement mode changed: the fold of the durable reconfigure audit fact (SS5.12).

session/branchChanged.description: A durable workspace-branch observation landed; null branch is a detached-HEAD fact (SS4.6.4).

session/closed.description: A loaded session was unloaded (idle | hostShutdown | leave) with the final view cursor; broadcast to every initialized connection (SS2.6.2).

session/contextUsage.description: A provider-reported context-occupancy fact folded to a changed (windowTokens, usedTokens, pressure) triple (SS4.6.6).

session/driveChanged.description: A session's drive holder changed; command-plane broadcast to every connection, not cursor-stamped, not subscription-gated, `youDrive` per recipient (SS2.16, ADR 58706-drive-handover D3).

session/eventLogDegraded.description: A loaded session's durable event log took a degraded write (today: the disk was full): pushed to the session's live connections when the degraded record commits and restated to a client whose session/resume serves item history; outside the view stream, no viewCursor (ADR 72648 D1).

session/goalChanged.description: The session's goal block changed value; replace wholesale, an explicit null clears (SS4.6.2).

session/leaveCompleted.description: Protected correlated terminal for an admitted session/leave (SS2.15).

session/listChanged.description: The changed session/list row, full-row replace; opt-in per connection via the sessionListStream capability, never subscription-gated (#33084, ADR 33084 D2/D3).

session/logFlushDegraded.description: A run's turn-end session-log flush on the host degraded or failed: pushed to the connections attached to the session's view when the run's terminal folded; outside the view stream, no viewCursor (ADR 78845 D1).

session/modelChanged.description: A durable model selection took effect (SS4.6.1).

session/modelRouteUnserved.description: An accepted login credential update installed a provider that cannot serve the session's standing model route; the standing selection is unchanged and a routable session/setModel repairs it (#25603, spec 5469 Amendment 16).

session/nameChanged.description: A durable session-name record landed (rename or first naming): the fold of the session_name record (SS4.6.7, #27598).

session/permissionProfileChanged.description: The active permission profile changed: the fold of the durable reconfigure audit fact (SS3).

session/reasoningEffortChanged.description: A durable session-default reasoning-effort change took effect (SS4.6.9, ADR 31255 D1).

session/rulesChanged.description: A rules refresh replaced the `rules_file` block's listed sources; clients replace their rules-status snapshot (live host-state projection, not a view event; SS3.37, ADR 70236 D1).

session/started.description: A session became newly loaded on this host via session/start or session/fork; broadcast to every initialized connection (SS2.6.1).

session/statusChanged.description: A loaded session's (status, attention) flipped; command-plane broadcast, cursor-stamped, not subscription-gated (SS4.6.10, ADR 31983 D2).

session/todoListChanged.description: The todo list was replaced wholesale; empty items is a cleared list (SS4.6.3).

session/tokenUsage.description: A model call completed with usage: raw counters plus counted-once derivations plus session cumulative (SS4.6.5).

session/viewHealthChanged.description: A loaded session's live view stream became unavailable, and why: a command-plane push delivered independent of the view subscription set when the materialized projection fails closed (ADR 32557; #32557).

skill/changed.description: The session's user-invocable skill set changed; clients re-issue skill/list. A live host-state projection, not a view event (SS3.22.2).

turn/completed.description: Turn terminal: completed | failed | cancelled, with usage and the settled error object (SS4.5.1).

turn/foregroundCompleted.description: The turn's foreground work is done while named background reminder checks hold the turn open; explicitly non-terminal (SS4.5.12).

turn/modelAttemptStarted.description: A turn's model attempt is starting: its model provider task recorded its opening status; observable mid-turn, non-terminal (SS4.5.1; ADR 68644-model-attempt-started D1).

turn/modelRetryScheduled.description: A provider backoff behind one model attempt is scheduled and waiting out its delay; observable mid-turn, non-terminal (SS4.5.1; ADR 50047-model-retry-scheduled-members D1).

turn/retracted.description: An accepted interrupt's paired retract durably settled, accepted or declined (SS4.5.1; ADR 50074 D1).

turn/retryScheduled.description: A failing model attempt's retry is scheduled and waiting out its backoff; observable mid-turn, non-terminal (SS4.5.1, D-026).

turn/toolBatchSubmitted.description: The model submitted a batch of two or more tool calls: every call's `callId`, `tool` and verbatim `args` in model order, before any of them starts (ephemeral-sourced, no sourceRange; FR-76702-1).

turn/unqueued.description: A queued submit's reclaim durably won: its pre-minted turn never runs, and no turn/started or turn/completed will follow for that turnId (SS3.6, SS4.5.1).

usage/changed.description: The host's last-observed subscription usage DATA changed (window, weekly, or tier — not a stamp-only refresh), with the same payload shape as usage/read's usage member; the absent-to-present first observation emits (ADR 32563 D3).

userInput/engaged.description: Client-to-server engagement note: the user started interacting with a timed prompt, so the host disarms its countdown; no result, no errors, no ledger row (SS5.10.4, ADR 45450 D2).

userInput/requested.description: A user-input prompt opened: the fold of its durable Requested record (SS5.10.1).

userInput/settled.description: The first durable user-input settlement landed; protected delivery (SS5.10.3).

view/gap.description: Push delivery dropped events: `(after, next)` brackets the undelivered range and delivery continues from `next` (SS4.8; spec 208 FM-001).

admission/request.description: Server-initiated must-answer request presenting a pending peer-admission prompt; the response is the SS5.3.3 presentation receipt — the decision travels as admission/decide (amendment 45445 FR-45445-6; #50032 slice 2b).

approval/request.description: Server-initiated must-answer request presenting a pending approval to every subscribed connection; the response is the SS5.3.3 presentation receipt — the decision travels as approval/decide (SS5.3; indexed by #23840).

hook/request.description: Server-initiated must-answer request to the session's drive-grant holder for one plugin hook that the connection declared; `timeoutMs` is the rest of the hook's deadline, and the result is the hook's answer (SS3.41.2).

userInput/request.description: Server-initiated must-answer request presenting a pending user-input prompt; the response is the SS5.3.3 presentation receipt — the answer travels as userInput/answer (SS5.10.1; indexed by #23840).
